研究结果表明，Stu2的活性表现出明显的酶样特征：其微管生长速率以双曲线形式依赖于微管蛋白浓度，且微管末端的Stu2量在不同微管蛋白浓度下保持不变。此外，TOG与微管蛋白结合的测量结果显示出高亲和力（10 nM）和缓慢的解离速率（0.03 s⁻¹）。这些数据表明，Stu2作为微管末端的微管蛋白转运天线，其高效能的运作主要受到微管蛋白与TOG结合速率的限制。

通过将聚合酶活性和结合测量统一在生化模型中，研究为基于TOG的聚合酶提供了定量生化机制的理解。这一发现不仅深化了我们对Stu2/XMAP215家族微管聚合酶的认识，也为未来相关研究提供了重要的理论基础。

items.title: Complementary vertebrate Wac models exhibit phenotypes relevant to DeSanto-Shinawi Syndrome
items.abstract: Monogenic syndromes are associated with neurodevelopmental changes that result in cognitive impairments and neurobehavioral phenotypes, including autism and seizures. Limited studies and resources are available to make meaningful headway into the underlying molecular mechanisms that result in these symptoms. One such example is DeSanto-Shinawi Syndrome (DESSH), a rare disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the WAC gene. Individuals with DESSH syndrome exhibit a recognizable craniofacial gestalt, developmental delay/intellectual disability, neurobehavioral symptoms that include autism, ADHD, behavioral difficulties, and seizures. However, no thorough studies from a vertebrate model exist to understand how these changes occur. To overcome this, we developed both murine and zebrafish Wac/wac deletion mutants and studied whether their phenotypes recapitulate those described in individuals with DESSH syndrome. We first show that the two Wac models exhibit craniofacial and behavioral changes, reminiscent of abnormalities found in DESSH syndrome. In addition, each model revealed impacts on GABAergic neurons and further studies showed that the mouse mutants are susceptible to seizures, changes in brain volumes that are different between sexes and relevant behaviors. Finally, we uncovered transcriptional impacts of Wac loss-of-function in mice that will pave the way for future molecular studies into DESSH. These studies present two new vertebrate models that begin to uncover biological underpinnings of DESSH syndrome and elucidate the biology of Wac .
items.title_zh: 互补脊椎动物Wac模型展现与DeSanto-Shinawi综合征相关的表型
items.summary_zh: 单基因综合征与神经发育变化相关，导致认知障碍和神经行为表型，包括自闭症和癫痫。DeSanto-Shinawi综合征（DESSH）是一种由WAC基因致病变异引起的罕见疾病，患者表现出可识别的颅面特征、发育迟缓/智力障碍及神经行为症状。为了解这些变化的机制，我们开发了小鼠和斑马鱼Wac/wac缺失突变体，并研究其表型是否与DESSH综合征患者相似。结果显示，两种Wac模型均表现出颅面和行为变化，类似于DESSH综合征的异常。此外，模型显示对GABA能神经元的影响，小鼠突变体易感癫痫，且脑体积在性别间存在差异。最后，我们发现Wac功能缺失对小鼠转录的影响，为未来的分子机制研究奠定基础。
items.l1_lead: 研究表明，Wac基因缺失的小鼠和斑马鱼模型展现出与DeSanto-Shinawi综合征相似的表型变化，为理解该综合征的机制提供了新线索。
items.l2_summary:
DeSanto-Shinawi综合征（DESSH）是一种由WAC基因（WAC gene）致病变异引起的罕见疾病，患者通常表现出特定的颅面特征、发育迟缓和智力障碍，以及一系列神经行为症状，如自闭症和癫痫等。为了深入了解这些表型变化的机制，研究团队开发了小鼠和斑马鱼的Wac/wac缺失突变体，以探讨其表型是否与DESSH综合征患者相似。研究结果表明，这两种Wac模型均表现出与DESSH综合征相关的颅面和行为变化，显示出明显的相似性。

具体而言，Wac缺失突变体在行为上表现出对GABA能神经元的影响，且小鼠突变体在癫痫易感性方面显示出显著的变化。此外，研究还发现小鼠的脑体积在性别间存在差异，这可能与DESSH综合征的神经发育特征相关。通过这些实验，研究团队揭示了Wac功能缺失对小鼠转录的影响，为未来进一步探讨DESSH综合征的分子机制奠定了基础。这些发现不仅为理解DESSH综合征的病理机制提供了重要线索，也为相关的治疗策略开发提供了潜在的研究方向。

items.title: Brain cognition gaps reveal associations with dopamine and factors related to brain health through artificial intelligence prediction of functional connectome
items.abstract: A key question in human neuroscience is to understand how individual differences in brain function relate to cognitive differences. However, the optimal condition of brain function to study between-person differences in cognition remains unclear. While many studies have developed objective biomarkers to accurately predict intelligence and general cognition, consensus on domain-specific markers has not yet emerged. Brain age has been proposed as a potential candidate, but recent research suggests that brain age offers minimal additional information on cognitive decline beyond what chronological age provides, prompting a shift toward approaches focused directly on cognitive prediction. Using a deep learning approach, we evaluated the predictive power of the functional connectome during various states (resting state, movie-watching, and n-back) on episodic memory and working memory performance. Our findings show that connectomes during tasks, especially during movie-watching, predict individual differences across cognitive domains, while resting state connectomes predict episodic memory meaningfully. Furthermore, individuals with a negative brain cognition gap (where brain predictions underestimate actual performance) exhibited lower physical activity and higher cardiovascular risk compared to those with a positive gap. This shows that knowledge of the brain cognition gap provides insights into factors contributing to cognitive resilience. Further, lower PET-derived measures of dopamine binding were linked to a greater brain cognition gap, mediated by regional functional variability. Together, our findings highlight the importance of brain state in connectome-based cognitive prediction and introduce the brain cognition gap as a potentially informative, dopamine-modulated marker of vulnerability to compromise brain function.
items.title_zh: 脑认知差距与多巴胺及脑健康因素的关联研究
items.summary_zh: 本研究旨在探讨个体脑功能差异与认知差异之间的关系。我们采用深度学习方法评估不同状态下（静息状态、观看电影和n-back任务）的功能连接组对情景记忆和工作记忆表现的预测能力。结果显示，任务期间的连接组，尤其是在观看电影时，能够有效预测认知领域的个体差异，而静息状态的连接组则对情景记忆有显著预测作用。此外，具有负脑认知差距（脑预测低估实际表现）的个体相比于正差距个体，表现出更低的身体活动水平和更高的心血管风险。这表明了解脑认知差距有助于识别与脑健康相关的因素。
items.l1_lead: 研究表明，脑认知差距与多巴胺及脑健康因素密切相关，任务期间的功能连接能有效预测个体的认知表现。
items.l2_summary:
本研究旨在探讨个体脑功能差异与认知差异之间的关系，特别关注多巴胺及脑健康因素的影响。研究采用深度学习方法评估在不同状态下（静息状态、观看电影和n-back任务）的功能连接组对情景记忆和工作记忆表现的预测能力。结果表明，在任务期间，尤其是在观看电影时，功能连接组能够有效预测个体在认知领域的差异，而静息状态下的连接组则对情景记忆的预测作用显著。

此外，研究发现具有负脑认知差距（即脑预测低估实际表现）的个体，其身体活动水平较低，且心血管风险较高，相较于正差距的个体。这一发现提示，了解脑认知差距不仅有助于揭示个体在认知表现上的差异，还能识别与脑健康相关的潜在因素。因此，研究结果强调了脑认知差距在评估个体健康状况和认知能力中的重要性，提示未来的研究可以进一步探讨如何通过改善脑健康来提升认知功能。

items.title: Cardiolipin deficiency disrupts electron transport chain and drives steatohepatitis
items.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a progressive disorder marked by lipid accumulation, leading to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). A key feature of the transition to MASH involves oxidative stress resulting from defects in mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS). Here, we show that pathological alterations in the lipid composition of the inner mitochondrial membrane (IMM) directly instigate electron transfer inefficiency to promote oxidative stress. Specifically, mitochondrial cardiolipin (CL) was downregulated with MASLD/MASH in humans and in mice. Hepatocyte-specific CL synthase knockout (CLS-LKO) led to spontaneous and robust MASH with extensive steatotic and fibrotic phenotype. Loss of CL paradoxically increased mitochondrial respiratory capacity but also promoted electron leak primarily at sites III QO and II F of the electron transport chain (ETC), reduced the formation of I + III 2 + IV respiratory supercomplex, and disrupted the propensity of coenzyme Q to become reduced. Thus, low mitochondrial CL disrupts the ETC to promote oxidative stress and contributes to the pathogenesis of MASH.
items.title_zh: 心磷脂缺乏破坏电子传递链并驱动脂肪性肝炎
items.summary_zh: 代谢功能障碍相关脂肪肝病（MASLD）是一种以脂质积累为特征的进展性疾病，最终导致代谢功能障碍相关脂肪性肝炎（MASH）。MASH转变的一个关键特征是由于线粒体氧化磷酸化（OXPHOS）缺陷引起的氧化应激。研究表明，内线粒体膜（IMM）脂质组成的病理变化直接导致电子转移效率降低，从而促进氧化应激。具体而言，心磷脂（CL）在MASLD/MASH患者和小鼠中均下调。肝细胞特异性CL合成酶敲除（CLS-LKO）导致自发性和显著的MASH，伴随广泛的脂肪变性和纤维化表型。CL的缺失反而增加了线粒体呼吸能力，但也主要在电子传递链（ETC）的III QO和II F位点促进了电子泄漏，减少了I + III 2 + IV呼吸超复合体的形成，并破坏了辅酶Q的还原倾向。因此，低水平的线粒体CL破坏了ETC，促进了氧化应激，并对MASH的发病机制产生影响。
items.l1_lead: 心磷脂缺乏导致电子传递链功能受损，进而引发氧化应激和代谢功能障碍相关脂肪性肝炎的发生。
items.l2_summary:
代谢功能障碍相关脂肪肝病（MASLD）是一种以脂质积累为特征的进展性疾病，最终可能发展为代谢功能障碍相关脂肪性肝炎（MASH）。MASH的转变与线粒体氧化磷酸化（OXPHOS）缺陷引起的氧化应激密切相关。研究发现，内线粒体膜（IMM）脂质组成的病理变化直接导致电子转移效率降低，从而促进氧化应激的发生。具体而言，心磷脂（CL）在MASLD/MASH患者和小鼠模型中均表现出下调的现象。通过肝细胞特异性心磷脂合成酶敲除（CLS-LKO），研究者观察到自发性和显著的MASH，伴随广泛的脂肪变性和纤维化表型。

值得注意的是，CL的缺失虽然增加了线粒体的呼吸能力，但却主要在电子传递链（ETC）的III QO和II F位点促进了电子泄漏，导致I + III 2 + IV呼吸超复合体的形成减少，并破坏了辅酶Q的还原倾向。这一现象表明，低水平的线粒体CL不仅破坏了ETC的正常功能，还加剧了氧化应激的发生，从而对MASH的发病机制产生了重要影响。因此，心磷脂的缺乏被认为是导致电子传递链功能障碍和脂肪性肝炎进展的关键因素。

items.title: Surgical management of intraocular lens dislocation in highly myopic eyes
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the postoperative visual function, intraocular lens (IOL) positional stability and ocular safety of surgical strategies tailored to capsular support status for the treatment of IOL dislocation in patients with high myopia, and to explore the potential impact of such complex surgeries on macular microcirculation.MethodsThis single-center retrospective included 28 patients (28 eyes) with high myopia and IOL dislocation who underwent surgical treatment from January 2024 to August 2025. Surgical approaches were selected based on preoperative anatomical conditions and capsular status, including IOL explantation without secondary IOL implantation in 10 eyes, in-the-bag IOL repositioning in 6 eyes, and sutured scleral fixation of a posterior chamber IOL in 12 eyes. The primary outcome measures were uncorrected distance visual acuity (UDVA), corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA), and IOL tilt and decentration before surgery and at 6 months postoperatively. Safety measures included intraocular pressure (IOP), corneal endothelial cell density (ECD), postoperative complications. Postoperative retinal microcirculation parameters assessed by WF-OCTA were included as exploratory outcomes. Whereas the IOL-position comparison included only the 18 operated eyes retaining an IOL and their corresponding 18 matched control eyes. Before quantitative analysis, all OCTA images were reviewed for image quality.ResultsCompared with preoperative values, UDVA (0.59 ± 0.46 logMAR, P = 0.005) and CDVA (0.38 ± 0.59 logMAR, P = 0.031) were significantly improved at 6 months postoperatively. Postoperative IOL position was evaluated in the 18 eyes retaining an IOL; 3 (16.7%) exceeded the 6° tilt threshold and 2 (11.1%) exceeded the 0.6 mm decentration threshold. The postoperative 2D tilt of IOL was 4.51 ± 2.17°, 2D decentration was 0.45 ± 0.33 mm, 3D tilt was 4.41 ± 2.09°, and 3D decentration was 0.44 ± 0.34 mm. Corneal ECD decreased from 2672.72 ± 312.26 cells/mm2 preoperatively to 2356.61 ± 420.15 cells/mm2 postoperatively (P < 0.001), yet no corneal decompensation occurred. IOP remained stable during the follow-up period, and the incidence of complications was low. Regional WF-OCTA parameters varied between the operated and matched control eyes, without a consistent pattern across macular regions.ConclusionIn patients with high myopia and IOL dislocation, different surgical approaches can achieve stable intraocular optical reconstruction and improve mid-to-long-term visual function under the corresponding anatomical conditions. Although the magnitude of visual acuity improvement is limited in this population due to high myopia- related high-risk fundus factors.

items.title: Correction: Best evidence summary for the management of epidermal growth factor receptor inhibitor-induced skin toxicity symptoms in cancer patients
Pulmonary hypertension optimal screening in interstitial lung disease (PHOS-ILD): a scoring system for the detection of pulmonary hypertension in patients with interstitial lung disease
items.abstract: BackgroundPulmonary hypertension (PH) is a common comorbidity of interstitial lung disease (ILD). Timely detection may improve outcomes through implementation of PH specific treatments.MethodsRetrospective, multicenter study aiming to identify features that predict PH in patients with ILD. In the derivation cohort (ILD cohort—University of South Florida), we identified predictors of PH in ILD and created a scoring system using the rounded value of odds ratio for each significant parameter. Correlation with hemodynamic parameters was investigated in the derivation and validation cohort (Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis cohort—Cleveland Clinic).ResultsWe included 164 patients with ILD that underwent right heart catheterization (RHC) [derivation cohort: n = 118, median age (years, 95% CI): 69.0 (65.9–71.0), female gender: 65 (54.6%), median mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) (mmHg, 95% CI): 25.0 (23.0–27.0), median pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) [Wood units (WU), 95% CI]: 3.6 (3.0–4.3), validation cohort: n = 46, median age (95% CI): 63.0 (60.0–66.0), female gender: 17 (37%), median mPAP (mmHg, 95% CI): 20.5 (18.0–27.2), median PVR (WU, 95% CI): 3.1 (2.2–3.4)]. Parameters and optimal cut-offs that significantly predicted precapillary PH in the derivation cohort were: age>42 years, heart rate recovery (HRR) at 1 min ≤ 15 bpm in 6-min walk test (6 MWT), 6-min walk distance (6 MWD) ≤ 270 meters, B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) > 136 pg/mL, pulmonary artery to ascending aorta diameter ratio (PA/AA) > 1 in high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT), main PA diameter > 29 mm in HRCT, right ventricular systolic pressure > 42 mmHg on echocardiogram. We created a PH detection model that ranged from 0 to 28. The optimal cut-off threshold for the detection of PH was > 14 (80% sensitivity, 68% specificity, AUC: 0.78). A simplified scoring system without BNP and main PA diameter (range: 0–21) maintained the same AUC. The simplified scoring system exhibited positive correlation with mean pulmonary artery pressure both in the derivation (rho = 0.47, p < 0.0001) and validation cohort (rho = 0.36, p = 0.013).ConclusionThis study demonstrates that incorporation of demographic, functional, imaging, and echocardiographic characteristics can optimize the early identification of precapillary PH in patients with ILD, paving the way to structured screening strategies. Timely detection of PH might lead to timely implementation of emerging PH specific treatments in patients with ILDs.

items.title: Is painless colonoscopy associated with trainee learning? A single-center study of insertion speed and adenoma detection curves in 1,769 procedures
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo compare the learning curves of cecal intubation time and adenoma detection rate (ADR) between painless (sedated) and conventional (non-sedated) colonoscopy performed by trainees.MethodsThis single-center retrospective cohort comprised the first 1,769 colonoscopies performed by eight trainees without prior colonoscopy experience, grouped by sedation status into a conventional group (n = 852) and a painless group (n = 917). Mixed-effects models characterized the learning trajectories of cecal intubation time and ADR, and an extended model allowing a random case-order slope tested individual heterogeneity. The caseload to independent cecal intubation competency was estimated with a rolling 20-procedure success-rate threshold and Bernoulli cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis.ResultsCecal intubation time was shorter in the painless group (median 6 vs. 10 min, P < 0.001). The case-order × procedure-type interaction fell from −0.113/SD (P < 0.001) in the random-intercept model to −0.027/SD (P = 0.589) in the random-slope model and was not significant under an exact trainee-level permutation test (exact P = 0.23); the overall shortening of intubation time with painless colonoscopy was robust to all specifications. Sedation status, calendar era, and scope model were highly correlated at the trainee level (r = 0.92), precluding separation of their independent effects. The overall ADR was 13.0% and declined early with experience (odds ratio 0.80/SD, P = 0.002). Fewer procedures were required to reach independent cecal intubation competency in the painless group (rolling threshold 37 vs. 114; CUSUM 107 vs. 134); however, this difference could not be separated from calendar era and equipment upgrades.ConclusionIntubation time was shorter overall under sedation, but the faster learning of the painless group vanished once individual heterogeneity was modeled, and ADR showed no robust improvement. Sedation, era, and equipment were confounded; no causal inference regarding the effect of sedation on learning can be drawn from these data, and prospective confirmation is required. Intubation speed alone should not serve as a benchmark of overall colonoscopy competence.

items.title: Association of early neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio trajectories with cardiac recovery and live ICU discharge in patients with sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy: a retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: BackgroundSepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SIC) is characterized by potentially reversible myocardial dysfunction accompanied by a profound systemic inflammatory response. However, the prognostic significance of early dynamic changes in the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) in patients with SIC remains unclear. This study aimed to identify distinct early NLR trajectories and examine their associations with cardiac recovery and live discharge from the intensive care unit (ICU).MethodsThis single-center retrospective cohort study included patients with SIC admitted to the Department of Critical Care Medicine, Hebei Cangzhou Hospital of Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine. NLR values were collected at ICU admission and at 24, 48, and 72 h thereafter. Latent class mixed modeling was used to identify distinct 72-h NLR trajectories. A 72-h landmark design was applied. The primary outcome was live ICU discharge within 28 days, with ICU death treated as a competing event and analyzed using Fine–Gray regression. The secondary outcome was cardiac recovery by days 5–7, defined as a follow-up left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of ≥50% or an absolute increase of ≥10 percentage points from baseline. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between NLR trajectories and cardiac recovery.ResultsA total of 510 patients contributed 2,040 longitudinal NLR measurements. Three distinct trajectories were identified: low-stable (n = 230, 45.1%), high-decreasing (n = 170, 33.3%), and persistent-high (n = 110, 21.6%). The geometric mean NLR changed from 7.85 to 6.16, from 18.47 to 8.01, and from 14.95 to 22.87, respectively, during the first 72 h. Live ICU discharge occurred in 85.7%, 67.1%, and 36.4% of patients in the three groups, respectively. Compared with the low-stable group, the adjusted subdistribution hazard ratios for live ICU discharge were 0.49 [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.38–0.63; P < 0.001] for the high-decreasing group and 0.25 (95% CI, 0.17–0.37; P < 0.001) for the persistent-high group. Cardiac recovery occurred in 80.4%, 61.8%, and 42.7% of patients, respectively. The corresponding adjusted odds ratios were 0.48 (95% CI, 0.29–0.79; P = 0.004) and 0.27 (95% CI, 0.14–0.51; P < 0.001). Associations with live ICU discharge were consistent across predefined subgroups. Septic shock showed an exploratory interaction with the association between NLR trajectories and cardiac recovery (P for interaction=0.034). Sensitivity analyses yielded similar results.ConclusionsEarly 72-h NLR trajectories were independently associated with cardiac recovery and live ICU discharge in patients with SIC. A persistent-high trajectory identified patients with the poorest prognosis, whereas a high-decreasing trajectory was associated with intermediate outcomes. Serial assessment of NLR may provide a simple and clinically accessible tool for early risk stratification in SIC, although prospective external validation is warranted.

items.title: Cultural context of professional identity formation: a perspective of health profession educators in Botswana
items.abstract: In Botswana, the phrase “motho ke motho ka batho—“I am because you are” is culturally a way of life and core to who we are as a people. As Batswana, our relationships and the evolution of our individual and collective identities are built on this key concept of Botho/Ubuntu. For us, Botho dictates that one does not merely “become” but “becomes with” in relation to identity formation, and by extension, professional identity formation (PIF). In this paper, the authors share their perspectives on professional identity formation (PIF) for health professions educators in the context of scarce African and non-Western epistemologies in the literature. The authors' guiding question and focus is: are the existing models/frameworks of PIF contextually relevant? If not, how can they be enriched and contextualized? This is one of the key tensions in the PIF discourse. The authors contend that contextualizing PIF efforts must integrate holistic cultural lenses and local ontologies into the current PIF models. We illustrate how leveraging indigenous knowledge frameworks encapsulated in the Botho belief system could contextualize existing PIF frameworks using a model we have termed, “Mabogo Dinku”. The phrase Mabogo Dinku is derived from a prominent Setswana proverb, “mabogo dinku a a thebana”, meaning, working together towards a common goal. The model is in a pictorial form and highlights the interconnectivity between the different frameworks. The model suggests that if any of the frameworks are misapplied the whole Botho belief system weakens and so too the concept of “becoming with”.

items.title: ADH7 and plasma proteins mediate smoking-related esophageal cancer: genetic causality and therapeutic insight
items.abstract: BackgroundSmoking has been linked to alterations in plasma protein profiles and increased risk of esophageal cancer (EC). However, the precise mediating roles of plasma proteins in this relationship remain unclear. This study explores the mediation effects of plasma proteins in smoking-associated EC, utilizing genetic proxies to uncover potential biological mechanisms underpinning this association.MethodsGenetic correlation and Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses were applied to examine the association between smoking traits and EC. Pathway enrichment analysis explored circulatory protein changes in smokers. A two-step mediation MR analysis identified key plasma proteins involved in smoking-related EC pathogenesis. Survival analysis assessed the impact of transcriptional levels of mediators on EC prognosis, while phenome-wide association studies (PheWAS) evaluated the safety of targeted molecules and investigated potential pleiotropy. The expression and function of ADH7 were evaluated by qRT-PCR and in vitro experiments.ResultsGenetic correlation analysis showed significant links between smoking and EC, supported by MR findings that confirmed a causal relationship. Smoking was found to influence pathways related to cytokine signaling, immune activation, and the STAT pathway. Five plasma proteins (ADH7, CPXM1, FUT3, GZMM, LYPD3) were identified as mediators in smoking-driven EC risk. Among these, ADH7 emerged as a key protein and was consistently associated with smoking traits; high ADH7 mRNA expression in EC tumor tissue was associated with reduced progression-free survival. PheWAS inferred that ADH7-targeted interventions might pose risks of neurological or psychiatric side effects, though these were not statistically significant. qRT-PCR and immunohistochemistry showed that ADH7 was downregulated in EC tissues relative to adjacent normal mucosa, and functional assays demonstrated that overexpression of ADH7 suppressed the proliferative and migratory capacity of EC cells. Serum ELISA further revealed that circulating ADH7 concentrations were elevated in smokers and in EC patients, with the highest levels observed in smoking EC patients, supporting a role for smoking-driven elevation of circulating ADH7 in EC risk.ConclusionsThis study reveals a compartment-specific, dual role for ADH7 in smoking-related EC: elevated circulating ADH7, driven in part by smoking, is associated with increased EC risk, whereas ADH7 acts as a tumor suppressor within esophageal tumor tissue. These findings provide novel genetic and mechanistic insights into smoking-related EC pathogenesis and highlight the importance of distinguishing circulating from tissue-level protein function when interpreting biomarker-disease associations.

items.title: Investigating risk factors and developing a predictive model for venous thromboembolism in patients with sepsis
items.abstract: BackgroundPatients with sepsis are at high risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, existing assessment tools designed for general medical or surgical populations may inadequately capture the specific risk profile of septic patients. This study aimed to identify independent predictors of VTE in sepsis and develop a sepsis-specific prediction model.MethodsIn this retrospective cohort study, adult patients with sepsis diagnosed at a single center (2015–2024) were enrolled. Candidate predictors and treatments were restricted to data available within the first 24 h of diagnosis. After exclusions, 157 VTE cases and 703 matched non-VTE controls formed the prediction cohort, which was split into training (n = 602) and validation (n = 258) sets. The Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique was applied to the training set. LASSO regression followed by multivariable logistic regression identified independent factors for the nomogram. Model performance was assessed via discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis and compared with the Padua and Caprini scores in the validation cohort.ResultsAmong 3,228 sepsis patients, 157 (4.86%) developed VTE. Multivariable analysis identified four independent predictors: surgery within 3 months, central venous catheterization within 24 h, history of VTE ≥1 year prior, and absence of early anticoagulant therapy (all P < 0.001). The resulting nomogram showed excellent discrimination (AUC: 0.905, 95% CI: 0.875–0.935 in training; 0.909, 95% CI: 0.867–0.951 in validation) and good calibration. Decision curve analysis supported its clinical utility. In the validation cohort, the nomogram significantly outperformed the Padua (AUC: 0.712) and Caprini (AUC: 0.738) scores, demonstrating superior incremental predictive value (P < 0.001 for net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement).ConclusionsA sepsis-specific nomogram incorporating recent surgery, early catheterization, previous VTE, and absence of early anticoagulation demonstrated good discrimination and calibration. It outperformed the Padua and Caprini tools in internal validation. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

items.title: Admission C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio and serum creatinine in relation to in-hospital mortality in non-HIV tuberculous meningitis: a retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: BackgroundThe independent and joint associations of admission C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) and serum creatinine with mortality in tuberculous meningitis (TBM) remain uncertain.MethodsWe analyzed a single-center retrospective cohort of non-HIV patients hospitalized with TBM from October 2013 to January 2024. Exposure measurements were the first tests within 24 h of admission, before acute interventions. Multivariable logistic regression modeled both exposures continuously, adjusted for age nonlinearly and prespecified covariates, and tested exposure nonlinearity and interaction. Covariate-only multiple imputation generated 20 datasets. Cohort-specific upper-quartile groups were descriptive. An adult sensitivity analysis used estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) calculated with the 2021 CKD-EPI equation.ResultsAmong 1,574 eligible patients, 187 died in hospital. The primary analysis included 1,563 patients and all 187 deaths; 11 survivors lacked CAR (n = 3) or creatinine (n = 8), without overlap. Creatinine showed evidence of nonlinearity (P = 0.022), whereas CAR did not (P = 0.105). The linear CAR estimate was near the null (adjusted odds ratio [OR] per doubling, 1.02; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.88–1.18); the interaction P value was 0.065. Relative to serum creatinine of 48 µmol/L, adjusted ORs for death were 1.31 (95% CI: 1.11–1.55) at 65 µmol/L, 1.49 (1.15–1.92) at 80 µmol/L, and 1.62 (1.17–2.24) at 100 µmol/L. Descriptive group mortality ranged from 9.02% when both markers were below their 75th percentiles to 19.38% when both were at or above them. Among 1,372 adults, the OR per 10 mL/min/1.73 m2 lower eGFR was 1.045 (0.984–1.109; P = 0.150).ConclusionsAdmission creatinine had a nonlinear adjusted association with in-hospital mortality in non-HIV TBM. CAR yielded a near-null linear estimate, and the interaction analysis did not establish effect modification. Unmeasured neurological severity limits interpretation; these results do not define kidney dysfunction, a clinical cutoff, or a clinically useful prediction model.

items.title: BCG-YOLO: an efficient YOLO-based framework for multi-class blood cell detection in microscopic images
items.abstract: ObjectivesAutomated blood cell detection from microscopic images is essential for routine hematological examination and computer-assisted laboratory diagnosis. However, accurate detection remains challenging because of the small size, dense distribution, overlap, and indistinct boundaries of blood cells. This study aimed to develop an efficient deep learning framework for accurate multi-class detection of blood cells in microscopic images.MethodsWe developed BCG-YOLO, an enhanced detector based on YOLO11n that integrates a lightweight backbone network, an improved multi-scale feature fusion module, and a dynamic detection head to improve feature representation and adaptive detection of small and densely distributed blood cells. The proposed model was evaluated on the public BCCD dataset and compared with representative one-stage detectors, transformer-based methods, and real-time object detection models. Ablation studies were conducted to assess the effectiveness of each proposed component. Additional five-fold cross-validation and paired image-level bootstrap analyses were performed for YOLO11n and BCG-YOLO.ResultsOn the original fixed test split, BCG-YOLO achieved an mAP@0.5 of 95.3%, an mAP@0.5:0.95 of 67.6%, and a recall of 89.8% while requiring only 3.80 GFLOPs. Under the common training and evaluation protocol used in this study, BCG-YOLO achieved the best overall detection performance among all evaluated models. Ablation experiments further demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed modules, confirming consistent improvements in overall detection performance and computational efficiency.ConclusionsBCG-YOLO provided a favorable balance between detection accuracy and computational cost in the internal evaluation on BCCD. These findings support its feasibility for microscopic blood-cell detection, while independent external validation is required to establish generalizability across laboratories, staining protocols, and imaging systems.

items.title: Prolonged infusion of meropenem for suspected intracystic infection in polycystic kidney disease during pregnancy: a case report
items.abstract: BackgroundIntrarenal cyst infection in polycystic kidney disease (PKD) is hard to confirm and harder to treat during pregnancy, when lipid-soluble antibiotics are generally avoided.CaseA pregnant woman at approximately 10 weeks’ gestation presented with recurrent fever and flank pain for over one month, with acute exacerbation one day prior to admission. Laboratory tests revealed progressively elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) levels despite repeatedly negative cultures. Serial ultrasound showed a right upper-pole renal cyst that evolved to exhibit internal septations and debris.Treatment and outcomeCyst aspiration was avoided; meropenem 1 g every 8 h was initiated on admission and converted to prolonged infusion (1 g infused over more than 3 h) on Day 4, followed by step-down oral amoxicillin–clavulanate, for a total antimicrobial course of 32 days. Fever resolved and CRP normalized; pregnancy continued uneventfully.ConclusionIn a pregnant patient with suspected PKD cyst infection, prolonged-infusion meropenem was followed by clinical improvement. The favorable response observed supports further evaluation of this therapeutic strategy, despite the absence of microbiological confirmation.

items.title: Clinical characteristics and mortality risk of sarcopenia in interstitial lung disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: ObjectiveSarcopenia, prevalent in interstitial lung disease (ILD), increases the risk of poor outcomes. This study aimed to define the clinical characteristics of ILD patients with sarcopenia (ILD-S) and quantify sarcopenia's impact on mortality.MethodsWe systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Scopus for English studies up to 1 September 2026 reporting clinical variables (mean ± SD) in ILD vs. ILD-S groups and adjusted hazard ratios with 95% confidence intervals (CI) for mortality risk. Subgroup analyses were stratified by sarcopenia diagnostic criteria, ILD subtype, and survival time. Heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran's Q and I2 statistics. Sensitivity analyses (leave-one-out) and publication bias assessments (Egger's test, trim-and-fill method) were performed.ResultsFourteen studies comprising 1,546 participants (628 with ILD-S) were included. Compared with ILD patients without sarcopenia, those with ILD-S were significantly older (WMD = 3.03, 95% CI: 2.12–3.93), had higher Gender-Age-Physiology (GAP) scores (WMD = 0.43, 95% CI: 0.15 to 0.71), and a higher FEV₁/FVC ratio (WMD = 1.97, 95% CI: 0.21 to 3.73, P = 0.03). Conversely, the ILD-S group showed lower values for FEV₁% predicted (WMD = −6.95, 95% CI: −9.80 to −4.09), FVC% predicted (WMD = −9.46, 95% CI: −12.04 to −6.88), DLCO% predicted (WMD = −5.87, 95% CI: −11.68 to −0.06), body mass index (WMD = −1.35, 95% CI: −1.89 to −0.82), handgrip strength (WMD = −12.80, 95% CI: −17.02 to −8.58), 6-minute walk distance (WMD = −31.01, 95% CI: −60.05 to −1.97), and appendicular skeletal muscle index (WMD = −1.45, 95% CI: −2.15 to −0.76). No significant difference was observed in smoking history. Sarcopenia was strongly associated with increased mortality risk (HR = 2.02, 95% CI: 1.67 to 2.45), and this association remained stable across different follow-up periods. Sensitivity and publication bias analyses confirmed the robustness of the findings.ConclusionPatients with ILD-S exhibit a distinctive profile characterized by older age, higher GAP scores, poorer pulmonary function, lower BMI, reduced muscle strength and mass, and significantly elevated mortality. Systematic recognition of these clinical features may facilitate early identification of ILD-S and inform the development of targeted interventions to improve patient outcomes.Systematic Review Registrationhttps://inplasy.com/, INPLASY202570030.

items.title: Pathogen-targeted quick multiplex PCR identification of Chlamydia psittaci and Haemophilus influenzae coinfection in pneumonia: a case report
items.abstract: This study describes a rare case of pneumonia induced by coinfection with Chlamydia psittaci (C. psittaci) and Haemophilus influenzae (H. influenzae). The patient had a history of chronic nephritis and long-term pigeon breeding. The initial manifestation was slurred speech, followed by rapid progression to high fever and respiratory failure. Chest computed tomography revealed bilateral interstitial pneumonia, predominantly in the right lung. Pathogen-targeted quick multiplex polymerase chain reaction (pt-qPCR) confirmed the pathogens as C. psittaci and H. influenzae, and metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) further verified consistent results. After 7-days of combination therapy with doxycycline and azithromycin, the treatment was switched to doxycycline combined with moxifloxacin for an additional 8-days. The patient achieved complete recovery and was discharged from the hospital. This case suggests that pt-qPCR may facilitate early identification of mixed infections in patients with severe pneumonia and a history of avian exposure, thereby providing valuable information to guide clinical decision-making.

items.title: Development and internal validation of a CatBoost–SHAP-guided nomogram for significant liver fibrosis in children with chronic hepatitis B
items.abstract: BackgroundSignificant liver fibrosis can develop in children with chronic hepatitis B (CHB), yet liver biopsy is invasive and unsuitable for repeated assessment. We developed an interpretable, non-invasive prediction model for significant fibrosis in pediatric CHB and evaluated whether baseline risk stratification was associated with subsequent treatment outcomes.MethodsThis retrospective study included 232 children with CHB who underwent liver biopsy, with significant fibrosis defined as Scheuer stage S ≥ 2. Patients were randomly assigned to a development cohort (80%) and a held-out test set (20%). A CatBoost model with Bayesian hyperparameter optimization was used to identify the most informative predictors, and these variables were incorporated into a logistic regression nomogram guided by Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). Model performance was evaluated by discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, and DeLong testing. Associations between baseline risk groups and longitudinal outcomes were examined using generalized estimating equations adjusted for age and sex and Kaplan–Meier analyses.ResultsSignificant fibrosis was identified in 96 children (41.4%). Liver stiffness measurement, alanine aminotransferase, and platelet count were retained in the final model. The nomogram achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.828 (95% CI, 0.767–0.889) in the development cohort and 0.782 (95% CI, 0.637–0.927) in the held-out test cohort, with performance comparable to that of the CatBoost model (P = 0.240). Compared with the low-risk group, high-risk patients showed greater longitudinal reductions in alanine and aspartate aminotransferase, whereas longitudinal changes in liver stiffness measurement and hepatitis B virus DNA were similar between groups. Conversely, low-risk patients achieved virological suppression, HBeAg seroconversion, and biochemical response earlier than those classified as high risk.ConclusionsAn interpretable three-variable prediction model based on CatBoost-guided feature selection accurately identified significant fibrosis in children with CHB while maintaining performance comparable to the machine-learning model. Baseline risk stratification was also associated with subsequent treatment outcomes, although external validation is needed before clinical implementation.

items.title: Development and preliminary psychometric evaluation of a spectacle trial-wear questionnaire for distance single-vision prescriptions
items.abstract: BackgroundExisting vision questionnaires were not designed to standardize immediate patient appraisal of a distance single-vision spectacle prescription during trial wear. This study developed and preliminarily evaluated the Adult Spectacle Trial-Wearing Experience Scale (ASTWES) for this decision point.MethodsCandidate items were informed by a structured literature search and interviews with eye-care and dispensing professionals, refined through two Delphi rounds, cognitively debriefed with 10 target patients, and piloted in 150 adults. Item reduction used corrected item-total correlations and principal-axis factoring with promax rotation. The independent formal psychometric evaluation sample comprised 393 adults within the prespecified 18–35-year age range; ordinal confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), robust maximum-likelihood sensitivity analysis, and reliability coefficients were used. An eligible subsample of 98 participants provided a 1-month satisfaction rating for exploratory association analyses.ResultsThe final questionnaire contained 9 items in 3 correlated domains: clarity and focus, comfort and stability, and environmental adaptation. Retained pilot-item loadings ranged from 0.694 to 0.890. The correlated three-factor model was supported under both CFA estimators, whereas a single-factor model fit poorly. Subscale Cronbach's alpha values ranged from 0.769 to 0.803. Omega hierarchical was 0.641, favoring subscale-first interpretation. The overall mean item score correlated with 1-month satisfaction (Spearman rho = 0.753, p < 0.001); its exploratory AUC was 0.850 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.772–0.918).ConclusionsASTWES is a concise candidate questionnaire with preliminary evidence of a correlated three-domain structure, acceptable internal consistency, and short-term clinical association in Chinese adults aged 18–35 years. Further independent patient-centered content evaluation and external validation are needed before routine use or fixed decision thresholds are considered.

items.title: A hybrid deep learning–based OCR model for handwritten medical prescriptions
items.abstract: The current trend involving the use of paper-based medical prescriptions and the exchange of such by the social media is a major problem in automated and accurate text extraction in healthcare processes. This paper suggests a complete smart pipeline to digitize the images of medical prescriptions with lightweight deep learning-based classification, specialized Optical Character Recognition (OCR) engines, and comparative benchmarking of results using a large language model (LLM). The web scraped images of medical prescriptions are initially processed through a GhostNetV2 classifier to differentiate between handwritten and digital medical prescriptions. According to this choice, digital images are sent to PaddleOCR, and handwritten images are considered in Tesseract OCR so that each image could be processed by the best suitable recognition engine. The OCR outputs from both branches are benchmarked against GPT-4o (OpenAI) as an independent baseline to assess competitive performance and provide error-rate context. Experimental analysis shows that the suggested adaptive routing strategy is characterized by the fact that it has a high classification rate and the character and word error rates are significantly lower than those single-OCR techniques. The system is competitive with, though does not exceed, the raw accuracy of a state-of-the-art LLM-based OCR baseline (GPT-4o), while offering practical advantages in cost, transparency, and on-premises deployability that the black-box, per-call LLM baseline does not. The findings verify that the combination of lightweight classifiers and multi-OCR decision routing and multi-LLM-aided comparative benchmarking offers a scalable and robust solution to real-world medical prescriptions digitization, which adds to better automation, accuracy, and safety in healthcare information processing.

items.title: Abdominal allergic reaction syndrome: a tentative definition
items.abstract: BackgroundSome patients with acute abdominal pain present with imaging findings suggestive of severe intestinal pathology, yet they remain hemodynamically stable and respond to corticosteroids rather than surgery. Recognizing this pattern early can prevent unnecessary laparotomy.CasesThree female patients (aged 91, 78, and 57 years) admitted to the emergency department presented with acute abdominal pain and diffuse bowel wall edema on a CT scan. Despite alarming imaging results, all three patients remained hemodynamically stable. The symptoms improved rapidly with intravenous methylprednisolone, and all patients were discharged without surgery.ConclusionsWe propose Abdominal Allergic Reaction Syndrome (AARS) as a preliminary recognition framework for this clinico-radiological pattern. AARS is not intended to replace specific diagnoses such as immunoglobulin A (IgA) vasculitis or lupus enteritis. Rather, it serves as an early identifier at a stage when the underlying etiology remains unclear. The core features (hemodynamic stability and clinico-radiological mismatch, supported by normal lactate levels) may help emergency physicians avoid unnecessary surgery while proceeding with the diagnostic workup. The term “allergic” is used here in its broader immunological sense (encompassing all type I–IV hypersensitivity reactions) and is not restricted to IgE-mediated reactions.

items.title: Editorial: Paediatric drug development
Correction: CXCL2/CXCR2 pathway regulates CD169high large macrophages to promote progression of malignant pleural effusion from lung adenocarcinoma
The value of cardiopulmonary ultrasound in diagnosing cardiogenic pulmonary edema in patients with heart failure
items.abstract: ObjectiveHeart failure (HF) is generally complicated with cardiogenic pulmonary edema (CPE), the early diagnosis and treatment is essential. We aimed to evaluate the effects of cardiopulmonary ultrasound (CPUS) in the diagnosis of CPE in HF patients, to provide reference for the management of HF.MethodsHF patients entering The People's Hospital of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region & Guangxi Academy of Medical Sciences intensive care unit (ICU) between March 2025 and July 2026 were included. All patients underwent CPUS and chest computed tomography (CT), and comparison of the detection rates of cardiogenic pulmonary edema between CPUS and CT.ResultsA total of 117 patients with HF were enrolled in this study. Of the 117 HF patients, 46 were diagnosed with CPE, and 43 were correctly diagnosed by CT, with a diagnostic accuracy of 94.9%, the positive predictive value (PPV) was 93.5%, the negative predictive value (NPV) was 95.8%, the sensitivity was 93.5%, the specificity was 95.8%, the positive likelihood ratio (PLR) was 22, and the negative likelihood ratio (NLR) was 0.07. While 41 were correctly diagnosed by CPUS, with a diagnostic accuracy of 92.3%, the PPV was 91.1%, NPV was 93.1%, the sensitivity was 89.1%, the specificity was 94.3%, the PLR was 16, and the NLR was 0.12. Comparison of CT and CPUS in the diagnosis of CPE, there was no statistically significant difference between the two methods (X2 = 0.111, P > 0.05). And The Cohen's kappa for the diagnosis of CPE by CT and CPUS is 0.873 (95% CI was 0.782–0.963, P < 0.001).ConclusionsIn conclusion, the present study suggests that CPUS is feasible for identifying cardiogenic pulmonary edema in ICU patients with heart failure. Based on diagnostic agreement analysis, CPUS demonstrates promising performance for CPE detection in this critically-ill cohort.

items.title: Comparison of sodium azide- and cooling-based immobilization methods for Caenorhabditis elegans chemotaxis assays
items.abstract: Chemotaxis assays are widely used to quantify sensory-driven behavioral responses in Caenorhabditis elegans. Sodium azide is commonly used to immobilize animals at assay endpoints, although concerns have been raised that diffusion beyond the endpoint region could affect behavior before a choice is completed. We compared sodium azide-mediated immobilization with post-assay cooling using the repellent 1-octanol and attractant diacetyl. Wild-type animals showed robust avoidance of 30% 1-octanol and attraction to 0.5% diacetyl with either method, across multiple assay durations, and with or without worm food Escherichia coli OP50. These results support post-assay cooling as an alternative endpoint-scoring method.
items.authors: Ji, R.; Wibisono, S.; Sun, J.

items.title: Analysis of Phycodnaviridae Tetrapyrrole Enzymes: Subcellular Localization and Functional Divergence from Host Homologs
items.abstract: Rationale Recent viral metagenomic studies have revealed a broad repertoire of enzyme encoding genes in Phycodnaviridae, whose contributions to viral replication and host infection remain poorly understood. These genes may expand the metabolic repertoire of viruses during infection of green algal hosts. Because neither the roles of these proteins during infection nor their subcellular localization have been experimentally characterized, comparative sequence, structural, and biochemical analyses done in silico can generate testable hypotheses on structure, function and localization. Methods In a recent viral metagenomic dataset, we identified viral homologues of two eukaryotic enzymes involved in bilin biosynthesis: heme oxygenase-1 (vHMOX1) and Phycocyanobilin:Ferredoxin oxidoreductase (vPcyA). Viral and algal homologues were compared through sequence analyses and AlphaFold3 structural predictions. Predicted biochemical properties were analyzed for their compatibility with subcellular compartments. Active site architecture and putative substrate binding were compared between viral and algal proteins using homologous structures deposited in the Protein Data Bank (PDB). Results Viral HMOX1 and PcyA sequences are truncated compared to algal homologues, lacking the N-terminal extension associated with chloroplastic targeting. However biochemical properties, including isoelectric point and surface charge distribution, are compatible with localization in chloroplast. Structural comparisons reveal modifications in the viral HMOX1 active sites, including altered substrate binding and substitutions of key residues, likely indicating modified heme-binding properties. In addition to these modifications, chloroplastic ferredoxin interaction predictions show compatibility for use of this electron donor. In contrast, vPcyA models show no significant differences with their algal counterparts. Conclusions Predicted active site remodeling in vHMOX1 suggests that these viral homologues may have evolved distinct heme-binding properties. Unlike vPcyA, vHMOX1 homologs appear to have diverged more substantially from their algal counterparts, potentially reflecting functional specialization in the viral infection context.
items.authors: Zehnacker, S.; Caffarri, S.; Blanc, G.; Johnson, X.; Siponen, M.
items.title_zh: 对藻病毒科四吡咯酶的分析：亚细胞定位及功能差异
items.summary_zh: 近期的病毒宏基因组研究揭示了藻病毒科中编码酶的基因库，这些基因在病毒复制和宿主感染中的作用尚不明确。我们在一项病毒宏基因组数据集中识别了两种参与胆色素生物合成的真核酶的病毒同源物：血红素氧化酶-1（vHMOX1）和藻蓝蛋白：铁氧还蛋白氧化还原酶（vPcyA）。通过序列分析和AlphaFold3结构预测比较了病毒和藻类同源物。分析了预测的生化性质与亚细胞区室的兼容性。结果显示，病毒HMOX1和PcyA序列相比于藻类同源物存在缺失，缺乏与叶绿体靶向相关的N端延伸，但其生化性质与亚细胞功能仍有潜在关联。

items.title: Selective suppression and biasing of chemokine receptors CCR9 and ACKR4 through targeting CCL25 with de novo miniproteins
items.abstract: Chemokines and their receptors mediate cell migration and coordinate immune responses, while dysregulation can lead to inflammation. Therapeutic modulation of the chemokine signaling axis has proven difficult. Most drug discovery efforts target the receptors, whereas natural regulatory mechanisms modulate immune responses by directly binding to or modifying the chemokine ligands. Despite this insight, development of effective chemokine-directed modulators has remained elusive. Recent advances in de novo protein design offer an unprecedented opportunity to produce high-affinity binders that efficiently block protein-protein interactions. We implemented a computational workflow leveraging the BindCraft platform to generate miniprotein binders against CCL25, the chemokine ligand for the receptors CCR9 and ACKR4 and implicated in inflammatory bowel diseases. The unbiased development results in several miniproteins designed to block the receptor N-terminus from wrapping the chemokine and prevent productive engagement. Thus, these proteins suppress CCL25-mediated effector coupling and halt MOLT-4 lymphoblast migration. Another class of miniprotein, represented by VUP25111, is predicted to bind CCL25 along the chemokine {beta}1 strand and retained receptor binding. This complex inhibited arrestin recruitment to CCR9, but not to ACKR4, indicating receptor specificity. Additionally, G protein recruitment to CCR9 was unimpeded by VUP25111, suggesting that the miniprotein biased the native agonist towards G proteins. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of differentially targeting CCL25 to suppress CCR9 signaling and new tools to resolve the structural basis of chemokine receptor activation and bias.
items.authors: de Boer, B.; Lamme, T. D.; Verdwaald, K.; Santamaria Medina, S.; Nemeth, C. G.; Elfrink, E. M.; Smit, M. J.; de Esch, I. J.; Schafer, C. T.
items.title_zh: 靶向CCL25的de novo小蛋白选择性抑制CCR9和ACKR4受体
items.summary_zh: 趋化因子及其受体介导细胞迁移并协调免疫反应，失调可导致炎症。针对趋化因子信号轴的治疗调节一直困难。我们利用BindCraft平台开发了针对CCL25的小蛋白结合剂，CCL25是CCR9和ACKR4的趋化因子配体，与炎症性肠病相关。通过无偏开发，设计出几种小蛋白，阻止受体N端与趋化因子的结合，从而抑制CCL25介导的效应耦合，停止MOLT-4淋巴母细胞迁移。另一类小蛋白VUP25111被预测能沿着趋化因子β1链结合CCL25，并保持受体结合能力。该复合物抑制了对CCR9的逮捕素招募，但对ACKR4没有影响，显示出受体特异性。

items.title: High-yield expression and purification of the non-phosphorylated form of Human CaMKIIα Kinase
items.abstract: Human Ca2+/calmodulin (CaM)-dependent protein kinase II alpha (CaMKII) is a highly abundant and conserved protein in the brain. It is a multifunctional serine/threonine kinase that phosphorylates cellular substrates across subcellular compartments, activating signaling pathways essential for long-term memory storage. However, a detailed understanding of protein structure and enzyme-substrate interaction mechanisms require a method to produce active, stable, and pure proteins at scale. Since phosphorylation can alter catalytic activity and substrate affinity, examining the non-phosphorylated state enables an unbiased characterization of basal enzymatic function. Therefore, producing the non-phosphorylated form of the kinase is important for biochemical and structural studies aimed at understanding kinase activation mechanisms. We describe a detailed protocol for the expression and high-yield purification of full-length, non-phosphorylated human CaMKII in bacterial cells. CaMKII was co-expressed with {lambda}-phosphatase to maintain it in a non-phosphorylated state. Protein expression was induced by autoinduction at low temperature to enhance the stability and solubility of CaMKII. Recombinant CaMKII was purified by Ni-NTA affinity chromatography, followed by gel filtration chromatography. Although CaMKII has been considered difficult to purify in its non-phosphorylated form, we obtained it in high yield, and the protein was predominantly non-phosphorylated. Our results show that combining co-expression with autoinduction improves both the solubility and yield of the homogeneous non-phosphorylated form of CaMKII, which could be suitable for subsequent biochemical and structural studies.
items.authors: Yadav, S.; Gaude, L. D.; Kumar, S.

items.title: Heterotypic Condensate Formation by Prion Proteins and Pro-Inflammatory S100A9
items.abstract: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) of biomacromolecules has been shown to influence a large variety of biological processes via the formation of membraneless organelles. Aberrant LLPS, however, has been implicated in a number of oncological and neurodegenerative disorders. Proteins related to Alzheimer's, Parkinson's diseases and other major amyloidoses have all been shown to form these condensates. Interestingly, some amyloidogenic proteins were demonstrated to form heterotypic droplets, where both molecules coexisted within the same condensate and affected each other's aggregation. While such cross-interactions have been reported numerous times under non-LLPS conditions, the heterotypic droplet assemblies were only shown for a very limited number of amyloidogenic proteins. In this work, we examine heterotypic LLPS of prion proteins and the pro-inflammatory S100A9, whose cross-interaction under non-LLPS conditions we confirmed in a previous work. The results show that this interaction under condensation-promoting conditions enhances their aggregation, leading to the formation of a higher concentration of amyloid structures. These findings suggest that the pro-inflammatory S100A9 may have a critical role in promoting prion protein aggregation via the assembly of heterotypic condensates under high molecular crowding conditions.
items.authors: Veiveris, D.; Karalkeviciute, V.; Mikalauskaite, K.; Sulskis, D.; Ziaunys, M.

items.title: Covalent Solvatochromic Membrane Probe for Sensing Lipid Surrounding of Proteins
items.abstract: Plasma membranes (PM) have been traditionally studied by fluorescent probes by either labelling lipid or protein parts. Based on our MemGraft concept, we report a fluorescent probe based on solvatochromic dye Nile Red (MemGraft-NR) for sensing lipid organization in the immediate surrounding of proteins, i.e. at the protein-lipid interface. Two sequentially attached MemGraft scaffolds are required to ensure robust grafting of Nile Red to PM. In contrast to classical lipid-bound membrane probes, MemGraft-NR exhibits high resistance to the presence of serum and fixation with permeabilization. Two-color confocal imaging of MemGraft-NR in live cells reveals higher polarity at the protein-lipid interface compared to lipid-bound probe NR12A. Surprisingly, MemGraft-NR displays higher sensitivity to variation of cholesterol content in PM compared to NR12A, suggesting that protein-lipid interface is particularly impacted by changes in the lipid composition. MemGraft-NR also enabled in situ monitoring of lipid exchange and permeabilization of PM, something impossible for classical solvatochromic PM probes. Unexpectedly, MemGraft-NR reveals a dramatic decrease in the local polarity in early endosomes, suggesting that endosomal negative curvature provides strong impact on organization of the protein-lipid interface. The developed probe opens a new way to study biological membranes by sensing lipid surrounding of membrane proteins.
items.authors: Visser, M.; Loo Chin Moy, T.; Pelletier, R.; Klymchenko, A. S.

items.title: Coumarin-based blue excitable probe for functional screening of dehalogenase activity
items.abstract: In the enzymatic toolbox of depollution, hydrolytic dehalogenases are of particular interest for the bioremediation of organohalogenated compounds. To better identify and characterize these enzymes, it is important to develop appropriate sensing methods. Fluorescent probes for dehalogenase detection have been developed in the past years, however, to this date none were available for application using the common FITC parameters (i.e. excitation laser at 488 nm). To address this limitation, we herein report a new fluorescent probe, COU4-Cl, excitable in the violet (405 nm) and blue (488 nm) wavelengths adapted for the detection and characterization of haloalkane dehalogenases. Its applicability is discussed and evaluated in comparison to the previously described COU2-Cl probe only excitable in the violet (405 nm). This study shows the advantages and complementarity of the two probes, and further demonstrate their application for the discrimination of dehalogenase activity in whole cell assays.
items.authors: Mion, S.; Mallet, M.; Louis, Y.; Fontanay, S.; Ruaudel, F.; Bastian, F.; Jacolot, M.; Popowycz, F.; Oger, P. M.

items.title: Mycothiazole enables structural characterization of entire ubiquinone-accessing tunnel in mitochondrial respiratory complex I
items.abstract: Mitochondrial NADH-ubiquinone (UQ) oxidoreductase (respiratory complex I) reduces UQ within its long tunnel-like cavity, which is coupled to triggering proton translocation at the membrane domain. Although mammalian complex I adopts distinct "open" and "closed" conformations, the architecture of the UQ-accessing tunnel in the open conformation remains poorly defined owing to partial disorder of the UQ catalytic region near Fe-S cluster N2 in the tunnel. Here, we applied cryo-electron microscopy (EM) single particle analysis to determine the structures of complex I in bovine heart submitochondrial particles in the presence or absence of a mycothiazole-type inhibitor. Preceding photoaffinity labeling experiments using a synthetic photoreactive derivative ([125I]pMT) revealed that mycothiazole specifically labels the 49-kDa and ND1 subunits, both of which form a part of the UQ-accessing tunnel. Cryo-EM analysis demonstrated that bound mycothiazole reorganizes and stabilizes the UQ catalytic region in both open and closed conformations, enabling the first complete structural modeling of the entire UQ-accessing tunnel in the open conformation. Unexpectedly, in the presence of bound mycothiazole, loops of the PSST subunit forming the catalytic region in the tunnel adopted closed conformation-like features, whereas open conformation-like features were determined for the transmembrane helices of ND1 and ND6 subunits. The present study revealed that bound mycothiazole can reorganize the UQ catalytic region in the UQ-accessing tunnel and lead to a hybrid conformational state beyond the canonical open-versus-closed conformational model.
items.authors: Akisada, S.; Otani, R.; Masuya, T.; Miyako, S.; Saito, H.; Mitsuoka, K.; Miyoshi, H.; Yokoyama, K.; Murai, M.

items.title: Pancreatic progenitor cells respond to laminar shear stress with transcriptomic changes, accompanied by reduced YAP1 activity
items.abstract: The human pancreas secretes digestive fluid that flows through an extensive ductal network before emptying into the duodenum. However, little is known about how hydrodynamic forces influence pancreatic function and development. We hypothesized that pancreatic cells respond to physiological levels of fluid shear stress. In this study, we developed a microfluidic system featuring reversible sealing between the device layer and the cell culture substrate, enabling (1) conventional open-well cell culture prior to fluid shear stress application and (2) selective patterning of proteins and cells for migration studies. Channel dimensions were chosen to support 24-hour perfusion using standard syringe pumps. Using this platform, we investigated effects of physiological shear stress levels representing basal and activated pancreatic function (2, 8 and 33 mPa) on human iPSC-derived pancreatic progenitor cells. Pancreatic progenitor cells exhibit graded sensitivity to shear stress at the transcriptomic level. Specifically, shear stress upregulated expression of cell cycle-related gene sets; endocrine-associated genes including NEUROG3; and Notch receptor ligands (DLL1, DLL3) in a magnitude-dependent manner. The exposure to unidirectional fluid flow also resulted in a reduction in YAP1 protein content, decreased WWTR1 gene expression, and downregulation of YAP/TAZ target genes. Furthermore, barrier-based migration assays under shear stress revealed that cell patches expanded their boundaries both along and against the flow, with greater distance in the direction of flow. Our system and findings may help lay the foundation for understanding biophysical regulation of developmental processes in a physiologically important, yet hard-to-access, epithelial model system.
items.authors: Yu, X.; Jiju, A.; Souresh, R.; Hasani, M.; Gaebler, L.; Lewis, A.; Grapin-Botton, A.; Doyle, A.
items.title_zh: 胰腺前体细胞对层流剪切应力的转录组响应及YAP1活性降低
items.summary_zh: 人类胰腺分泌的消化液通过广泛的导管网络流动，最终排入十二指肠。然而，水动力学力对胰腺功能和发育的影响尚不清楚。本研究假设胰腺细胞会对生理水平的流体剪切应力作出反应。我们开发了一种微流控系统，能够在细胞培养基与设备层之间实现可逆密封，支持在施加流体剪切应力前进行常规开放式细胞培养，并进行蛋白质和细胞的选择性图案化。我们研究了代表基础和激活胰腺功能的生理剪切应力水平（2、8和33 mPa）对人类诱导多能干细胞来源的胰腺前体细胞的影响。结果显示，胰腺前体细胞在转录组水平上对剪切应力表现出分级敏感性，剪切应力上调了细胞周期相关基因、内分泌相关基因（如NEUROG3）及Notch受体配体（DLL1、DLL3）的表达。同时，单向流体流动还导致YAP1蛋白含量减少、WWTR1基因表达降低及YAP/TAZ靶基因下调。

items.title: Interconnected Macroporous GelMA Scaffolds for Cell Culture through Temperature Controlled Spinodal Decomposition
items.abstract: Developing biomaterials that faithfully recapitulate the complex architecture of native tissues is central to tissue engineering. Conventional hydrogels typically exhibit nanoscale porosity, which limits mass transport and cell migration and thereby constrains tissue development. Here, we exploit liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) to generate interconnected macroporous gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) scaffolds with tunable pore sizes ranging from 2 to 50 m under physiological pH conditions. By mapping the GelMA/dextran phase diagram, we identify a composition range in which LLPS occurs through spinodal decomposition, resulting in a spontaneous bicontinuous, trabecular-like architecture. Pore size can be further tuned by varying polymer concentrations and temperature. We advantageously combined thermal gradients and photopatterning to enable spatial control over pore morphology to fabricate hierarchically structured materials. The biological relevance of these architectures is assessed using fibroblasts cultured within controlled porosity gradients. We show that pore size strongly influences cell infiltration, growth, and spatial organization, with larger pores providing sufficient space for cell migration while reducing the dependence on matrix degradation. Pore size of 7-15 m is identified for maximizing fibroblast growth. Overall, our approach provides a versatile platform for porosity screening, enabling the engineering of biomimetic hydrogels with optimized microarchitectures tailored to specific biological contexts for three-dimensional cell culture.
items.authors: Dumas, S.; Gonzalez Martinez, D.; Peixoto De Oliveira, A.; Ferri-Angulo, D.; Bacchin, L.; Arcas, A.; Blatche, C.; Goudouneche, D.; Paounov, R.; Hut, M.; Puaud, M.; Foncy, J.; Moran-Mirabal, J.; Malaquin, L.

items.title: Designed nanofiber immunogens prime antibody responsesto diverse conformations of the HIV-1 fusion peptide
items.abstract: Focusing antibody responses towards known neutralizing epitopes is a major strategy for protective immunization. Targeting flexible antigenic regions represents a unique challenge because functional antibodies must be able to bind the epitope of interest in multiple conformations. The fusion peptide (FP) of HIV-1 is a flexible peptide critical to viral entry of host cells for which broadly neutralizing antibodies have been identified. Because elicitation of potent, functional antibodies toward this epitope remains an unmet challenge in HIV-1 vaccination, we introduce a designed immunogen platform capable of raising anti-FP-antibodies with increased conformational tolerance relative to a traditional carrier protein. Antibodies induced by these immunogens bind heterologous FP sequences when elicited in mice and infant non-human primates. This platform shows promise for preclinical development to prime antibody responses toward FP of the HIV-1 envelope and can likely be translated to peptide immunofocusing for other viral pathogens.
items.authors: Fries, C. N.; Chen, J.-L.; Votaw, N. L.; Cossette, B.; Roe, E. F.; Dennis, M.; Curvino, E. J.; Issah, L.; Lazar, K. M.; Shetty, S.; Katz, R.; Nief, C. A.; Permar, S.; Van Rompay, K. K. A.; Fouda, G.; Collier, J. H.
items.title_zh: 设计纳米纤维免疫原激发针对HIV-1融合肽的抗体反应
items.summary_zh: 针对已知中和表位的抗体反应是保护性免疫的重要策略。由于HIV-1的融合肽（FP）是一个灵活的肽，对病毒进入宿主细胞至关重要，因此针对其灵活抗原区域的免疫应答面临挑战。我们引入了一种设计的免疫原平台，能够诱导相较于传统载体蛋白具有更高构象耐受性的抗-FP抗体。这些免疫原诱导的抗体在小鼠和婴儿非人灵长类动物中能够结合异源FP序列。该平台在临床前开发中显示出前景，有望为HIV-1包膜的FP激发抗体反应，并可能推广至其他病毒病原体的肽免疫聚焦。

items.title: Enriching microlaser-labelled cells by commercial flow cytometry-based cell sorting systems
items.abstract: Microlasers based on whispering-gallery modes (WGMs) provide bright, spectrally narrow emission, making them ideal optical probes for high-resolution cellular tagging, single-cell tracking, and biosensing. To reproducibly apply WGM microlasers in biomedical or tissue-engineering contexts, control over the number of lasers in a cell population is highly desirable. Here we use a commercial instrument for flow cytometry-based cell sorting to obtain HEK293T cell populations with a controlled number of polystyrene laser particles (LPs). By modifying the particle surface with poly(ethyleneimine) (PEI) or lipofectamine, we enhance LP-association to cells. We demonstrate that our sorting procedure yields viable cells showing unchanged proliferation rates. Manufacturer-dependent differences in particle-cell interactions were observed and investigated by scanning and transmission electron microscopy (SEM/TEM) and flow cytometry. Finally, we show that the same sorting approach enables the generation of multi-cellular spheroids with a defined ratio of LP-containing and LP-free cells. This work lays the foundation for larger tissue engineering studies with defined LP populations and control over LP-placement with respect to the cell.
items.authors: Koenig, M.; Plaskocinski, T. T.; Popczyk, A.; Titze, V. M.; Gaedke, F.; Germer, M.; Schumacher, A.-L.; Schmidt, A. M.; Schubert, M.; Gather, M. C.
items.title_zh: 利用商业流式细胞术系统富集微激光标记细胞
items.summary_zh: 基于低声波腔模式（WGM）的微激光器具有明亮且光谱窄的发射特性，适合用于高分辨率细胞标记、单细胞追踪和生物传感。在生物医学或组织工程中，控制细胞群体中激光粒子的数量至关重要。本文使用商业流式细胞术系统获取具有可控数量聚苯乙烯激光粒子（LPs）的HEK293T细胞群体。通过用聚乙烯亚胺（PEI）或脂质体转染试剂修饰粒子表面，增强了LP与细胞的结合。我们的分选程序获得的细胞具有良好的活性且增殖速率未发生变化。通过扫描和透射电子显微镜（SEM/TEM）及流式细胞术观察到制造商间粒子-细胞相互作用的差异。最后，我们展示了相同的分选方法能够生成具有特定LP含量和无LP细胞比例的多细胞球体。这项工作为具有明确LP群体和LP定位控制的大规模组织工程研究奠定了基础。

items.title: Engineered mRNA-packaging virus-like particles enable efficient and precise mitochondrial base editing in vitro and in vivo
items.abstract: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) base editors (mtBEs) are promising tools for studying and correcting pathogenic mtDNA mutations. However, the application of mtBEs is often hindered by substantial mtDNA-wide off-target editing that accumulates with prolonged mtBE expression resulting from plasmid DNA or viral delivery. To overcome this limitation, we developed mtBE-VLPs, a virus-like-particle (VLP) platform for transiently delivering mtBEs in vitro and in vivo with minimal off-target effects. While canonical protein-packaging VLPs yielded undetectable mtDNA base editing, engineered mRNA-packaging VLPs enabled efficient but transient mtBE cargo delivery. By iteratively engineering mRNA-packaging VLP compositions, we improved mtBE-VLP-mediated base editing efficiencies from less than 1% to greater than 50% across multiple target mtDNA loci in bulk populations of treated cultured cells. To further improve the packaging and delivery of certain mtBEs, we developed a strategy to selectively reduce mtBE cargo expression in VLP producer cells but not transduced cells, which increased VLP-mediated base editing efficiencies for certain mtBEs by 7.1-fold. Compared to plasmid DNA delivery in vitro, mtBE-VLPs exhibited equivalent on-target editing but 23- to 41-fold lower mtDNA-wide off-target editing, highlighting the improved editing specificity offered by transient mtBE delivery. mtBE-VLPs efficiently installed a pathogenic mtDNA mutation in mouse embryonic fibroblasts (88% efficiency) and corrected a pathogenic mtDNA mutation in a human patient-derived cell line (41% efficiency). Additionally, a single subretinal injection of mtBE-VLPs yielded 6-20% (average 12%) mtDNA base editing in the mouse retinal pigment epithelium with minimal mtDNA-wide off-target editing. These findings establish mRNA-packaging mtBE-VLPs as promising vehicles for efficient and precise mitochondrial base editing via transient mtBE delivery.
items.authors: Jang, H.; Rodrigues Menezes, C.; Palczewski, K.; Raguram, A.

items.title: Agentic campaign control for high-throughput de novo binder design
items.abstract: Progress in artificial intelligence has produced a rapidly growing ecosystem of methods for de novo protein design. With access to many specialized and often complementary tools, how does one use them effectively, especially with a finite compute budget? Here, we introduce Target adaptive Rescue-Explore-eXploit (T-REX), an agentic protein binder design framework that orchestrates multiple state-of-the-art protein generative models and structure evaluators. Over the course of a design campaign, T-REX leverages large language model (LLM) agents to reason over accumulating outcomes and decide whether to rescue promising candidates, explore alternative settings, or exploit productive routes, while a deterministic controller validates and schedules proposed actions. Across seven targets, we find that T-REX adaptively allocates its compute across methods in a target-dependent manner and achieves the highest throughput of structurally distinct hits compared to all baselines. These results suggest that adaptive orchestration can complement increasingly powerful protein design models, and we openly release T-REX to support compute-efficient binder design workflows.
items.authors: Jeon, M.; Song, J.; Kim, J.; Zhong, E. D.

items.title: Answering clinicians' questions over trial evidence tables with verifiable, feedback-driven language models
items.abstract: Systematic reviews condense clinical trials into evidence tables, yet clinicians can interrogate these tables only through database queries, and many questions concern attributes that the table does not record, such as a drug's target class or a harmonised endpoint. Here we introduce FD-SCoPE, a language-model framework that answers both kinds of question, exposes the query, the selected trials and the derivation rule behind every answer, and learns from expert corrections. On an oncology evidence table of 159 immune checkpoint inhibitor trial records, FD-SCoPE completed all 140 clinician-style tasks (alternatives, 90.7--97.9%). For questions needing derived attributes it retrieved 99.3% of relevant trial records at a positive predictive value of 89.8% and outperformed four alternative approaches (derived-value F1 77.7% versus 64.8--73.4%). Corrections on 299 questions, simulated from reference answers, raised F1 on 1,201 unseen questions from 77.9% to 84.9%. Language models coupled with executable queries, verified programs and expert feedback can give clinicians auditable access to trial evidence.
items.authors: Roy Choudhury, M.; Roy Chowdhury, S.; Sahoo, S.; Khan, M. A.; Khakwani, K. Z. R.; Sonbol, M. B.; Riaz, I.; Gupta, V.

items.title: A 4D GelMA-Cad/Gelatin Hydrogel for High-Resolution DMD Bioprinting of Vascularized Soft Tissue Models
items.abstract: Digital micromirror device (DMD)-based bioprinting enables high-resolution fabrication of hydrogel-based tissue constructs, but print fidelity and hydrogel mechanics are typically coupled through polymer concentration, light exposure, and crosslinking density. This creates a materials constraint for vascular bioprinting, where constructs must preserve microscale architecture during fabrication while supporting multicellular remodeling, lumen formation, and long-term tissue organization. To meet these requirements, we developed a 4D GelMA-Cad/gelatin hydrogel with time-dependent mechanics that maintains print fidelity while providing a soft, cell-permissive matrix. GelMA-Cad provides a covalently photocrosslinked, bioactive network containing an N-cadherin-mimetic peptide, while uncrosslinked gelatin serves as a transient matrix-modifying component that diffuses from the hydrogel after fabrication, producing further softening without bulk degradation of the GelMA-Cad network. We characterized hydrogel chemistry with NMR, quantified time-dependent changes in stiffness, visualized pore morphology with cryo-SEM, and evaluated the platform in retinal and pulmonary constructs. The 4D hydrogel supports 3D-patterned accuracy, cell viability, inner blood-retinal barrier vasculature, and vascularized lung-alveolar tissue models. Single-cell RNA-sequencing of the pulmonary vascular-alveolar model demonstrated compartment-specific transcriptional responses, including enrichment of lung capillary-associated endothelial features and AT1-like epithelial states. Overall, this platform decouples DMD print fidelity from post-print matrix mechanics for vascularized soft tissue bioprinting and tissue modeling.
items.authors: Wang, J.; McClain, C.; Krystofiak, E.; Marguerite, N.; Hoskins, W.; Sutphen, H.; Kropski, J. A.; David, H.; McCall, A. S.; O'Grady, B.

items.title: Pervasive Backdoor Vulnerabilities in Genomic Foundation Models
items.abstract: Genomic foundation models are revolutionizing biological research and biotechnology, yet their vulnerability to data poisoning remains poorly characterized. Here we show that backdoor attacks can be reliably implanted during fine-tuning across diverse model architectures, tasks and model scales by poisoning only a small fraction of training data with short DNA motifs, including triggers derived from transposon terminal inverted repeats (TIRs). Attack success rates are generally high across encoder-based and autoregressive models, while clean-task performance remains almost unchanged. Increasing model scale does not confer measurable resistance. To detect such threats, we develop a two-stage auditing framework that flags potentially poisoned sequences through localized single-nucleotide mutation sensitivity in model predictions, without prior knowledge of trigger sequences. These results identify downstream fine-tuning as an attack surface for genomic foundation models and motivate stronger data provenance, adversarial evaluation and post-training security auditing.
items.authors: Ni, S.; Wang, Q.; Wei, C.; Ni, X.; Li, S.; Zhao, Z.; Li, H.; Ji, R.; Xu, R.; Alinejad-Rokny, H.; Wang, T.; Yang, M.

items.title: PhyloZoo: a unified framework for phylogenetic network analysis in Python
items.abstract: Reticulate evolutionary processes (events in which lineages merge, such as hybridization, recombination, and horizontal gene transfer) are widespread across nature but cannot be represented by phylogenetic trees alone. Phylogenetic networks have therefore become an important modelling tool, yet existing software is typically tied to specific inference paradigms and provides limited support for working with multiple network representations in a unified and programmable environment. PhyloZoo is an open-source Python framework that lowers the barrier to developing practical, easy-to-use software for phylogenetic network analysis. It provides data structures and algorithms covering the main representations used in the field, together with dedicated visualization tools and robust I/O for all major phylogenetic file formats. A particular emphasis lies on semi-directed phylogenetic networks, which explicitly represent root uncertainty and have so far received limited support in existing software. By offering a shared, scalable foundation for developing interoperable tools and a combinatorial layer that supports computational proofs and theoretical exploration, PhyloZoo enables reproducible workflows for applied, methodological, and theoretical studies of reticulate evolution. Availability and implementation: PhyloZoo is implemented in Python and installable from PyPI, with source code, documentation, and examples available at https://github.com/nholtgrefe/phylozoo.
items.authors: Holtgrefe, N.

items.title: Extreme conservation and rare evolutionary deviations in mammalian NOTCH3 inform the interpretation of CADASIL pathogenicity
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: NOTCH3 is a highly conserved transmembrane receptor whose pathogenic variants cause CADASIL, a hereditary cerebral small vessel disease characterized by vascular smooth muscle cell degeneration and extracellular NOTCH3 accumulation. Most established CADASIL variants alter cysteine residues within the extracellular EGF like repeats, but the influence of residue position, disulfide connectivity, surrounding sequence, and domain context on NOTCH3 structure and pathogenicity remains incompletely understood. We used comparative mammalian analysis to identify rare changes within conserved NOTCH3 regions and evaluate their potential relevance to disease associated molecular mechanisms. Methods: NOTCH3 protein sequences from 113 mammalian species were ana-lysed using multiple sequence alignment together with complementary structural modelling, intrinsic disorder prediction, stability, aggregation propensity, solvent-accessibility, and molecular dynamics analyses. Results: NOTCH3 showed exceptional overall conservation, including all 204 extracellular cysteine positions across nearly all species examined. Three rare sequence configurations were identified: seven cysteine substitutions and one cysteine deletion in jaguar EGFr13,14,15; an NRR deletion in Brandt bat predicted to increase S2 cleavage-site accessibility; and an exon 16 associated X1 deletion affecting EGFr20,22, previously reported in a human CADASIL pedigree and also found in selected mammals.
