items.authors: Yuting Yang, Gang Mei, Nengxiong Xu, Yongshuang Zhang, Jianbing Peng

items.title: Structure-Driven Methodology: An Emerging Cross-Domain Paradigm
items.abstract: This article proposes and articulates structure-driven methodology as an emerging cross-domain paradigm. In contrast to the objective-driven paradigm that has dominated inverse-problem solving for over two centuries, structure-driven methodology advocates identifying and exploiting the intrinsic structure of a problem to construct the solution method directly, rather than approaching the solution through iterative search. Drawing on examples from the Liouville-variant Goldbach conjecture, the three-dimensional Kakeya conjecture, Noether's theorem, and the author's nearly four decades of geophysical inversion practice, the article illustrates the common logic of structure-driven thinking in number theory, pure mathematics, physics, and seismic imaging. The author also systematically proposes the Structure-Driven Inversion (SDI) paradigm, comprising Mathematical Structure-Driven Inversion (MSDI) and Physical Structure-Driven Inversion (PSDI). Structure-driven methodology does not negate objective-driven methodology but complements it: objective-driven is a general search strategy, whereas structure-driven is a custom direct strategy. The article concludes that the significance of this shift lies not only in efficiency gains but also in cognitive deepening---when facing complex problems, the first question is no longer ``how to solve the problem faster'' but ``what is the structure of the problem.''
items.authors: Shengchang Chen

items.title: Acceleration methods for the planar 3D ILSA hydraulic fracturing model
items.abstract: Planar 3D models of hydraulic fracturing provide a practical balance between models with restrictive geometric assumptions and fully 3D simulators, capturing fractures with arbitrary planar footprints at moderate computational cost. Nevertheless, applications such as treatment design optimization and mini-frac test interpretation require large ensembles of simulations, for which the cost of planar 3D models remains a significant bottleneck. This work presents acceleration strategies for the planar 3D Implicit Level Set Algorithm (ILSA) to reduce simulation runtime while preserving numerical accuracy. A unified planar 3D ILSA scheme that consolidates the nested loops of the elastohydrodynamic solver and the front tracking algorithm into a single iterative process is introduced. A matrix splitting approach is applied to the linearized elastohydrodynamic system, moving the dense part of the elasticity operator to the right-hand side and yielding a sparse system matrix that can be solved more efficiently. Anderson acceleration is incorporated into the solution of the elastohydrodynamic system to improve convergence. A predictor--corrector scheme is additionally examined in combination with these methods. Each technique is evaluated individually and in combination on both the reference and unified schemes across five benchmark cases. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the unified scheme alone delivers an average 2.3x speed-up, reaching 3.8x for the Sandglass case. The combined application of all techniques achieves an average 4.2x speed-up and up to 14.4x for the Sandglass case. The schemes are also assessed during fracture closure, where the matrix splitting and Anderson acceleration prove most effective, together reaching up to 3.4x.
items.authors: V. I. Shukalo (Lavrentyev Institute of Hydrodynamics SB RAS), A. V. Valov (Lavrentyev Institute of Hydrodynamics SB RAS), A. N. Baykin (Lavrentyev Institute of Hydrodynamics SB RAS)

items.title: Magnetoconvection in a spherical shell: Bridging the gap between weak and strong-field dynamo regimes
items.abstract: At moderate levels of convective driving, simulations of dynamos in spherical shells often separate into two broad dipolar regimes characterised either by their relative magnetic field strength (weak/strong) or by their dominant force balance. These regimes can tend smoothly from one to the other but can also be bistable, a phenomenon which occurs particularly at low magnetic diffusivity. Nonlinear simulations of the geodynamo cannot be performed at realistic parameters and hence it is important to ensure that the (strong-field) branch, appropriate for Earth's core, is tracked as a distinguished limit is established towards a suitable parameterisation from the simulations that we can perform. In order to understand the transition to strong-field dynamos, and better understand the mechanisms that occur in both branches, we report on a series of magnetoconvection simulations: models in which an external magnetic field modifies the dynamically-generated dynamo. Our primary input parameters are the magnetic diffusivity, imposed magnetic field strength, and the convective forcing; as these vary, we show how the morphology of the flow can change gradually, as modifications of an existing mode or continuous variations in force composition, and also abruptly, when onset modes become unstable to secondary instabilities and are replaced either by newly-dominant modes, a vacillating regime, or highly nonlinear configurations of the flow. The loss of equatorial symmetry is also investigated, as this typically coincides with the weak-to-strong transition, and we discuss why an anti-symmetric instability emerges inside the tangent cylinder along with its implications for the geodynamo.
items.authors: Luke J. Gostelow, Robert J. Teed

items.title: Directional Control of Droplet Motion via Geometric Gating
items.abstract: We explore new methods for inducing the movement of water droplets on elastomeric substrates, such as polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). Our approach builds upon the well-known phenomenon that water droplets move easily across these substrates when swelled with silicone oil. While designing shallow open channels and traps on a PDMS film offers a simple way to control a droplet's trajectory by tilting the substrate in two orthogonal directions, this method is poorly suited for manipulating multiple droplets simultaneously. To address this limitation, we introduce two new methods. The first method utilizes a piano-concave PDMS platform with a radius of curvature significantly larger than the size of the droplet and its translation distance. When the system's configuration is altered, this curved substrate consistently guides the droplet along a curved geodesic. The second method incorporates diode-like gates on the PDMS. These gates are created on either flat or piano-concave PDMS films by embedding thin, rigid plates into the elastomer prior to crosslinking, followed by swelling in silicone oil. This process generates sigmoidal steps that restrict droplet motion to a single direction. Finally, we demonstrate how combining these two strategies enables various forms of directed motion for both single and multiple droplets.
items.authors: Manoj K. Chaudhury, Vanessa Elias, Michelle Fruge

items.title: Photoresponsive Dynamics in HABI-Carbamate-Silsesquioxane Hybrid Polymer Networks with Tunable Thermomechanical Properties and Shape-Memory Behaviors
items.abstract: Photoresponsive polymer networks that reversibly modulate their mechanical properties under light irradiation are promising materials for advanced actuators and shape-memory systems. Herein, we report the synthesis of a new family of hexaarylbiimidazole (HABI)-carbamate-siloxane hybrid polymer networks containing methyl, phenyl, vinyl, acrylate, methacrylate, and isooctyl organotrialkoxysilane structures. The polymers were prepared through simultaneous urethane formation and siloxane condensation. We characterized all synthesized compounds by ATR-FTIR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, solid-state 13C NMR, 29Si NMR, LC-HRMS, UV−Vis spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, and dynamic mechanical analysis. Chemical characterization confirmed successful incorporation of HABI moieties, formation of carbamate linkages, and cross-linked siloxane networks. The organotrialkoxysilane substituents significantly influenced the thermal and mechanical properties of the polymer networks. Methacrylate- and acrylate-containing polymers showed the highest thermal stability (Td5% = 237 °C and 207 °C, respectively), while ceramic yields increased from 7% for the pristine network to 15%- 19% for the modified systems. Dynamic mechanical analysis revealed pronounced, reversible light-induced changes in storage and loss moduli arising from reversible HABI C−N bond cleavage and recombination, with the vinyl-containing polymer exhibiting the largest storage modulus variation (8 × 103 MPa). Several polymers also demonstrated reproducible light-assisted shape-memory behavior, with the acrylate-, methacrylate-, methyl-, and isooctyl-containing systems showing the most distinct responses. These HABI-carbamate-siloxane hybrid networks provide a versatile platform for developing mechanically tunable, photoresponsive materials for smart polymer and shape-memory applications.
items.authors: Mehdi Erfani Jazi, Ethan T. Chandler, Fatemeh Aghabozorgi, Buddhima Rupasinghe, Joseph C. Furgal

items.title: Integrating Ion Mobility–Resolved Tandem Mass Spectrometry and Microcrystal Electron Diffraction for Structural Elucidation
items.authors: Aleyna Lumsden, Amalia-Sofia Piticari, Amar Rai, Artemy Novokhrost, Timea Pálmai-Pallag, Yufeng Li

items.title: A robust multiwell workflow for quantitative and nontargeted chemical exposomics at cohort scale
items.abstract: Chemical exposomics enables comprehensive profiling of environmental substances and their metabolic perturbations, providing new opportunities to uncover environmental drivers of disease. To realize its full potential in human exposome initiatives, more reproducible high-throughput workflows are needed that combine sensitive quantitative targeted analysis with nontargeted molecular discovery in small serum volumes. We describe a 96-well phospholipid depletion workflow using 100 µL of serum and liquid chromatography – high-resolution mass spectrometry to quantify 247 priority pollutants, drugs and metabolites while confidently annotating hundreds of additional exogenous and endogenous molecules. In contrast to evaporation-to-dryness workflows, adding a small volume of dimethyl sulfoxide retained more analytes and improved recovery (99% median target recovery), with negligible effect on sensitivity (0.5 ng/mL median method limit of quantification), resulting in robust within-laboratory reproducibility across four operators over 1.5 years (18% median relative standard deviation). Application to 718 human serum samples confirmed scalability while maintaining reproducible quantitation and molecular discovery (761 annotated substances) at the cohort scale.
items.authors: Solveig Thiele, Bénilde Bonnefille, Sophia Harlid, Stefano Papazian, Jonathan W. Martin

items.title: DNA binders based on the integration of duocarmycins into minor groove-targeting polyamides have potent and selective anti-trypansosomal activity
items.abstract: Duocarmycins are attractive DNA alkylating agents due to their high potency; however, increasing their selectivity has always been a challenge. Here, we describe the integration of the duocarmycin subunits DSA and CI into minor groove-targeting polyamides, compounds that can ‘read’ DNA sequences. The synthesis of a CI analogue suitably substituted for solid phase synthesis using Fmoc-chemistry is described. The synthesis of the hybrid compounds is achieved using solid phase methods on chloro-trityl resin. The resulting hybrids display sequence-selective DNA alkylation, depending on the enantiomer and position of the duocarmycin unit as might be expected, except for the compounds with a central DSA alkylation subunit, which act more similarly to reversed analogues. The CI hybrids with a central unit are relatively unreactive with DNA and modelling studies suggest that the CI subunit is sub-optimally located for alkylation in these structures. Investigations against the parasite T. brucei, responsible for African trypanomiasis, highlight compounds with nanomolar potency and high selectivity (SI 300), showing that the integration of duocarmycins into the backbone of polyamides has promise for developing gene-targeting small molecule anti-parasitic agents.
items.authors: Zoë R. Goddard, Bethany R. Hood, Michael Brazzill, Deanne Hayward, Dietmar Steverding, Victoria Kamperi

items.title: Phase-Controlled Efficient Nitrate-to-Dinitrogen Electroreduction on an α-Co/NC@CNT Electrified Membrane Platform
items.abstract: Selective electrochemical conversion of nitrate (NO 3 - ) to dinitrogen (N 2 ) is attractive for nitrate remediation but remains challenging because competing hydrogenation pathways often yield reduced nitrogen products. Here, we develop a self-supported flexible electrified membrane (α-Co/NC@CNTFEM) by integrating phase-defined hexagonal close-packed (HCP) α-Co/nitrogen-doped carbon (NC) into a conductive carbon nanotube (CNT) framework. The resulting membrane combines a uniformly integrated catalytic phase with a thin, interconnected porous architecture suitable for flow-through electrochemical operation. At an initial nitrate concentration of 10 mg L -1 , α-Co/NC@CNT-FEM achieves 96.5% nitrate conversion, 81.5% N 2 Faradaic efficiency, and 97.9% N 2 selectivity, exceeding the corresponding mixed-phase Co NP /NC@CNT-FEM and bare CNT-FEM. The enhanced N 2 selectivity is associated with the coupled effects of the phase-defined α-Co, N-doped carbon matrix, and flow-through CNT microenvironment, which may favor N–N coupling while suppressing excessive hydrogenation. Moreover, our results also reveal that stable nitrate removal on this platform is maintained over 10 consecutive cycles. This work demonstrates crystal-phase engineering coupled with electrified membrane design as a materials strategy for selective nitrate-to-N 2 conversion.
items.authors: Jiantao Xu, Ruxin Han, Jifa Zhang, Dawei Li, Feihu Li

items.title: Mousanes: Convergent Synthesis and Diversification of Serially Spiro-Fused Cyclobutanes
items.abstract: Connecting cyclobutanes through successive spiro junctions offers a way to restrict the relative positions and orientations of functional groups along a saturated framework. Here we describe a convergent synthesis of mousanes, dispirodecane scaffolds comprising three cyclobutanes. A functionalized methylenecyclobutene is prepared on decagram scale by elimination of an iodo-bicyclo[1.1.1]pentanederived precursor. This 1,3-diene undergoes regioselective, triplet-sensitized [2+2] homodimerization to construct the central cyclobutane and both spiro junctions. Hydrolysis and stereoconvergent hydrogenation provide a bifunctional mousane on multigram scale, from which amino acid, diamine, diol and differentially functionalized derivatives are prepared. Calculations suggest that regioselectivity is established during the initial C–C bond-forming step and show that mousane stereochemistry controls terminal geometry. The exo,exo framework has dimensions comparable to short hydrocarbon linkers but displays a narrower calculated range of terminal-vector orientations. We illustrate the use of these building blocks through incorporation into drug analogues and a BRD4-targeting heterobifunctional ligand directed degrader.
items.authors: Manivel Pitchai, Sankar Ulaganathan, Nanjundaswamy K.C., Mohammad Javeed, Pavan Srinivas, Sourav Roy

items.title: Consecutive hydrodefluorination for the regioselective synthesis of partially fluorinated arenes
items.abstract: Fluorinated arenes are critically important motifs in drug discovery, often exhibiting superior bioactivity compared to their non-fluorinated counterparts. While advances in fluorination methods have improved access to monofluoroarenes, the synthesis of di- and trifluoroarenes remains challenging. Here, we present a powerful method for access to partially fluorinated arenes via consecutive hydrodefluorination of perfluoroarenes, executed in one ‘pot’. This method utilises hydridosilicates as the reducing species, which are formed in situ by the combination of phenylsilane and cesium carbonate in dimethylsulfoxide. These conditions avoid precious metal catalysts and exotic reagents, exhibiting exceptional regioselectivity and control over the degree of defluorination. Through an in-depth mechanistic study, we found that hydridosilicates can perform hydrodefluorination by two distinct mechanisms, one thermal and one photochemical. These mechanisms are complementary in substrate scope—together, they enable a method with notable generality.
items.authors: Yanxian Tan, Howard Toh, Chieh-Yu Chang, Phillip S. Grant

items.title: Hydrogen-Assisted Reduction of Metal Oxides: Reaction Mechanisms, Process Optimization, and AI/ML-Enabled Pathways for Sustainable Materials Processing
items.abstract: Hydrogen reduction of metal oxides has been identified as a promising approach for producing some engineering (metallic) materials, both through primary production and the reprocessing of waste materials. Such an approach offers a viable promise for the production of value-added materials in a sustainable manner. Unlike in other reduction processes, where obnoxious gases get 2 released as byproducts, hydrogen reduction, on the other hand, generate water vapor as the clean principal byproduct. Such an approach renders the overall mcheaping process inexpensive because of the use of metal oxides as the cheap feedstocks. However, the manufacturing process offers several challenges, upscaling being one of the major ones. In the present review, an attempt has been made to assess the overall reduction process in an integrated manner, which relates thermodynamic principles, reduction mechanisms, reactor-scale phenomena, and specific application requirements. The principles of thermodynamic constraints related to oxide reducibility are described in relation to the role of reduction temperature, gas compositions, and the gas-solid reaction mechanisms to determine rate-controlling processes, diffusion coefficients, and the role of catalysis for the production of metallic materials by primary manufacturing processes and environmental remediation. There is also the consideration of an enabling role of automation, modeling, and digital twin technologies. The manuscript describes practiced hydrogen reduction processes to produce some of the specific metals, such as iron, nickel, cobalt, and refractory metals, but also the need to improve hydrogen access, efficiency, scalability, and ensure catalyst longevity. Enhanced research in hydrogen, renewable power coupling, AI-assisted process control and reactor design are some of the aspects that have been observed to be the major enablers. The manuscript not only describes the status and future projections but also provides a roadmap for improving the status quo.
items.authors: Kunal Mondal, Rigoberto C. Advincula, Prabhat K. Tripathy, Nagaraj P. Shetti

items.title: When Philicity Fails: Mechanistic Control of Ambiphilic Metal–Superoxo Reactivity
items.abstract: A fundamental challenge in oxygen activation chemistry is understanding the factors that govern the switch between electrophilic and nucleophilic reactivity in metal–superoxo intermediates. Notably, only four ambiphilic metal–superoxo systems have been reported to date, yet the origins of their ambiphilic behavior remain poorly understood, limiting the rational design of catalysts with predictable and tunable reactivity. Here, we systematically investigate these four reported complexes, [(L 1 ) •+ Co II –O2 •⁻ ] – ( 1b ) (where L1 = (N • ( o -PhNC(O) i Pr) 2 ) 2– ) , [(L 2 )Mn III –O 2 •– ] ( 2b ) (where L 2 = BDP Br P = 2,6-bis((2-( S )-di(4-bromo)phenylhydroxylmethyl-1-pyrrolidinyl)methyl)pyridine) 2– ), [(L 3 )Fe III (O 2 •⁻ )] 2− ( 3b ) (where L 3 = TAML = Tetra Amido Macrocyclic Ligand) 4- and [(L 4 )Co III –O 2 •⁻ ] ( 4b ) (where L 4 = BDPP = 2,6-bis((2-(S)diphenylhydroxylmethyl-1-pyrrolidinyl)methyl)pyridine) 2– ) , using density functional theory to elucidate their O 2 activation and reactivity toward electrophilic and nucleophilic substrates. O 2 activation preferentially proceeds through inner-sphere pathways, in which electron transfer and M–O 2 bond formation occurs concomitantly, with ligand-to-O 2 electron transfer for 1a and metal-to-O 2 electron transfer for 2a – 4a . For PPA deformylation, coordinatively saturated complex 2b favor α-hydrogen atom abstraction, whereas the open, four-coordinate 1b preferentially undergoes nucleophilic addition. In contrast, oxygen-atom-transfer reactivity toward triphenylphosphine does not follow electrophilicity alone: despite the higher intrinsic electrophilicity of [(L 5 )Cu II –O 2 •– ] + (L 5 =TMPA = tris(2-pyridyl methyl)amine); ( 5b ), 1b exhibits a lower activation barrier (68.4 vs 81.4 kJ/mol) owing to stronger orbital interactions and reduced deformation requirements. Collectively, these results establish that metal–superoxo reactivity is governed by the interplay of coordination environment, philicity, orbital interactions, steric effects, and deformation energy. These insights provide a framework for rational catalyst design in which reactivity can be tuned by optimizing the complete electronic and structural reaction landscape rather than maximizing philicity alone.
items.authors: Chandrasekhar Nettem, Abitha Periyasamy, Manjeet Kumar, Gopalan Rajaraman

items.title: Photocatalytic performance of silver clusters on anatase TiO2 for bisphenol A degradation in water under solar light
items.abstract: The increasing occurrence of bisphenol A (BPA) in water sources raises significant environmental and health concerns, demanding efficient and sustainable remediation strategies. In this work, we investigate the photocatalytic degradation of BPA using silver metal clusters (Ag5) supported on anatase TiO2 under simulated solar irradiation. The deposition of Ag5 clusters significantly enhances visible-light absorption, promotes charge separation and improves photocatalytic performance, achieving an apparent rate constant (kobs) of 0.0142 min-1, corresponding to a ~43% improvement compared to bare TiO2. In addition, the Ag5@TiO2 catalyst exhibits higher photocatalytic activity, demonstrating the beneficial effect of Ag5 clusters incorporation. HPLC-MS analysis enabled the identification of intermediate degradation products. Compared to literature reports on modified TiO2-based photocatalysts, the present system demonstrates competitive performance even at significantly lower catalyst loadings. These results highlight the potential of Ag5@TiO2 photocatalysts as highly efficient alternatives for removing endocrine-disrupting compounds from water.
items.authors: María Moreno-Pérez, José Manuel Ageitos, Iria R. Arias, José Manuel Blanco Trillo, M. Arturo López-Quintela, Carlos Vázquez-Vázquez

items.title: A Stereochemical Blueprint for Thermoresponsive Polymers
items.abstract: Predicting polymer structure-property relationships is challenging due to the vast chemical expanse of polymer design space and the limited availability of high-quality datasets that effectively span the design space. Here, we present a physics-informed framework that integrates high-throughput molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with machine learning to predict the lower critical solution temperature (LCST) of stereochemically diverse poly(Nisopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM) systems using 5632 MD simulation trajectories, corresponding to a cumulative simulation time of 2816 µs. We use validated MD simulations to generate descriptors that capture local hydration and conformational environments, enabling the extraction of molecular features directly linked to thermoresponsive behaviour. The resulting model accurately reproduces subtle experimentally observed LCST variations arising from changes in tacticity, demonstrating that sequence derived features and simulation-derived hydration descriptors encode the molecular information required to resolve compositiondependent phase behaviour. Beyond LCST prediction, the framework provides mechanistic insight into the molecular origins of thermoresponsive behaviour of PNIPAM, revealing that meso and racemic dyads undergo distinct backbone rotational mediated collapse pathways, with meso dyads requiring backbone rotation through partially hydrated intermediates, whereas racemic dyads collapse within a fixed backbone rotational conformation through closure of the isopropyl-isopropyl distance. These findings establish a transferable simulation-machinelearning strategy for linking polymer structural information to macroscopic properties and accelerating the discovery of functional polymer materials.
items.authors: Rangika Munaweera, Martin Stroet, Megan L. O'Mara

items.title: Lookahead Bayesian Optimisation for Molecular Growth in Self-Driving Laboratories
items.abstract: Self-driving laboratories can autonomously execute iterative design-make-test-analyse cycles, but molecular optimisation presents a distinctive challenge: selecting which compound to elaborate determines not only the next experiment, but also the chemical space accessible in subsequent rounds. Conventional molecular Bayesian optimisation typically evaluates compounds without considering how their selection changes what can subsequently be synthesised. Here, we introduce Lookahead Bayesian Optimisation (LABO), which instead values candidate molecules according to the predicted value of the synthetically accessible chemical space they unlock, enabling optimisation to account for future experimental opportunities. We evaluate LABO in simulated five-round molecular optimisation campaigns across 30 lead-like starting compounds and five kinase targets. LABO outperformed established molecular optimisation strategies from the literature across all 30 optimisation landscapes, as well as random, greedy and Bayesian optimisation controls. LABO was shown to improve ligand-lipophilicity efficiency by 1.25 units over random selection, equivalent to approximately 18-fold greater potency at equal lipophilicity, and by 0.34 units (2.2-fold) over greedy elaboration. These results demonstrate a general principle for autonomous molecular optimisation: under synthetic constraints, the value of a molecule depends not only on its predicted properties, but on the future experiments that selecting it makes possible. By explicitly incorporating this future experimental value into molecular selection, LABO provides a framework for planning successive rounds of molecular growth in self-driving laboratories.
items.authors: Connor J. Taylor

items.title: Nucleus-Independent Chemical Shifts in disordered nanoporous carbons are governed by the long-range magnetic response of the carbon framework
items.abstract: Nanoporous carbons are widely used in energy storage, gas storage, and separation technologies due to their high surface area, porosity, and electrical conductivity. Understanding atomic-scale structure is critical for interpreting performance, yet disorder greatly complicates characterization. NMR chemical shifts of adsorbed molecules have emerged as a probe of structural disorder, but how nucleus-independent chemical shifts (NICS) relate to structure in realistic, disordered carbons remains poorly understood. Here, we generate realistic nanoporous carbon structures using molecular dynamics simulations and compute pore-averaged NICS using density functional theory, reproducing experimentally observed negative values across commercial nanoporous carbons. We find a moderate correlation between sp 2 domain area and NICS, indicating that domain size alone is a poor predictor of the observed shifts, while NICS value also weakly correlate with heteroatom content and 6-membered ring fraction. Instead, decomposing local shielding from non-local contributions shows that the framework's bulk magnetic susceptibility, which implicitly encodes domain size, packing arrangement and defects, dominates the pore-averaged response. These results reframe NICS as a reporter of the framework's collective magnetic susceptibility, rather a local probe of isolated aromatic environments. This position NMR as a quantitative tool for characterizing functional disorder in nanoporous carbons and will help establish a link between framework architecture and performance.
items.authors: Thomas Kress, Xinyu Liu, Alexander C. Forse

items.title: Fusion-Number-Dependent Emergence of 16π-Electron Antiaromatic Circuits in Thienocyclopenta-Fused Pyrenes
items.abstract: Antiaromatic 4nπ-electron circuits provide a powerful strategy for narrowing the HOMO–LUMO gaps of π-conjugated molecules, yet their contribution is often attenuated or obscured in stable polycyclic frameworks by competing local aromatic stabilization. Here we report a systematic series of thienocyclopenta-fused pyrenes containing one ( 1TP ), two ( trans -2TP and cis -2TP ), or four ( 4TP ) fused thienocyclopentadiene units, designed to evaluate the stepwise contributions of embedded 16π-electron circuits. The molecules were synthesized through Suzuki–Miyaura coupling followed by palladium-mediated annulation. Notably, 4TP was isolated as an air- and ambient-light-stable green solid, and its structure was confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Comparative 1 H NMR analysis revealed a progressive upfield shift of diagnostic protons upon increasing the number of fused thienocyclopentadiene units, indicating the emergence and amplification of a paratropic ring-current effect. Theoretical calculations supported the emergence and strengthening of 16π-electron antiaromatic contributions in the two 2TP isomers and 4TP . Frontierorbital calculations and cyclic voltammetry further showed that the LUMO level is substantially stabilized whereas the HOMO level remains nearly unchanged, resulting in a systematic decrease in the HOMO–LUMO gaps. These results establish thienocyclopenta fusion as an effective molecular design strategy for controlling the antiaromatic contribution of 16π-electron circuits within a stable carbon-rich π-framework.
items.authors: Kenji Tsukamoto, Koji Takagi, Yasutomo Segawa

items.title: Assessing the state of the art in ADMET prediction: Lessons from the OpenADMET-ExpansionRx community blind challenge
items.abstract: Computational blind challenges are essential for advancing drug discovery, especially in research areas with limited public data, such as absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, toxicity (ADMET) prediction. In this paper, we present the results of our latest community blind challenge, organized in collaboration with Expansion Therapeutics (ExpansionRx). Participants were tasked with predicting nine distinct ADMET endpoints routinely evaluated during lead optimization of compounds in drug discovery programs. Following unprecedented engagement from the global community, this challenge provided valuable insights into the state of the art in machine learning for ADMET modeling. Evaluating submissions against a realistic, challenging dataset from active ExpansionRx drug discovery programs revealed that message-passing neural networks and chemical foundation models dominated among the top performers. Furthermore, the results highlighted the power of proprietary industry datasets and a critical need to optimize predictive workflows for different endpoints independently via multitasking and task-affinity grouping. We also demonstrate how hosting our open-source blind challenge infrastructure on a flexible platform like Hugging Face was pivotal for driving community engagement and visibility. Ultimately, blind challenges supported by robust infrastructure, widespread dissemination, and rigorous post-challenge analysis are fundamental to maximizing the utility of public data releases. We anticipate that these community benchmarks will continue to drive the advancement of ADMET models, enabling their deployment in both early- and late-stage drug discovery.
items.authors: Maria A. Castellanos, Hugo MacDermott-Opeskin, Jon Ainsley, Jonathan A. Swain, Sean Colby, Devany West

items.title: Mathematical Modeling of Coupled Electronic and Ionic Transport Mechanics in Flow-Electrode Capacitive Deionization
items.abstract: Flow Capacitive Deionization (FCDI) is an electrochemical ion removal technology well-suited for continuous desalination of brackish waters, as well as ion-specific removal. Despite over a decade of research into FCDI, few researchers have probed the transient and spatially dependent mechanisms of ion transport and electro-adsorption within flow electrodes. In this study, transport equations describing the advection of overpotential along with the flowing electrode are coupled with the Nernst-Planck equations governing ion transport within the ion exchange membranes, water channel, and slurry electrolyte. The effect of flow velocity on electrical potential profiles and active regions of capacitive electro-adsorption are illustrated using 2-dimensional Finite Element Analysis (FEA) simulations. The model is then validated against a representative experimental cell using experimentally determined slurry properties and membrane properties as model inputs. The model shows general agreement with experimental data despite a high variability in experimental results. Finally, an empirical correlation for slurry conductivity, capacitance, and velocity, is fitted to non-dimensionalized simulation results, yielding power model correlations analogous to the Nusselt number and Peclet numbers in conductive heat transfer, Nu c ∝Pe c 0.258±0.002 . The result is a useful tool for predicting FCDI cell performance based on material inputs and operating parameters. This model serves as valuable groundwork for the expansion of FCDI modeling capabilities and subsequent optimization of operational parameters and cell geometries.
items.authors: Garrett Pohlman, Floria Li, Emna Aidi, Bilen Akuzum, Ertan Agar, Lukas Hackl

items.title: Harnessing π-d magnetic interactions in Co porphyrins by metal-ligand coordination
items.abstract: π-Multiradicalic compounds fabricated by on-surface synthesis have emerged as a powerful platform to interrogate spin interactions at the atomic scale. However, the introduction and role of unpaired d-electrons on such systems, and the study of π-d electronic interactions, are still incipient. In this context, a crucial point is the tunability of the inherent magnetic properties of such π-d architectures by incorporation of peripheral metal-organic coordination, which at the same time allows creating self-assembled architectures. Herein, to this aim we exploit an ex-professo synthesized Zn-porphyrin (1) equipped with two carbonitrile-dimethyl-phenyl moieties at its trans-meso positions, which forms π-extended metallo-organic nanostructures featuring unpaired π-electrons through cyclodehydrogenation and concomitant carbonitrile-gold coordination. Transmetallation of such Zn-based nanoarchitectures with Co atoms gave rise to the several Co-based porphyrin multiradicalic species featuring both unpaired π and d electrons, including porphyrin monomers (CoPor M) and dimers (Co-Por D) as well as one-dimensional porphyrin nanochains (1D CoPor NC) and nanotapes (1D CoPor NT). Scanning probe spectroscopy combined with theoretical calculations reveal that the carbonitrile-gold coordination environment dramatically alters the magnetic structure of the cobalt center as compared to analogue porphyrin species lacking the CN group. On the one hand, in both CoPor M and 1D CoPor NC the cobalt atom presents a S=3/2 ground state versus the S=1/2 case for Co porphyrins analogues lacking the nitrile moiety. Additionally, no Kondo interactions are detected at the metal center, as a consequence of a diminished magnetic interaction of CoPor M and 1D CoPor NC with the Au(111) substrate. On the other hand, CoPor D presents two radical electrons distributed between the cobalt atoms and the carbon π-system which interact ferromagnetically yielding a S=1 ground state. Our findings demonstrate how metal-ligand coordination can be used to harness the magnetic interactions within surface-supported multiradicalic molecular systems.
items.authors: María Tenorio, Lenka Cerna, Marco Lozano, Ana Barragán, Miguel Martínez García, Aurelio Gallardo

items.title: A field-deployable method for measuring picomolar mercury levels in natural waters
items.abstract: Measurements of mercury (Hg) at sub- to picomolar concentrations in natural waters often rely on cold vapor atomic fluorescence spectrometry (CVAFS), which provides the sensitivity required for trace detection. However, CVAFS instruments are not well suited for routine field deployment and require compressed high-purity argon or helium gas to operate, limiting their use in remote regions and locations without established analytical infrastructure. Cold-vapor atomic absorption spectrometry (CVAAS) offers a robust alternative but generally lacks the sensitivity required for low-level natural waters. Here, we optimized and tested the Nippon Instruments EMP Gold+, a purge-and-trap preconcentration system coupled to a portable CVAAS detector, to address this analytical challenge. We developed protocols for total Hg (THg) and dissolved gaseous Hg (DGM) and evaluated their performance in seawater during field deployments in Monterey Bay, California, USA and the Gulf of Guinea, Ghana. The optimized methods achieved detection limits of 0.97 pM for THg and 0.25 pM for DGM. THg measured in the Gulf of Guinea agreed closely with laboratory CVAFS measurements (R 2 = 0.953, slope = 1.11), with field matrix-spike recoveries of 90.6-96.2%. In Monterey Bay, portable DGM measurements reproduced the vertical structure observed independently for dimethylmercury using gas chromatography coupled to CVAFS. We demonstrate that this new approach can support direct measurements in regions where compressed gases and specialized analytical infrastructure are unavailable and provide rapid screening to guide subsequent sampling for more detailed Hg speciation.
items.authors: Roland P. Ovbiebo, Johannes West, Abril Hernandez, Hannah M. Adams, Ziheng Kuang, Gabriella A. Yeboah

items.title: Solving density-of-states occupation in disordered systems using neural networks
items.abstract: Describing density-of-states occupation with high precision in disordered systems is crucial for modeling charge transport and understanding doping mechanisms or interfacial energy-level alignment. Beyond fundamental insight from a mechanistic understanding of these physical phenomena, accurate modeling is pivotal for optimizing technological applications in optoelectronic and thermoelectric devices. However, the required calculations are computationally demanding and inherently complex, preventing systematic computational-experimental approaches. Here, we leverage neural networks to perform these calculations precisely and efficiently. We first demonstrate this approach for the Fermi-Dirac occupation of Gaussian densities of states, achieving accelerations of up to three orders of magnitude, a substantial advantage for advanced modeling workflows that require repeated evaluation of the underlying integrals. We then introduce a neural network for doped molecular materials, such as organic semiconductors, that directly predicts doping levels and Fermi level shifts, circumventing conventional recursive schemes and accelerating computations by nearly five orders of magnitude.
items.authors: Melissa Berteau-Rainville, Emanuele Orgiu, Ingo Salzmann

items.title: Glycine specifically labelled proteins to enhance solution NMR of methylene groups
items.abstract: Specific isotopic labelling of proteins has greatly advanced biomolecular NMR. Protein domains, individual residues or certain chemical groups with specific patterns of isotopes can be incorporated to optimize the use of NMR pulse schemes. Here, we describe a novel cell-free protein expression protocol that allows specific isotopic labelling of glycine residues, whilst all other amino acids are independently labelled. This technique enables us to prevent amino acid scrambling and cross-protonation from the solvent resulting in high labelling selectivity of glycine residues as attested by quantification of 15N amide scrambling and residual Ca protonation. We then highlight the potential applications of these samples in the field of biomolecular NMR. We produced a 1 H, 13 C glycine specifically labelled sample of a subunit of the heavy metal ATPase HMA8, in a completely perdeuterated 2 H background and demonstrate how the CH 2 -TROSY experiment recorded on such a sample improves the spectral quality of glycine residues.
items.authors: Rachel Lenoir Capello, Lionel Imbert, Jérôme Boisbouvier, Emeric Miclet

items.title: Surface hydroxyls act as key intermediates in the selective oxidative dehydrogenation of 2-propanol on Co3O4
items.abstract: Transition-metal oxides typically catalyze aerobic oxidation reactions with high activity even at low temperatures, but rarely with high selectivity. Owing to the complexity of competing surface processes on such catalysts, the rational design of selective low-temperature catalysts still requires a deeper mechanistic understanding of the active surface and reaction intermediates. In this work, we combine operando modulation-excitation infrared spectroscopy with density functional theory and molecular dynamics to mechanistically investigate 2-propanol oxidation over Co3O4 with a focus on surface hydroxyls, acting as hydrogen acceptors during alcohol adsorption. We identify two chemically distinct hydroxyl populations: linear hydroxyls, which actively participate in acetone formation and can be considered part of the active surface ensemble, and bridged hydroxyls, which behave largely as spectators. Together, these results provide a molecular-level mechanistic picture of alcohol oxidation on Co3O4 and establish the dynamic role of surface hydroxyl species as active players in heterogeneous oxidation catalysis.
items.authors: Pierfrancesco Ticali, Stephane Kenmoe, Hamidreza Hajiyani, Amir Omranpour, Nicolas Cosanne, Hauke Scheele

items.title: Hybrid Organosilicon Polymers Integrating Latent Si–Si Chromophores and Orthogonal Si–O–C Reactivity
items.authors: Bercis Pektas, Cuong Minh Quoc Le, Kenshiro Hitoshio, Hideki Yorimitsu, Jun Shimokawa, Hatice Mutlu

items.title: Deoxygenative Dialkylation of Vinylic Epoxides to Chiral Alkanes by Double SN2’
items.abstract: Chiral alkanes bearing two contiguous tertiary all-carbon stereocentres are important motifs in bioactive molecules, natural products and functional compounds, yet their stereocontrolled synthesis remains challenging. Here we report their modular preparation through the formal deoxygenative dialkylation of enantioenriched vinyl epoxides. Two consecutive organocopper-mediated S N 2′ substitutions enable stereospecific transfer of the starting stereochemical information followed by diastereoselective installation of the adjacent stereocentre. The sequence can be performed in one pot, providing densely substituted hydrocarbon frameworks with high regio- and stereocontrol. The method accommodates diverse, including sterically demanding, alkyl substituents, extends to cyclic substrates, and leaves a terminal alkene for downstream diversification. Vinyl epoxides thus provide a stereochemically encoded platform for straightforward access to complex chiral alkanes.
items.authors: Nicolò Rossi, Gwilherm Evano

items.title: From Rotor to Motor: Dissecting Design Principles for Light-Driven Directional Motion
items.abstract: Research on molecular motors continues to expand as increasing attention is devoted to dynamic and out-of-equilibrium chemical systems. Among the different classes of artificial molecular machines, light-driven motors are the most extensively present, yet the fundamental principles governing their directional motion remain difficult to disentangle, particularly for non-specialists. This work applies these concepts in a tutorial setting by gradually implementing molecular features to a base scaffold that turns it from a bistable system into an experimentally observable light-driven molecular motor. In doing so, it demonstrates how directional bias emerges as soon as relaxation of a high-energy state is coupled to a mechanical movement (a power stroke), while the motor performance can be addressed through modification of the underlying energy landscape. In addition, we show a practical workflow for benchmarking new motor candidates along with the experimental determination of their kinetic and thermodynamic parameters. To complement this study, we provide procedures for undergraduate students to synthesize and operate a molecular motor in practical courses.
items.authors: Nils C. Jansen, Romain Jamagne, Johannes Wega, Ludmilla Sturm, Aya Lebrazi, Marion Pupier

items.title: Pore-network homogeneity for mechanically reliable powder-compacted solid-electrolyte separators
items.abstract: All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) with alloy anodes require solid-electrolyte (SE) separators that sustain ion transport while accommodating repeated electrode-derived mechanical loads. However, the mechanical state of powder-compacted separators is commonly inferred from bulk porosity, averaged mechanical properties, or cell-level stack pressure changes, obscuring spatially heterogeneous local responses. Here, we show that pore-network homogeneity is a key determinant of the mechanical reliability of sulfide solid-electrolyte separators by governing local mechanical heterogeneity and stress localization. FIB-SEM tomography and spatially resolved nanoindentation reveal that a highly densified separator with a broad particle-size distribution (PSD) retains clustered pore-rich and mechanically compliant regions, whereas a narrower-PSD separator exhibits a more homogeneous pore network and local mechanical response. Despite comparable cell-level pressure evolution, the two separators show markedly different cycling stability. Post-cycling microscopy reveals cracking and interfacial delamination in the heterogeneous separator, while microstructure-resolved simulations reveal stronger local stress amplification consistent with these observations. Controlled digital structures with identical D50 and porosity further isolate PSD-dependent changes in pore architecture and stress distribution. These findings establish pore-network homogeneity as a key design criterion for mechanically reliable solid-electrolyte separators beyond ionic conductivity and bulk densification.
items.authors: Hyeok-Rae Cho, Hyeong-Jong Kim, Jae-Seung Kim, Beom Jin Park, Youngkyung Kim, Daeyeon Lee

items.title: Polymorph Influence on Sequential Anion Exchange Doping and Charge Transport in Poly(didodecyl-quaterthiophene) (PQT) for Organic Thermoelectrics
items.authors: Jie-Hao Chen, Naisong Shan, Yunhao Zhao, Alexander Filatov, Sihong Wang, Shrayesh Patel

items.title: Transition-State Steric Fields Capture Geometric Signatures Associated with Electronic Perturbations in Asymmetric Catalysis
items.abstract: In data analysis of molecular catalysis, molecular shape can be represented by voxel descriptors generated by mapping molecular structures onto a three-dimensional grid according to atomic van der Waals radii. Such voxel representations of molecular shape can be treated as steric molecular fields and are generally used as steric descriptors. However, because electronic perturbations can lead to systematic changes in molecular geometry, steric fields constructed from transition-state (TS) structures may also capture geometric signatures. We therefore examined whether steric fields derived from TS geometries can capture such structural changes associated with electronic perturbations in asymmetric catalysis. Using DFT-calculated TS structures from three asymmetric Michael addition systems, we generated two voxel-based molecular-field representations, steric fields and NPA-charge fields, for the major and minor TS pathways and used them to construct regression models with calculated enantioselectivity (ΔΔ G ‡ ) as the target variable. The resulting steric- and NPA-charge field models showed similar pathway-dependent trends in cross-validated coefficients of determination (q 2 ). The NPA-charge fields revealed distinct charge responses across the three reaction systems, and the associated changes in TS geometry were captured by the steric fields. These results indicate that TS-derived steric fields can encode not only molecular shape but also the geometric changes associated with electronic perturbations, providing simple and interpretable descriptors for data analysis in asymmetric catalysis.
items.authors: Shigeru Yamaguchi

items.title: Plasmonic Coupling Within Atomically Precise Nanocluster Dimers for Engineering Hot-Carrier Generation and Molecular Activation
items.abstract: Activating the exceptionally strong N≡N remains a fundamental challenge due to the chemical inertness of molecular nitrogen (N2). Plasmonic nanoclusters offer a promising approach by generating localized electromagnetic fields and energetic hot carriers that can drive bond activation at ambient conditions. Here, we combine real-time time-dependent density functional theory with Ehrenfest molecular dynamics to reveal how plasmonic coupling between tetrahedral Ag20 nanoclusters governs N2 activation and dissociation. Systematic variation of the intercluster separation shows that a 6 Å nanogap maximizes near-field enhancement and hot-electron transfer to the adsorbed N2, accompanied by N-N activation. Consequently, N2 dissociation is achieved at incident field strengths as low as 0.5 VÅ–1, whereas larger-gap dimers exhibit substantially lower activity. Similarly, isolated N2 remains intact under comparable conditions. These findings establish nanogap engineering as an effective strategy for optimizing plasmon-driven N2 activation and provide design principles for developing efficient plasmonic catalysts.
items.authors: Khushboo Bhardwaj, Samir Kumar Nayak, Pramod K. Verma, Sharma S. R. K. C. Yamijala

items.title: Carboxyl–Group Removal and Return: Mechanistic and Strategic Advances in Decarboxylation–Carboxylation
items.abstract: Carboxylic acids are ubiquitous functionalities and indispensable synthetic linchpins in organic chemistry. In recent years, strategies involving the removal, exchange, or recycling of the carboxyl group, particularly decarboxylation and carboxylation have gained remarkable momentum, partly driven by the imperative to valorize carbon dioxide generated in chemical transformations. Beyond simple CO2 extrusion, tandem decarboxylation–carboxylation and related cyclic processes have emerged as powerful yet underexplored approaches for constructing carboxylic acids in a single operation. This review highlights recent advances (2000–2026) in decarboxylation–re-carboxylation chemistry, with an emphasis on mechanistic understanding, reactive intermediates, and the strategic use of CO2 as a transient functional handle. We introduce a unified conceptual framework that classifies carboxyl–group transfer based on the identity of the carbon shuttle, the timing and mode of carboxyl reintroduction, and the nature of reactive intermediates. Subsequent sections discuss three major mechanistic archetypes: CO2–cycling decarboxylation–re-carboxylation, ester–cycling decarboxylation–re-esterification, and non-in situ carboxyl transfer using exogenous CO2 or alternative carboxyl sources. By delineating key developments and conceptual trends, we aim to inspire further innovation in exploiting carboxyl–group recycling as a platform for sustainable molecular synthesis.
items.authors: Yujuan Xie, Liliang Huang, Huangdi Feng, Erik V. Van der Eycken

items.title: DeMiR: Density-Matrix-Informed Representations for Molecular Property Prediction
items.abstract: The Hohenberg–Kohn theorem, which states that all physical quantities in the ground state are functionals of the electron density, suggests that much of a molecule's behavior is encoded in its electronic structure. This study proposes DeMiR, a model that treats electron density matrix prediction as a pretraining task. DeMiR reconstructs cc-pVDZ/B3LYP density matrices for molecules ranging in size from QM9-scale molecules to drug-like molecules with up to 146 atoms, achieving median NMAE values of 1.0% and 2.16%, respectively. At the atomic level, the model's embeddings contain electronic structure information: per-atom electronic observables are predicted with an R² of 0.94 by a linear probe, whereas Uni-Mol reaches 0.84 and a randomly initialized model of the same architecture only 0.63. The embeddings also remove 44.9% of the residual error left by a geometry-based descriptor, showing that this information is not linearly accessible from an explicit geometric descriptor. At the molecular level, transfer depends on the label type. Where electronic structure directly determines the property, transfer holds: on an external experimental pKa test set, fine-tuned DeMiR achieves an MAE of 1.143, significantly outperforming a randomly initialized control with the same architecture and training budget (1.397), and performing on par with or better than chemical foundation models pretrained on far larger datasets. In contrast, for labels such as pIC50 and ADMET, DeMiR shows no consistent advantage over existing general-purpose foundation models, as two-dimensional substructures and physicochemical descriptors have already saturated predictive performance. This study presents the scope within which a connection between electron density prediction capability and molecular property prediction capability holds, along with its boundaries.
items.authors: Donghyeon Kim, Dongsup Kim

items.title: Fourteen-Membered Macrocyclic Copper Complex for Highly Selective Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
items.abstract: The selective electrochemical reduction of nitrate (NO3−) to ammonia (NH3) represents a promising route for sustainable NH3 production. However, achieving high NH3 selectivity remains challenging due to competing reactions. Additionally, many reported catalysts rely on noble metals and often require relatively elevated catalyst loadings to achieve high apparent activity, while most systems operate only at relatively low current densities. Herein, a fourteen-membered macrocyclic copper complex supported on Ketjenblack (Cu-14MR/KB) is reported as a cathode catalyst for the highly selective electrochemical reduction of NO3− to NH3. With a low Cu loading of 1.34 μmol cm−2, Cu-14MR/KB delivered a high Faraday efficiency for NH3 synthesis of up to 94.8% at a current density of −26.3 mA cm−2 and maintained high NH3 selectivity over a wide current density range from −26.3 to −150 mA cm−2. Notably, at −150 mA cm−2, Cu-14MR/KB achieved an NH3 yield rate of 604 μmol cm−2 h−1 with an NH3 Faraday efficiency of 86.4%. Furthermore, a more contracted Cu–N4 coordination environment was revealed in Cu-14MR than in CuPc, with a shorter Cu–N bond distance, suggesting relatively stronger Cu–N interactions. This work provides an efficient strategy for high-performance NO3− electroreduction using a low-loading and non-noblemetal catalyst.
items.authors: Yuantao Yang, Ryotaro Iwata, Shoji Iguchi, Ritsu Hibino, Koyata Nishiyama, Makoto Moriya

items.title: A quantitative roadmap from catalyst benchmarks to commercial hybrid electrolysis
items.abstract: Hybrid water electrolysis replaces the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction with the oxidation of an organic substrate, producing hydrogen alongside another value-added chemical. In its most efficient form, the electrochemical oxidative dehydrogenation (EOD) of aldehydes, hydrogen evolves at both electrodes with specific electricity consumption down to 4 kWh kg−1 totalH2 , tenfold lower than conventional water electrolysis. Yet whether such efficiency gains translate into commercial viability has never been tested, as the field lacks standardized performance metrics, limiting catalyst comparability and industrial viability assessment. We propose three performance metrics: Anodic Hydrogen Productivity (AHP), Specific Electricity Consumption (SEC), and Deactivation Rate (DR), and benchmark all reported EOD systems as a case study. A techno-economic analysis links these metrics to net present value and reveals a roadmap to commercial viability: (i) Feedstock selection is the primary economic determinant; (ii) Catalyst stability is the foremost bottleneck, with DRs exceeding tolerable values by three orders of magnitude; (iii) Current density is a linear lever on economics; (iv) Energy efficiency, the property most intensively optimized by the field, matters least, contributing under 1% of net present value for high-value products. This offers quantitative benchmarks for catalyst and process development toward commercially viable EOD. Because the metrics depend only on measurable cell performance, benchmarks and roadmap transfer directly to other hybrid electrolysis concepts.
items.authors: Katharina M. Ebeling, J. Raphael Seidenberg, Benni Zou, Dominik Bongartz, Alexander Mitsos, Regina Palkovits

items.title: Energy ordering of singlet and triplet excitedstates in s-indacene, Pentalene,Cyclobutadiene derivatives in singlet fission : A model exact and density matrixrenormalization group study
items.authors: Ramen Patra, Mousumi Das

items.title: Minimum Knowledge Collaboration enables joint materials development through protected optimization
items.abstract: Materials companies must jointly develop products that meet competing requirements while keeping their formulations, processes and models private. Sample exchange alone can leave their searches poorly coordinated. We introduce Minimum Knowledge Collaboration (MKC), which connects private Bayesian optimizers through bounded candidate descriptions and company-specific search directions. Mathematical analysis links representation error, feasible private responses and information-limited search. In 256 controlled synthetic programs, all methods pursued the same reachable product target, defined as 100%. After 64 complete-product tests, MKC reached 92.4%, the information-rich reference 93.8%, and reusable better, neutral or worse feedback 6.0%. By 2,048 tests, ternary feedback reached MKC's result in 30 of 32 simplest bilateral programs; attainment across all 1,024-candidate programs was 12.5%. A cross-study scenario calculation gave a 0.0063% complete-state reconstruction index. This assumption-based design screen complements the measured reconstruction results. MKC demonstrates coordinated product development with bounded disclosure and supports industrial evaluation.
items.authors: Yakov Kutsovsky

items.title: Mechanochemical Activation of Strontium for the Selective Cross-Coupling of Chlorosilanes
items.abstract: Silicon-containing compounds are important in both academic and industrial settings, and the reductive coupling of chlorosilanes is a widely used approach for the formation of Si–Si bonds. However, despite its long history, this strategy for the formation of Si–Si bonds has remained largely limited to homocoupling, while a general synthetic method for selective heterocoupling has yet to be established. Previous strategies have relied on the stepwise generation of silicon nucleophiles or electrochemical methods. Here, we demonstrate that mechanochemical activation of strontium metal by ball milling enables the one-pot, cross-selective coupling of a broad range of chlorosilane pairs. Notably, after screening group 1 and group 2 metals, strontium was found to exhibit higher reactivity under mechanochemical conditions than commonly used metal reductants such as lithium and sodium. Importantly, no reaction occurs when strontium is employed under conventional solution conditions, highlighting the crucial role that mechanical activation plays in the reaction. Finally, this method is also applicable to the cross-coupling of chlorosilanes with chlorogermanes, thus establishing a practical and operationally simple protocol for the formation of E–E (E = Si, Ge) bonds.
items.authors: Hyehwang Kim, Koji Kubota, Hajime Ito

items.title: Protein Language Model-Boosted Prediction of Isoelectric Point
items.abstract: pH plays a key role in many biological processes. When the solution pH equals the isoelectric point (pI) of a protein, the protein carries zero net charge, which minimizes its solubility and thus promotes aggregation. Here we present ESMpI, a sequence-based protein pI predictor that combines optimized pKa values of seven ionizable residue types and two terminals with embeddings from a pre-trained protein language model. Benchmarked against experimental protein pI values, ESMpI outperforms other state-of-the-art methods, including structure-based approaches that derive the pI of a protein from residue-specific pKa calculations. Finally, ESMpI requires only sequence information, making it well suited for high-throughput proteomescale analyses and protein engineering.
items.authors: Fangfang Luo, Xiangxiang Lu, Zhitao Cai, Hongyu Lin, Yandong Huang

items.title: d10 Coinage Metal Organic Chalcogenolates: Tuning Dimensionality and Properties through Phenylthiolate Functionalization
items.abstract: Metal–Organic Chalcogenolates (MOCs) based on d 10 coinage metals constitute a versatile class of coordination polymers combining anisotropic structures with diverse functional properties. In this review, we examine a series of 23 Cu(I), Ag(I), and Au(I)-based MOCs obtained from eight functionalized thiophenolate ligands. The systematic comparison of these compounds highlights how the metal identity, ligand functionalization, steric hindrance, and secondary interactions govern the coordination modes and, most importantly, the dimensionality of the resulting networks. The 1D and 2D MOCs provide a particularly relevant platform to establish relationships between network dimensionality and physical properties. Their photoluminescence and electrical properties reveal distinct trends across the Cu, Ag, and Au series, with dimensionality playing a key role in both light emission and charge transport. The review further discusses the dynamic behavior of these materials, including ligand-exchange processes and reversible transformations between different structural and physical states. Their ability to form fibers, thin films, glasses, and composite materials further illustrates the versatility of MOCs beyond their crystalline structures. Selected examples of optical thermometry, optoelectronics, phase-change materials, sensing, and catalysis demonstrate their emerging functional potential. Overall, this review emphasizes dimensionality as a central structural parameter for understanding structure–property relationships and guiding the design of functional MOCs.
items.authors: Alexis Giraudon, Buqin Xu, Chloé Andrade, Nathalie Guillou, Régis Debord, Gilles Ledoux

items.title: A bipartite quantum-acoustic architecture stabilizes multi-exciton solitons at 323 K
items.abstract: A fundamental thermal paradox has constrained the physical viability of quantum coherent Davydov solitons in protein α-helices for over 50 years. At 323 K (0.0278 eV), ambient thermal noise disrupts the localized amide I self-trapping resonance, rapidly scattering multi-quanta excitations into delocalized thermal states on femtosecond timescales. This long-standing decoherence gap is resolved by a non-equilibrium, bipartite quantum-acoustic stabilization matrix which induces a transverse acoustic viscoelastic phonon gap, extending exciton coherence lifetimes from 6.5 fs to 42.6 fs by acting as a macroscopic low-pass filter. Utilizing non-Markovian open quantum system simulations, we demonstrate that a highly polarizable variable-dipole linactant at the lipid raft interface induces localized electrodynamic Stark defects, breaking lattice translation symmetry to anchor the wave packet. Sustaining this protective boundary against passive diffusive loss mandates a strict kinetic equilibrium that arrests uncoupled proton leaks, directly coupling the continuous, hydrogen-bonded α-helices of eukaryotic F/V-type rotary c-rings to a hyper-rigid viscoelastic membrane locked in a far-from-equilibrium state. Finally, we present a definitive pathway to bypass thermal decoherence by establishing three physical boundary conditions to translate these biological principles into a predictive blueprint for synthetic quantum-acoustic metamaterials.
items.authors: Doris Loh, Russel J. Reiter

items.title: Quantum Subspace Expansion for Molecular Excited States: Representability, Stability, and Practical Considerations
items.abstract: Accurate treatment of excited states remains challenging for classical electronic-structure methods, motivating quantum algorithms that may provide more favorable resource scaling. We systematically assess the practical performance of Quantum Subspace Expansion (QSE) for low-lying electronic states across 28 organic molecules from the Thiel benchmark set. Statevector simulations reveal that QSE representability depends strongly on the target state, active space, and molecular electronic structure, with multiconfigurational character emerging as an important factor. In several cases, the one-body QSE subspace cannot adequately represent the target states, while explicit double-excitation operators improve representability at the cost of a larger operator space. Analysis of the QSE overlap matrix shows that although eigenmodes with small eigenvalues drive numerical instability, they cannot be discarded indiscriminately without compromising spectral accuracy. Under finite-shot sampling, energy errors exhibit an empirical scaling of approximately n_{\mathrm{orb}}^2/\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{shots}}} , which, combined with the growth in measurement groups, yields a total measurement cost of approximately \mathcal{O}(n_{\mathrm{orb}}^{11}) for constant accuracy under our direct-estimation protocol. These results expose a central tension between representability, numerical stability, and measurement cost. Encouragingly, we find that the projected matrices exhibit recurring structural patterns, while the finite-shot perturbations in the Hamiltonian and overlap matrices show nontrivial covariance, suggesting opportunities for more efficient structure-aware measurement and reconstruction strategies. Overall, our results provide an assessment of QSE across chemically-relevant organic molecules, identifying present limitations while highlighting potential routes toward more practical future implementations.
items.authors: Naythan Z. X. Yeo, Shi Jun Ang

items.title: Selective Operando Visualization of Ultrathin Lithium in Li-Metal Batteries by Neutron Capture Imaging
items.abstract: Operando visualization of ultrathin lithium is essential for understanding plating and stripping in lithium-metal batteries, but existing neutron imaging techniques lack sufficient sensitivity for ultra-thin lithium layers formed at crucial early stages. Here we introduce neutron capture imaging (NCI), which selectively detects tritons generated by neutron capture in 6 Li. Ex situ measurements of electrochemically plated and thermally evaporated 6 Li demonstrate sensitivity around 10 nm for a 1.5 h acquisition and two-dimensional imaging with around 100 μm lateral resolution. Simulations indicate that the resolution could approach 25 μm through optical optimization. Operando measurements in an asymmetric Cu|| 6 Li cell reveal spatially heterogeneous lithium plating and stripping in agreement with electrochemical data. Our results establish NCI as a high-sensitivity, near-zero-background tool for operando studies of lithium metal batteries, opening new possibilities for resolving early-stage deposition, dead lithium formation, and interfacial dynamics with broad applicability to ultrathin reactive lithium layers in electrochemical systems.
items.authors: Xiaolong Zhang, Leon Skarjan, Ricardo Carreon, Jongmin Lee, Andreas Borgschulte, Thomas J. Schmidt

items.title: Ultra-Low CoNi Alloy Nanoparticle Loaded Polypyrrole Nanospheres as Oxygen Electrocatalysts in Alkaline to Near-Neutral Zinc-Air Batteries
items.abstract: Dearth of a wide-range pH-adaptable bifunctional oxygen electrocatalyst is a bottleneck in the advancement of efficient metal-air batteries as catalysts optimized for alkaline media often lose effectiveness under near-neutral conditions. Herein, we report an ultralow (~1 atomic%) amount of CoNi alloy loaded polypyrrole-derived graphitic nanoparticle (CoNiPpy) system as a pH-adaptable oxygen electrocatalyst for high energy density and durability in near-neutral zinc-air batteries (ZABs) with 100% coulombic efficiency. The efficient activity of CoNiPpy towards oxygen reduction and oxygen evolution reactions (ORR and OER) is established, with CoNiPpy showing a lower overpotential than the benchmarked Pt-IrO2 catalyst combo in both alkaline and near-neutral electrolytes. When employed as the air cathode in rechargeable ZABs, CoNiPpy outperforms Pt/C benchmarks, sustaining 650 cycles in alkaline electrolyte and 1100 cycles for ~200 h in near-neutral electrolyte. Stable operating voltages of 1.435 V and 1.235 V are achieved in alkaline and near-neutral ZABs respectively. Series connected cells further power a 33 mW lighting load for more than 1 h and operate portable sensors, demonstrating functionality beyond conventional electrochemical benchmarking. Detailed full-cell analysis demonstrates that, rather than relying on high metal loadings, trace CoNi incorporation into a conductive N-containing carbon framework can enable a single bifunctional air cathode to operate across both alkaline and near-neutral ZAB chemistries. The findings further emphasize that appropriate electrolyte selection plays an important role in full-cell performance and guiding the development of scalable zinc-air battery systems.
items.authors: Subhra R. Pattanayak, Pallavi Thakur, Saswata Goswami, Hyoju Park, Arun Devaraj, Chandra Sekhar Tiwary

items.title: Discovery of new octadecanoids in γ-linolenic acid rich oils
items.abstract: 17 novel hydroxy fatty acids derived from LA, ALA, and GLA were characterized in evening 2 primrose, borage and hemp oil. Structural characterization was based on semi-synthetic 3 standards generated by autoxidation, photoxidation and enzymatic conversions, combined 4 with LC-MS and GC-MS analysis with multiple derivatization strategies. Novel oxylipins 6-5 HODE and 7-HODE, presumably formed as site-products of Δ6-desaturase, showed 6 characteristic patterns in GLA-rich oils: 6-HODE occurred at high levels in in evening primrose 7 oil (23 ± 1 mg/100 g) and in borage oil (84 ± 7 mg/100 g), whereas 7-HODE (28.7 ± 8 0.6 mg/100 g) was abundant in hemp oil. These novel oxylipins occurred in similar 9 concentrations in both cold-pressed and refined oils and did not relate to the oxidation status. 10 Although, the occurrence of autoxidatively formed hydroxy-LA, ALA and GLA correlated with 11 peroxide value. Overall, these findings highlight novel oxylipins as promising markers of oil 12 quality and authenticity. 13 14 15 16
items.authors: Ariane Löwen, Lia Warja Musielak, Kathrin Plitzko, Nils Helge Schebb

items.title: Hypoboric Acid Catecholate (HAC) Catalysis for Stereoselective Decarboxylative Borylation of Redox-Active Esters
items.abstract: The Hypoboric Acid Catecholate (HAC) is a new class of diboron reagent bearing a borylcatecholato and a boronic acid moiety. Herein, we demonstrate that HACs can also be expontaneously formed in situ from collections of catechols and hypoboric acid. These HACs catalyze the decarboxylative borylation of redox-active esters, providing superior reactivity and selectivity. Equilibrium and kinetic NMR experiments indicate that the catalytic turnover is enabled by the high affinity of catechols for hypoboric acid and their low affinity for boronic acids that is uncovered herein. The catalytic system operates in mild conditions and is robust towards air and moisture, demonstrating its utility in the synthesis of important medicinally-relevant boronates. The enhanced selectivity is sourced in the regioselective radical capture by HAC intermediates at their customized borylcatecholato moiety, which can easily be stereoelectronically tailored for specific applications. These features of the catalytic approach with unsymmetrical HACs presented herein contrast with current state-of-the-art methods based on stoichiometric symmetrical diboron reagents.
items.authors: S. V. Kohlhepp, M. Costantini, B. Meana-Baamonde, Abraham Mendoza

items.title: pH-responsive nanopores enable programmable transmembrane potential
items.abstract: Biological ion channels achieve highly selective, ultrafast ion transport through stimulus-responsive gating, in which conformational changes triggered by chemical cues such as pH that modulate channel permeability with exquisite precision. Replicating this coupled chemical-structural functionality in synthetic membranes remains a fundamental challenge, particularly for scalable platforms relevant to energy harvesting, desalination, and chemical sensing. Here, we report a bioinspired polymer-metal-organic framework (MOF) composite membrane in which an amino acid (histidine) functionalized MOF nanopores serve as synthetic proton-gated anion channel. The histidine modified, spatially confined ion transport pathway exhibited selective Cl- diffusion at pH 4, enabling pH programmable control of transmembrane potential. Micrometer-scale percolated transport networks within the composite membrane, architecturally inspired by ion channels embedded in lipid bilayers, translate localized αNH2(histidine)-anion specific interaction into macroscopic, anion selective transmembrane potential output. This work establishes a generalizable design strategy for coupling chemical gating with macroscopic ion transport in synthetic membrane systems, with direct implications for ion separations, sensing and osmotic energy generation.
items.authors: KM. Archana Yadav, Ritupan Sarmah, Bibhab Bandhu Majumdar, Renjith B. Nelliyil, Jaideep Mor, A R Ramya

items.title: Electrochemically Controlled Crystallization Using Selective Bipolar Membrane Electrodialysis
items.abstract: Nitrogen and phosphorus nutrient recovery from wastewater represents a critical frontier for circular fertilizer manufacturing and effective water treatment. Conventional chemical precipitation remains hindered by the need for expensive reagent consumables. Here, we examine an integrated, chemical-free electrochemical mixer (ECM) system that leverages selective bipolar membrane electrodialysis (SBED) to achieve precise struvite (MgNH4PO4 · 6H2O) crystallization. We furthermore demonstrate how control over current density (1–5 mA cm−2), specific charge loading (20–40 C m−3), and hydraulic retention time (τ = 2.3–6.9 s) enhances downstream crystallization yield, purity, and morphology. Shortening retention promotes boundary-layer convection, reducing in-cell scaling energy penalty (∆E) by 86% and total stack energy consumption by 22%. Operating within an optimized pH window (7.7 pH 9.0) governs crystal morphology and allows for 91% yield of highly pure struvite ( 97%), bypassing competitive newberyite crystallization. We unify the ECM transport kinetics and crystallization thermodynamics into a single dimensionless descriptor—the crystallization index—which establishes a linear correlation to predict the product yield based on upstream transport dynamics. Steady specific energy consumption of 9.38 ± 0.9 kWh kg−1 − struvite through autonomous in-situ acid flushing confirms system stability with minimal scaling. Finally, techno-economic analysis evaluates the levelized cost of struvite produced as $996 t−1, which is a reduction in operating expenditures by a maximum of 89% compared to commercial phosphorus recovery installations. Ultimately, the ECM eliminates crystallization chemical dependencies and reduces membrane scaling bottlenecks, establishing a highly tunable and efficient separations reactor with precise control of crystal products.
items.authors: Hyuck Joo Choi, Spandan Mondal, Mohammed Tahmid, Marta C. Hatzell

items.title: Bonding, Biradicaloid Character, and Real-Space Topology of the Dinitrosyl Beryllium Dimer Be2(NO)2: A Multiconfigurational and Energy-Decomposition Study
items.abstract: The structural, vibrational, thermodynamic, multiconfigurational electronic structure, biradicaloid character, charge-transfer bonding, and real-space topological properties of the dinitrosyl beryllium dimer, Be2(NO)2, are investigated using density functional theory (DFT) at the TPSS/def2-TZVP-D4 level, complete active space self-consistent field (CASSCF) coupled with N-electron valence state second-order perturbation theory (NEVPT2), STEOM-DLPNO-CCSD, and multi-wavefunction topological analyses via Multiwfn. Energy Decomposition Analysis combined with Natural Orbitals for Chemical Valence (EDA-NOCV) and Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM) reveal that the stability of this unique main-group cluster is governed by strong electrostatic interactions, pronounced charge-transfer components, multi-centre core bonding, and synergistic orbital back-donation channels. Natural orbital occupation numbers and narrow singlet–triplet gaps further confirm significant biradicaloid character.
items.authors: D. K. Jha, M. Pathak, Dhananjay Kumar Jha

items.title: A Fragment-Based Mechanistic Potential for Noncovalent Systems: Combining Conceptual DFT and Quantum Chemical Topology Domains
items.abstract: Within a framework combining conceptual Density Functional Theory (cDFT) with the computational efficiency of the quantum chemical topology (QCT) description of matter, we introduce a mechanistic potential designed for the fast exploration of intermolecular potential-energy surfaces between rigid molecular fragments. The proposed strategy deliberately retains only a minimal set of physically interpretable contributions, namely electrostatics, charge transfer, and dispersion. All electronic properties are evaluated once for the isolated rigid fragments and subsequently propagated using the Kabsch algorithm during their relative translations and rotations, so that the potential energy depends only on the six intermolecular degrees of freedom. The proposed workflow is illustrated using a set of noncovalent and donor-acceptor complexes displaying different degrees of directionality and intermolecular overlap. In the long-range regime, the effective potential mimics a substantial part of the orientational selectivity and correctly identifies the main low-energy regions and interaction-energy minima. This behavior is illustrated for weakly bound systems, hydrogen-bonded and donor–acceptor complexes, σ-hole interactions, the guanine–cytosine pair, and the CO2 molecule confined within a (H2O)20 clathrate cage. Deviations from reference DFT profiles become more pronounced at shorter intermolecular separations, where Pauli repulsion and polarization contributions, which are not explicitly included in the model, become significant.
