items.abstract: Nuclear-spin quantum sensing requires coherent molecular electron spin qubits embedded in analyte-recognizing local environments that bring target nuclei into their short-range hyperfine detection volume. Here, we introduce TA-TEMPO, a covalent organic framework in which dilute nitroxide radicals and Li + -binding triazine moieties form defect-engineered recognition pockets for room-temperature 7 Li sensing. Optimizing radical density preserves spin coherence while maximizing the 7 Li/ 1 H response acquired by hyperfine spectroscopy. TA-TEMPO detects Li + in a tetrahydrofuran solution of LiBr with a sensitivity of 1.0 × 10 −4 mol·L −1 at room temperature, a 50-fold improvement over the previous benchmark, and enables quantum sensing across several lithium-based electrolytes. Control experiments and density functional theory calculations show that triazine sites preferentially bind Li + over Na + and position it near nitroxide radicals, accounting for selective detection in a large excess of Na + . These results establish chemically programmed host-guest recognition as a strategy to integrate sensitivity, selectivity, and coherent spin readout in porous molecular quantum sensors.
items.authors: Zhecheng Sun, Chang Tang, Guangfu Ni, Zexin Jin, Lei Sun
items.title_zh: 缺陷工程识别口袋中的锂离子量子传感研究
items.summary_zh: 核自旋量子传感需要将分子电子自旋量子比特嵌入识别分析物的局部环境中，以便将目标核引入短程超精细检测体积。本文介绍了TA-TEMPO，这是一种共价有机框架，其中稀释的亚硝基自由基和锂离子结合的三嗪基团形成缺陷工程识别口袋，用于室温下的锂-7传感。优化自由基密度可保持自旋相干性，同时最大化通过超精细光谱获得的锂-7/氢-1响应。TA-TEMPO在室温下检测Li +，在LiBr的四氢呋喃溶液中灵敏度达到1.0 × 10 −4 mol·L −1，比之前的基准提高了50倍，并实现了在多种锂基电解质中的量子传感。对照实验和密度泛函理论计算表明，三嗪位点优先结合Li +而非Na +，并将其定位于亚硝基自由基附近，从而在大量Na +中实现选择性检测。这些结果确立了化学编程的宿主-客体识别作为在多孔分子量子传感器中整合灵敏度、选择性和相干自旋读出的策略。

items.title: Mining the cysteine-motif repertoire of airway mucins reveals redox-active mucolytic peptides
items.abstract: Muco-obstructive lung diseases are characterized by hyper concentrated airway mucus in which gel-forming mucins form mechanically reinforced polymer networks. Thiol-based mucolytics can reduce disulfide bonds within these networks, but clinically used monothiols show limited potency, whereas stronger reducing agents are constrained by instability and toxicity. Here, we systematically mined the major airway mucins MUC5B and MUC5AC for closely spaced cysteine motifs and screened the resulting mucin-derived peptide library for redox activity, oxidation stability, solubility, epithelial compatibility, and mucolytic activity. The identified Cys–[X]n–Cys peptides displayed pronounced sequence- and pH-dependent thioldisulfide exchange capabilities, with many peptides reacting faster than monothiol controls and several exhibiting reactivity approaching or superior to dithiothreitol (DTT). Reactivity was governed by the combined effects of thiol number, apparent thiol pKa, and local motif architecture rather than by a single physicochemical descriptor. Analysis of free-thiol stability and oxidation products further revealed sequence-dependent access to distinct intra- and intermolecular disulfide states. Together, these measurements provide a systematic sequence-redox framework for understanding how closely spaced cysteine motifs tune thioldisulfide exchange, with implications for the design of redox-active peptides and for understanding how local cysteine sequence environments may contribute to oxidative protein folding. Developability profiling identified soluble, reduced-thiol-stable, and epithelialcompatible candidates. Selected peptides reduced high-molecular-weight MUC5B multimers in cystic fibrosis mucus and MUC5AC multimers in asthma mucus, with activities in the range of DTT and greater than NAC under the tested conditions. These peptides were active in both pathological and healthy mucus, while showing compound-dependent differences in their concentration-response profiles across mucus environments. Our findings point at airway mucins as a source of redox-active peptide candidates with potential for mucolytic therapy and provide a broadly applicable resource for relating cysteine-motif sequence to disulfideexchange behavior.
items.authors: Hussein Mamkhezri, Cosmin Butnarasu, Jolly Thomas, Nico Boback, Fabian Nußhardt, Hans Christian Brakebusch
items.title_zh: 气道粘蛋白中半胱氨酸基序的挖掘揭示了红氧活性粘液溶解肽
items.summary_zh: 粘液阻塞性肺病的特征是气道粘液的高度浓缩，其中形成凝胶的粘蛋白构成了机械增强的聚合物网络。硫醇类粘液溶解剂可以减少这些网络中的二硫键，但临床使用的单硫醇效力有限，而更强的还原剂受到不稳定性和毒性的限制。本文系统挖掘了主要气道粘蛋白MUC5B和MUC5AC中的紧密半胱氨酸基序，并筛选了得到的粘蛋白衍生肽库，评估其红氧活性、氧化稳定性、溶解性、上皮兼容性和粘液溶解活性。识别出的Cys–[X]n–Cys肽显示出显著的序列和pH依赖的硫醇-二硫键交换能力，许多肽的反应速度超过了单硫醇对照，且有些肽的反应性接近或优于二硫苏糖醇（DTT）。反应性受硫醇数量、表观硫醇pKa和局部基序结构的综合影响，而非单一物理化学描述符。自由硫醇稳定性和氧化产物的分析进一步揭示了序列依赖的不同分子内和分子间二硫状态的获取。这些测量为理解紧密半胱氨酸基序如何调节硫醇-二硫键交换提供了系统的序列-红氧框架。

items.title: Tissues As a Synthetic Target – A Framework For the Multiscale Molecular Design Of Thermogelling Polymers
items.abstract: Tissues are living, water-swollen composite polymer networks whose dynamic biochemical composition, hierarchical architecture, and mechanics collectively regulate cell behavior and physiological function. Recreating these properties across biological and biomedical contexts ( e.g. , 2D and 3D cell culture, tissue engineering, organoid culture, and regenerative medicine) remains a critical challenge as existing synthetic matrices cannot fully recapitulate the multiscale organization and dynamic properties of native extracellular matrices. Most hydrogel platforms rely on “drag-n-drop” combinations of polymers, crosslinkers, fabrication methods, and bioactive motifs to approximate the biophysical and biochemical properties of an individual tissue or biomedical context. In this Review, we seek to motivate the pursuit of thermogel-based “plug-n-play” approaches by framing tissues as synthetic targets and examining the potential of polymers that undergo thermally-triggered assembly to serve as modular building blocks for next-generation synthetic ECMs. The ultimate goal is a universal framework for programming composition, structure, mechanics, and biofunction from a common multiscale molecular design language. We first closely examine the composition, assembly, and properties of ECMs to clearly establish targets of interest and processes that may serve as inspiration. Finally, we connect the thermodynamic principles of lower critical solution temperature behavior with macromolecular topology, phase separation, and hierarchical assembly to establish design opportunities for creating thermogeling polymers that more closely mimic the fibrous, hydrated, mechanically adaptive, and cell-instructive nature of native ECMs. We propose that future progress will require the integration of precise polymer synthesis, topology-dictated assembly, macromolecular crowding, high-throughput formulation, and multiscale characterization to establish predictive structure–assembly–property relationships. This framework is intended to facilitate the transition of thermogeling polymers from injectable or temperature-responsive materials to a latent scalable synthetic platform for writing bespoke tissue-like microenvironments from molecularly programmed building blocks.
items.authors: Wynter A. Paiva, Rebecca Tobias, Aiden Saul, Benjamin R. McDonald

items.title: A Giant Fluoride-Bridged Rare-Earth Cluster with Moderate Hydrophobicity and Bright Luminescence Develops High-Resolution Latent Fingerprints
items.abstract: Visualization of latent fingerprints (LFPs) at high resolution plays a vital role in crime scene investigation. The key to obtain high resolution image of LFPs is to design a developer that has strong contact with LFPs and bright luminescence. Since LFPs comprise both hydrophilic components (e.g., inorganic salts and water from sweat) and hydrophobic components (e.g., fatty acids and squalene from sebum) designing luminescent materials with appropriate hydrophobicity holds significant importance. Here we show that a family of fluoride-bridged rare-earth (RE) clusters with a common formula of [RE 26 (µ 3 -F) 40 (µ-F) 4 (µ 6 -F)(piv) 31 (H 2 O) 8 (cyclen) 2 (DCA) 2 ]·DMF (abbr. REFC-26, RE = Nd, Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy and Er) can achieve this goal. REFC-26 has not only the largest nuclearity among air-stable fluoride-bridged RE clusters known to date, but also both hydrophobic and hydrophilic functional groups on the surface. Coupled with the excellent luminescent properties of EuFC-26 and TbFC-26, these clusters effectively suppress background interference, yielding high-contrast and high-resolution fingerprint images. The resolution reaches a precise identification of level 1-3 features that range from macroscopic ridges to microscopic sweat pores even after the LFPs are aged for 30 days. Such a remarkable performance outperforms most LFP developers and may open a new photographic developer design based on luminescent RE clusters.
items.authors: Yu Wang, Jian-Yue He, Sai-Sai Xie, Jing-Mei Wu, Xia-Li Ding, Wei-Peng Chen

items.title: An Algorithm for computing Three- and Four-Body Density Matrices from CASCI Wavefunction and AI-Assisted Code Optimization
items.abstract: Three- and four-body reduced density matrices in the active space are required for second-order n-electron valence perturbation theory (NEVPT2) following complete active-space configuration interaction (CASCI) calculations. We developed an algorithm to generate these computationally demanding quantities by extending the pi-CASCI program, which is based on the graphical symmetric group approach (GSGA). A manually written prototype was subsequently optimized through AI-assisted code optimization, resulting in substantially improved performance.
items.authors: Kiyoshi Tanaka, Takahiro Katagiri, Tatsuya Nakano, Yuji Mochizuki

items.title: Reviving Fused-ring Currents on Pentagonal Bipyramidal Cages
items.abstract: The coexistence of 2D π-aromaticity and 3D σ-aromaticity within a single edge-fused molecule remains an open question, as the two aromatic subsystems are often assumed to be electronically incompatible. Here we fuse benzene, C 7 H 7 + and C 7 H 7 – onto the pentagonal-bipyramidal B 7 H 5 /C 2 B 5 H 5 fragment and systematically vary the fusion-edge composition (B–B, B–C, C–C), evaluating the 2D ring with GIMIC bond currents, NICS, ISE and EDDB. The 3D cage aromaticity remains essentially intact in aromatic cases, whereas the fate of the 2D ring depends strongly on the ring type and the fusion edge. Benzene fusion gives only weakly aromatic 2D rings, while C7H7 + fused through boron-rich edges develops a desymmetrized through-edge current path and sustains strong diatropic circuits up to 13.2 nA/T, restoring magnetic communication between the 2D ring and the 3D cage. Adding two electrons instead produces local paratropic circuits on the 2D rings via a HOMO-to-LUMO rotational transition. Throughout these systems the four descriptors diverge within both aromatic and antiaromatic series.
items.authors: Guo Yu, Zhanchao Meng, Guangxin Liang

items.title: Diabat 2.0: A Comprehensive Diabatization Toolkit for Multichromophoric Systems
items.abstract: The construction of physically meaningful quasi-diabatic states and the evaluation of their electronic couplings are essential for describing nonadiabatic processes in molecular aggregates and other multichromophoric systems. Existing software implementations, however, are often restricted to dimers, two-state models, or particular types of quasi-diabatic states. Here, we present Diabat 2.0, a comprehensive toolkit for multistate diabatization in multichromophoric systems. It constructs the adiabatic-to-diabatic (ATD) transformation based on the adiabatic-state wave functions and energies obtained from external quantum chemistry calculations, yielding quasi-diabatic states and their electronic couplings in a nearly black-box manner. Diabat 2.0 implements several advanced ATD methods, including a general approach that can reliably construct quasi-diabatic states with diverse charge and excitation distributions without prescribing state types. This enables Diabat 2.0 to support diabatization in a broad range of scenarios that involve not only conventional charge-transfer, locally excited, and correlated triplet pair states, but also a variety of exotic states, such as mixed radical-triplet states, trion states, radical-coupled triplet-pair states, and charge-localized dicationic states. These capabilities are demonstrated in applications to several multichromophoric systems that pose substantial challenges to existing software.
items.authors: Yu-Chen Wang, Yicheng Qin, Yi Zhao, WanZhen Liang

items.title: When aggregation becomes the norm: interpreting experiments beyond their molecules
items.abstract: Chemical theory and the interpretation of experiments are typically articulated in terms of individual molecules. In the condensed phase, this approach is less generally applicable than commonly believed: phases, aggregates and clusters abound. But without an indication if and when to look for them, they tend to escape the chemist’s eye and consideration. Nonetheless, assemblies of even a handful of molecules show behaviour that resembles that of bulk phases rather than of individual molecules. We review illustrative examples and revisit general scientific laws for assemblies. We then illustrate how they apply to surprisingly common experimental situations, and outline some methodology and general cues for detecting phase behaviour that could otherwise remain hidden. We conclude that analysis in terms of phases enables straightforward interpretation of behaviour that can otherwise be quite perplexing.
items.authors: Alex Blokhuis, Yannick Geiger, Sijbren Otto

items.title: ToSCA: Total Scattering Conditioned Variational Autoencoder for Atomic Structure Prediction from Pair Distribution Function Data
items.abstract: Designing new materials is often slow and experimentally intensive, with structural characterization representing a particular bottleneck. Recent advances in machine learning (ML) aim to accelerate this process by predicting plausible atomic structures describing a material directly from experimental data. Here we present the total scattering conditioned variational autoencoder (ToSCA), a generative ML model for predicting plausible atomic structures of metal oxide nanomaterials from total scattering and pair distribution function (PDF) data. ToSCA learns a chemically meaningful latent representation and predicts unit cells within tolerances suitable for subsequent real-space refinement. The model also shows behavior consistent with learning structural relationships between related crystal types, and can correctly place the new CHILI-Interpolation dataset in the latent space. Finally, we demonstrate that ToSCA is able to retain useful performance in a realistic use-case by testing it on 11 experimental PDFs from 3 crystal types, including test cases outside of the training distribution.
items.authors: Ulrik Friis-Jensen, Frederik L. Johansen, Erik B. Dam, Raghavendra Selvan, Kirsten M. Ø. Jensen

items.title: Cyclic Block Copolymers via Ring Expansion Metathesis Polymerization
items.abstract: Cyclic block copolymers are a captivating class of macromolecules with the potential for advanced materials applications due to their distinctive self-assembly behavior. Ring expansion metathesis polymerization (REMP) is a promising method towards such high molar mass cyclic polymers, but uncontrolled intermolecular ring-transfer processes have precluded its extension to cyclic block copolymers synthesis. As a result, the synthesis of cyclic block copolymers remains exceedingly rare. In this work, we utilize newfound living characteristics of REMP with cyclic Ru-benzylidene initiator Pyr-CB6 to develop novel block copolymerization methodology. Using an operationally simple sequential monomer-addition strategy followed by thermally triggered intramolecular backbiting, we produce cyclic multiblock copolymers of low dispersity ( 1.2) and high yields (up to 97%). Mechanistic analyses elucidate the delicate role that pyridine plays in the polymerization process. As a metathesis inhibitor, pyridine makes intermolecular ring-transfer prohibitively slow, but permits intramolecular backbiting when triggered. Overall, this study demonstrates the power of REMP with Pyr-CB6 as a vehicle towards a diverse future of cyclic block copolymer materials and applications.
items.authors: Lucy P Miller, Matthew R Golder

items.title: Orthonym: verified IUPAC names for chemical structures in the wild
items.abstract: Chemical structures can be named systematically, and the 2013 IUPAC recommendations define one preferred name for each. For most of history, only a specially trained chemist or dedicated closed software tools could generate a correct, systematic molecule name from a chemical structure. Published neural structure-to-name translators can produce a fluent name for the wrong molecule. Here we present Orthonym: a generator of verified IUPAC names for chemical structures. This open, deterministic, rule-based generator emits a name only after verifying that it correctly describes the input structure. OPSIN reads back each candidate name, and the InChIKey of the parsed structure must equal that of the input; otherwise, the engine declines to name. On 2.2 million selected molecules from ChEBI, QM9, PubChem and ZINC22, it named 97.37% correctly and emitted no name for the wrong molecule. Orthonym is available under the MIT licence as a Python package and a web application.
items.authors: Kohulan Rajan, Achim Zielesny, Christoph Steinbeck

items.title: Liquid State 31P NMR as a Tool to Leverage the Understanding of Reconstituted Milk Systems
items.abstract: The objective of this work was to establish the peak assignment in liquid state 31P NMR of milk systems and investigate the method as a tool to identify di!erences in casein micelles as consequence of di!erent processing history. Suspensions of milk protein concentrate with removal of casein micelles by EDTA addition and ultra-centrifugation were analyzed by liquid state 31P NMR and compared with the original suspensions. Moreover, 1H-31P total correlation spectroscopy NMR was applied to di!erentiate between peaks from phosphoserines and inorganic phosphate in dairy systems. The results provide direct evidence that the signals observed in liquid-state 31P NMR of milk systems originate from phosphoserine residues in soluble caseins and inorganic phosphate in the serum phase, thereby resolving conflicting assignments reported in previous studies. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that liquid state 31P NMR is able to quantitatively di!erentiate the native amount of inorganic phosphate in the serum phase in suspensions of milk protein concentrate and skim milk. In light of the crucial importance of the calcium phosphate equilibrium between milk serum and casein micelles for understanding the casein micelle structure and its changes, liquid state 31P NMR shows potential as a suitable technique to get a better understanding of how processing a!ect the mineral equilibrium in casein micelles.
items.authors: Pernille Koch, Dennis W. Juhl, Kirsten G. Malmos, Thomas Vosegaard

items.title: Azobenzene-Mediated Reversible Conformational Switching in 9,9′-Bifluorenylidene-Based Molecular Machines
items.abstract: Intrinsically dynamic molecules offer attractive building blocks for molecular machines, yet controlling their conformational motion with external stimuli remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report Azo–BF–Azo, a photoresponsive molecular machine in which an intrinsically dynamic 9,9′-bifluorenylidene (BF) core is coupled to two visible-light-responsive tetra-orthofluorinated azobenzene (Azo) units that act as molecular actuators. Irradiation at 525 nm induces trans-to-cis photoisomerization of the Azo units, accompanied by a shift of the BF framework from the closed toward the open conformation, whereas irradiation at 456 nm reverses Azo isomerization and restores the BF-closed state over time. DFT calculations reveal that the extended trans-Azo units favor intramolecular π–π interactions that stabilize the closed BF conformation, while their conversion to the folded cis state disrupts these interactions and alters the steric environment surrounding the BF core. Variable-temperature NMR spectroscopy provides experimental support for the role of these intramolecular interactions in regulating the BF conformational equilibrium. The photoinduced state additionally undergoes spontaneous thermal relaxation, recovering approximately 65% of the initial state. Together, these results demonstrate that local photoisomerization of peripheral Azo actuators can reshape the conformational landscape of an intrinsically dynamic BF core through the cooperative modulation of steric and intramolecular π–π interactions. This work provides a strategy for converting intrinsic molecular dynamics into externally programmable motion and establishes a design principle for constructing integrated molecular machines in which one type of molecular motion regulates another.
items.authors: Sohail Mahajan, Reese Rich, Lin Jiao, Duhan Zhang, Wendu Ding, Jinjia Xu

items.title: Neural Kinetics: LEARNING KINETICS AS TRANSPORT IN COMPOSITIONAL SPACE
items.abstract: Complex bio-derived and fossil mixtures contain thousands of molecules whose individual structures and reaction pathways cannot be fully resolved, making conventional mechanism-based kinetic modelling impractical. A reaction network detailed enough to describe every formula-level transformation would contain far more reactions and parameters than the available data can constrain. We propose to overcome this limitation by representing mixtures directly as abundance fields on a compositional grid indexed by molecular descriptors, specifically carbon number (#C) and double-bond equivalent (DBE), and by learning a time-conditioned, chemistry-informed operator that maps the initial composition to predict a later state. The evolution rates of the chemical space are learned by a two-dimensional Fourier neural operator (FNO) acting jointly on a set of heteroatom classes, with normalized time and compositional coordinates appended as input channels. Because experimental data are limited, we enlarge the training set with synthetic trajectories generated from the measured samples, pre-train on this ensemble, and then calibrate a small subset of parameters on the measured distributions. We tested the framework on a case of oxidation of a complex hydrocarbon mixture that is tracked by FTICR-MS over sixty seconds of reaction. On an independent sample the framework, that we named NeuralKinetics, reproduced the measured endpoint class composition within a mean absolute error of approximately one percent and arranged the heteroatom classes correctly on the compositional grid. The second test was an entirely different system: litter decomposition in a peatland warming experiment, also followed by FTICR-MS but over two years. The developed operator accurately predicted the endpoint class composition of the held-out sample proving that the framework is flexible enough to adapt to diverse reactive systems.
items.authors: Paolo Guida, Naydu Zambrano Urrutia, Elia Colleoni, Shekhar R Kulkarni, Kevin Van Geem, William L. Roberts

items.title: Self-Assembled 3,4,9,10-Perylenetetracarboxylic Dianhydride is a Molecular Graphite
items.abstract: Viable organic charge storage materials must display rapid cation insertion. Typically, these materials are composed of monomers that undergo slow outer-sphere electron transfer coupled to significant bond rearrangement. Here we show that 3,4,9,10-perylenetetracarboxylic dianhydride (PTCDA) self-assembles into an organic material that undergoes graphite-like cation insertion-coupled electron transfer rather than forming a radical anion or an enolate, as previously thought. This charge storage pathway is enabled by a semiconducting band structure, coincident with cation insertion between self-assembled PTCDA molecules. Based on these results, we propose that self-assembled PTCDA is best thought of as a synthetically tunable “molecular graphite” that combines the best features of molecules with the rapid insertion pathways of traditional intercalation solids.
items.authors: Jaeyoung Lee, Nuren Lara, Tyler Case, Carrie Donley, Natalie Druffner, Nathaniel Yeboah

items.title: Revealing Solvent-free Solid-fed Aerosol Flame Technique to Synthesize Copper Oxide Deposited on Ceria Catalyst for Efficient CO Oxidation Applications
items.abstract: Developing efficient technologies for CO oxidation is an urgent priority in environmental catalysis. Copper oxide deposited on cerium oxide (CuO/CeO 2 ) has attracted considerable attention as a promising non-precious-metal catalyst for low-temperature CO oxidation. Furthermore, aerosol process emerged as a scalable route to engineer CuO/CeO 2 with tailored structures and interfacial properties, however, popular vapor-fed and liquid-fed aerosol flame approaches remain constrained by precursor requirements (vapor-fed: sufficient vapor pressure; liquid-fed: precursor solubility or dispersibility in carrier solvents). Here, for the first time, we introduce solid-fed aerosol flame synthesis (SAFS) as a single-step, solvent-free route to synthesize heterostructured CuO/CeO 2 catalysts. Through selective vaporization of Cu 2 O followed by heterogeneous nucleation onto solid CeO 2 particles, SAFS produces a well-defined architecture of CuO nanoparticles intimately deposited on CeO 2 supports. By varying the flame conditions and Cu loading, we systematically investigate their effects on particle formation, interfacial properties, and catalytic performance. The highest performance catalyst, synthesized at 2 L/min-CH 4 flame with 2 wt.% Cu 2 O, exhibits the highest CO oxidation activity, achieving a CO oxidation rate of 13.73 mLCO/min·gcat and a turnover frequency of 0.026 s -1 at 120 ºC. This enhanced performance, compared to other as-prepared CuO/CeO 2 samples, arises from an optimal balance between oxygen vacancy generation and metal-support interaction achieved during the SAFS process. Here, oxygen vacancy generation is favored under fuel-rich conditions, whereas metal-support interaction decreases with CeO 2 sublimation and CuO nanoparticle sintering under elevated combustion enthalpy. These findings advance the fundamental understanding of flame-based synthesis and provide a scalable route toward high-performance, cost-effective catalysts for environmental remediation.
items.authors: Tung Van Pham, Tomoyuki Hirano, Izuki Maruhashi, Eka Lutfi Septiani, Kiet Le Anh Cao, Takashi Ogi

items.title: Wireless Bipolar Electrochemistry for Organic Electrosynthesis: Principles, Mechanistic Insights, and Emerging Autonomous Systems
items.abstract: Wireless bipolar electrochemistry (BPE) has emerged as a powerful platform for organic electrosynthesis, enabling redox transformations on electrically floating conductors without direct electrical wiring. Through electric-field-induced polarization, bipolar electrodes simultaneously promote spatially separated oxidation and reduction reactions, offering unique opportunities for reaction design, miniaturized reactor architectures, parallel processing, and sustainable chemical synthesis. Recent years have witnessed significant advances in both exogenous and endogenous bipolar electrochemical systems, expanding the scope of wireless electrosynthesis to asymmetric transformations, flow chemistry, low-electrolyte conditions, autonomous microreactors, and self-propelled electrochemical systems. This review critically examines the fundamental principles governing bipolar electrochemistry, recent developments in organic synthesis, and emerging diagnostic methodologies, including split bipolar electrodes and electrochemiluminescence-based imaging, which have substantially improved mechanistic understanding of charge transport, polarization phenomena, and reaction control. The advantages and limitations of wireless bipolar systems are evaluated in comparison with conventional electrolysis, highlighting challenges associated with reaction selectivity, scalability, energy efficiency, and quantitative electrochemical characterization. Finally, future opportunities involving advanced materials, operando analytical techniques, artificial intelligence-assisted optimization, and continuous-flow processing are discussed. Collectively, these developments position wireless bipolar electrochemistry as a promising enabling technology for next-generation sustainable electrosynthesis and autonomous electrochemical manufacturing.
items.authors: Sadia Rani, Najoua Sbei, Afshan Ramzan, Seyfeddine Rahali, Zia ul Haq, Nisar Ahmed

items.title: Assessing the state of the art in ADMET prediction: Lessons from the OpenADMET-ExpansionRx community blind challenge
items.abstract: Computational blind challenges are essential for advancing drug discovery, especially in research areas with limited public data, such as absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, toxicity (ADMET) prediction. In this paper, we present the results of our latest community blind challenge, organized in collaboration with Expansion Therapeutics (ExpansionRx). Participants were tasked with predicting nine distinct ADMET endpoints routinely evaluated during lead optimization of compounds in drug discovery programs. Following unprecedented engagement from the global community, this challenge provided valuable insights into the state of the art in machine learning for ADMET modeling. Evaluating submissions against a realistic, challenging dataset from active ExpansionRx drug discovery programs revealed that message-passing neural networks and chemical foundation models dominated among the top performers. Furthermore, the results highlighted the power of proprietary industry datasets and a critical need to optimize predictive workflows for different endpoints independently via multitasking and task-affinity grouping. We also demonstrate how hosting our open-source blind challenge infrastructure on a flexible platform like Hugging Face was pivotal for driving community engagement and visibility. Ultimately, blind challenges supported by robust infrastructure, widespread dissemination, and rigorous post-challenge analysis are fundamental to maximizing the utility of public data releases. We anticipate that these community benchmarks will continue to drive the advancement of ADMET models, enabling their deployment in both early- and late-stage drug discovery.
items.authors: Maria A. Castellanos, Hugo MacDermott-Opeskin, Jon Ainsley, Jonathan A. Swain, Sean Colby, Devany West

items.title: “Head-cut” 2DLC–HRMS (RPLC → HILIC) enhancing non-targeted chemical coverage in environmental exposomics.
items.abstract: Chemical coverage remains a major limitation in environmental non-target analysis (NTA), as conventional one-dimensional liquid chromatography (1D-LC) provides incomplete retention and separation across the broad physicochemical space encountered in complex samples. Here, we developed an online “head-cut” two-dimensional liquid chromatography–high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry (2DLC–HRMS/MS) approach combining reversed-phase liquid chromatography (RPLC) and hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography (HILIC), using a dual-trap system combining porous graphitic carbon and trimodal ion-exchange sorbents, to recover complementary regions of environmental chemical space within a single analysis. Trapping and modulation were first evaluated using a representative set of contaminants of emerging concern (CECs), evidencing that the combined complementary trapping materials achieves quantitative transfer (40-100%) of chemically diverse polar and mobile analytes to HILIC. Feature-based NTA performance of the optimized 2DLC method was comparatively evaluated in river water and effluent wastewater and compared with the corresponding 1D-HILIC and 1D-RPLC. “Head-cut” 2DLC yielded approximately 2.3–2.6-fold more blank-corrected ESI(+) and ESI(−) features than either individual 1D separation. Beyond feature level coverage, DIA componentization demonstrated that precursor-associated MS/MS information increased and successfully distributed across both 2DLC chromatographic domains. Fragment Ambiguity Score (FAS) analysis of ESI(+) data further confirmed the occurrence of low-ambiguity, structurally informative fragments within the expanded separation space. These results demonstrate that wide-interaction recovery of the RPLC blind spot can extend measurable chemical space and access to fragmentation information relevant for structural annotation, supporting “head-cut” RPLC→HILIC–HRMS/MS as a promising strategy for increasing chemical coverage in environmental NTA.
items.authors: Lapo Renai, Guylain. T. A. Cuiper, Viktoriia Turkina, Aleksandra Chojnacka, Saer Samanipour, Andrea F. G. Gargano

items.title: Agentic Paper: From Tacit Expertise to AI-Ready Scientific Data and Knowledge Corpora
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) for domain science demands large, well-structured training corpora that integrate experimental data with not only explicit knowledge but also tacit expertise underlying scientific decisions. However, the tacit knowledge regarding practical reasoning, assumptions, failed attempts, parameter choices, and interpretive judgment is often held by authors and unpublished, hindering its use for AI development. Here, we propose Agentic Paper, a large language model (LLM)-enabled, author-curated scientific publishing framework that organizes these resources into a structured Agentic Paper package accessible through LLM-based interfaces, enabling the integration of connected, AI-ready data, explicit knowledge, and tacit expertise. Within Agentic Paper, the LLM serves as an interactive reasoning and orchestration layer that connects knowledge content with raw and processed data, figures, methodological details, metadata, code, and author-provided interpretation. Case studies in materials synthesis and characterization demonstrate how the LLM-enabled framework supports questioning, data visualization and inspection, numerical verification, and preparation of AI-ready datasets. By combining author-based organization of scientific data and knowledge, Agentic Paper provides a scalable pathway toward provenance-rich training corpora and more reliable AI-enabled scientific workflows.
items.authors: Luke Schneider, Ganesh Narasimha, Sumner B. Harris, Ralph Bulanadi, Asraful Haque, Rama Vasudevan

items.title: Excited-State Intramolecular Proton Transfer Dynamics with Neural Network Potentials and Nuclear Quantum Effects
items.abstract: Excited-state intramolecular proton transfer is a prototypical ultrafast process that forms the foundation for many chemical and biological phenomena and is highly sensitive to changes in the underlying potential energy landscape. Here, we develop neural network potentials for 10-hydroxybenzo[h]quinoline that describe ground- and excited-state dynamics with near ab initio accuracy. These neural network potentials enable efficient sampling of the proton transfer coordinate and incorporation of nuclear quantum effects through path-integral molecular dynamics. The free energy profiles show that excited-state intramolecular proton transfer proceeds on a largely barrierless excited-state surface, with nuclear quantum effects reducing and smoothing the residual barrier. Non-equilibrium simulations yield an average proton transfer time of ~11.5 fs for quantum hydrogen, consistent with experiment, and reveal a clear isotope effect, with slower dynamics for deuterium and classical nuclei. Mechanistic analysis identifies transient proton donor–acceptor contraction as the key enabling coordinate, while the proton crosses the midpoint prior to reaching the minimum of this coordinate, indicating a dynamically driven transfer. Subtle changes in the conjugated backbone precede proton transfer, reflecting early electronic reorganization and coherent coupling between proton motion and backbone vibrations. Bond-length alternation and vibrational coherence analysis reveal isotope-dependent coherence loss, with deuteration producing stronger damping and more localized proton/backbone dynamics relative to hydrogen. These results establish neural network potential-based approaches as an effective framework for simulating excited-state proton transfer with explicit nuclear quantum effects.
items.authors: Axel Gomez, Amke Nimmrich, Victor M. Freixas, Chenghao Zhang, Shaul Mukamel, Munira Khalil

items.title: Dynamic Parameter Screening for Accelerated Mechanistic Analysis
items.abstract: Mechanistic studies are essential for the continued advancement of the chemical sciences however; classical approaches remain laborious and material intensive. Graphical reaction analysis techniques such as RPKA and VTNA have substantially reduced this burden, yet the time and resources required to comprehensively study increasingly complex reactions remain high. Medium- and high-throughput batch and flow kinetic methods have been developed to further streamline data acquisition, but their widespread adoption is limited by the need for specialized equipment or expertise. Here we introduce dynamic parameter screening (DPS), in which a single batch reaction is monitored continuously while sequential reagent and catalyst additions are used to probe kinetic impacts of multiple species within one experimental setup. Using the palladium-catalyzed Kumada–Tamao–Corriu cross-coupling as a model system, we compared DPS with traditional one-factor-at-a-time approach across three catalytic systems (PdCl 2 (dppf)·CH 2 Cl 2 , PEPPSI-iPr, and XPhos Pd G2). DPS afforded essentially identical qualitative and quantitative (kinetic modeling) conclusions except for the case of XPhos Pd G2. This latter system exhibited multiple kinetic regimes where the traditional approach revealed the global impact of reagent concentrations, whereas DPS provided complementary, higher-resolution insight into reagent effects within a specific kinetic regime. The insights obtained from DPS guided a simple slow-dosing strategy that markedly improved reaction rates even at reduced catalyst loadings. DPS therefore provides a practical, low-barrier route to high-resolution kinetic information that is fully compatible with conventional modeling, broadening access to mechanistic understanding in resource-limited settings.
items.authors: Dylan J. Pyle, Finn Bork, Wesley McNutt, Ekaterina Trushina, Joshua S. Derasp, Sara M. Guzman

items.title: Drop-in Silver Nanogap−Cellulose Concentrator for Surface-Enhanced Raman Monitoring of Water Contaminants
items.abstract: Organic contaminants in natural waters threaten ecosystems and human health, motivating integrated strategies for trace-level monitoring. Although surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) offers molecular specificity and trace-level sensitivity, many platforms require separate preconcentration, provide limited control over analyte delivery to plasmonic hot spots, and lose performance in complex water matrices. Here, a poly(ether-block-amide) (PEBAX)-coated Ag nanogap–cellulose concentrator is reported, coupling self-driven interfacial enrichment with Raman readout through an amphiphilic, chemically heterogeneous, mixed-polarity interface. The engineered interface enabled charge-diverse partitioning of cationic and anionic molecular probes down to 10 -10 M across a broad pH range. Relative to the uncoated sensor, interfacial enrichment coupled to Ag nanogaps lowered SERS detection limits by up to 3,100-fold, reaching 1.1 × 10 -11 M for crystal violet and 2.3 × 10 -9 M for methyl orange. In untreated tap and lake water, the coated sensor resolved crystal violet and methyl orange fingerprints that were weak or variable on the uncoated sensor and identified acetamiprid and thymol within 30 min. These results show that coupling interfacial concentration with nanogap-mediated molecular readout establishes an integrated route for passive monitoring of trace contaminants in complex water matrices.
items.authors: Jonghyun Shin, Young Jun Kim, Yaprak Özbakir, Tzu-Chiao Wei, Cho-Hee Yang, Jiwoo Ko

items.title: Towards Environmentally Friendly Removal of Acrylate-Based Impregnation from Commercial Carbon Fiber Roving
items.abstract: Carbon fibers face a growing use in industry due to their exceptional mechanical and light-weight properties. Particularly they are used as carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) in lightweight mobility, wind turbines and as concrete reinforcements to create light-weight and durable structural components. To fully enable their environmentally friendly use, full life cycles and end-of-life scenarios have to be developed. Therefore, energyand cost-effective carbon fiber retrieval from polymer impregnated commercial samples needs to be investigated. In this study, we investigate a commercially available CFRP roving with an industrial acrylate-based impregnation, commonly used in construction as concrete reinforcements. The impact of several chemical solvents was assessed identifying acetic acid as a highly effective and environmentally friendly agent. To further reduce the concentration of acetic acid, electrochemical dissolution was tested where the carbon fiber was used as a working electrode in an electrochemical cell. Applying a voltage as low as 1.5 V vs. Ag|AgCl, the acetic acid concentration required to dissolve the polymer could be reduced by 33% compared to pure chemical treatment, while the tensile strength of the carbon fiber was maintained.
items.authors: Stefan Röher, Julius Scheel, Alexandra Apel, Stella Welzel, Lissy Flechsig, Christina Scheffler

items.title: Spins Afar - Long-Range Pulse Dipolar EPR Spectroscopy Uncovers Curvature in TRIM25’s Coiled Coil
items.abstract: Pulse Dipolar Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Spectroscopy (PDS) is a powerful method for determining nanometer distances in biomolecular systems. This methodology has been successfully used to validate structure hypotheses and to identify disorder. However, inherent distance limitations are under-explored. Many challenging biomolecular applications require long distance information, driving the need for a benchmarking study. We demonstrate distances up to 10.5 nm in TRIM25 reliably extracted from data obtained under standard sample conditions. By protein perdeuteration accurate distance measurements up to 17.3 nm were enabled. Enhancing sensitivity through optimization of the measurement and sample preparation conditions the achievable dipolar evolution time was extended to 150 µs. Thus, distances close to 20 nm should become experimentally accessible, highlighting the potential of advanced PDS methodologies for probing previously inaccessible long-range structural information in complex systems.
items.authors: Yannik Limbach, Katrin Ackermann, Aisika Chakraborty, David G. Norman, Bela E. Bode

items.title: Closing the Loop Between Synthetic and Living Cells
items.abstract: Synthetic cells are moving beyond compartmentalised microreactors to become integrated components of biological networks that physically and chemically merge with their hosts. Existing reviews classify this field by mode of emission, by chemistry, or by architecture, and so describe the construct rather than its effect. This review takes the receiver's side, treating the functional adaptation of the living host as the readout of bio-hybrid function: how living cells probe their synthetic partners mechanically and adapt to them metabolically. We consider the bio-hybrid interface by how far the feedback loop (sensing-actuation) is closed and set out the evidence that would place a study in each of four tiers: open-loop, half-loop, partial feedback, and closed-loop. Read against these criteria, sixteen of the eighteen studies surveyed here are half-loop, two reach partial feedback, and none is closed-loop. Both partial-feedback systems work the same way, by metabolic interception, which the existing taxonomies have no category for. The one construct that comes closest to closed-loop operation contains no living cell at all. We then trace how single-cell coupling is scaling into hybrid prototissues that act as discovery platforms for pathological microenvironments, and we outline the translational barriers these constructs must survive to reach the clinic.
items.authors: Ion Ioannou

items.title: Sorting Commodity Plastics by MOF-based Molecular Sieving
items.abstract: Efficient sorting of waste plastics according to their chemical structure is desirable for plastics recycling. Here, we present a novel methodology based on a molecular sieving mechanism to realize molecular-level sorting of polymer chains. Using nanopores in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) as the sieve, polymer chains are differentiated by their thickness and branching structure through selective infiltration into the nanopores in the molten state. The infiltration process is evaluated in situ and semi-quantitatively via continuous monitoring of relative diffraction intensity from the MOF using variable-temperature X-ray diffraction. Three MOFs with varying effective pore window diameters are identified as promising candidates that enable sequential sorting of four highly important commodity plastics: low-density polyethylene, polystyrene, polypropylene, and high-density polyethylene. This work would open up a new paradigm in the field by providing a versatile method capable of sorting the waste plastics mixture with molecular-level precision.
items.authors: Haruaki Suzuki, Ryo Shimura, Nobuhiko Hosono, Takashi Uemura

items.title: Critical assessment of published Kalina cycle studies: cycle configuration, state-point reporting and optimisation bounds
items.abstract: The Kalina cycle is widely proposed for converting geothermal, solar and waste heat, including in systems that also supply cooling, fresh water or hydrogen. It differs from an ammonia–water Rankine cycle in two respects established in its original formulation: a separator that produces a working solution richer in ammonia than the basic solution, and internal recuperation of turbineexhaust heat. Three operational criteria were derived from these features: non-zero mass flow in both separator outlets, a working-to-basic ammonia mass-fraction difference of at least 0.05, and non-zero recuperator duty. These criteria, a ten-item reporting checklist and a comparison of reported optima with the published search bounds were applied to 88 full-text journal articles, 84 of which designate a cycle as a Kalina cycle. In 17 of the 84 studies (20%; 95% CI 13–30%), at least one designated Kalina layout contained no recuperator or no separator. At the operating point of the principal results, all three criteria were demonstrably satisfied in 19 studies (23%), at least one was violated in 20 (24%), and 45 (54%) reported insufficient data for a decision. A complete state-point table was reported in 20 of the 88 studies. Of 40 optimisations performed with a named algorithm, 22 reported both bounds and optimal values; in 18 of these, at least one optimum coincided with or exceeded a bound, including all 14 single-objective cases. Agreement between an initial and a blinded repeat scoring was substantial (κ = 0.69–0.77). A verification procedure and a minimum reporting set are proposed.
items.authors: Mohammad Masrur Hossain, Mohammad Mehran Hossain

items.title: An Ultrathin Embedded SnO2 Interface for Water Dissociation in Bipolar Membranes and pseudo-PEM Electrolyzers
items.abstract: Water dissociation (WD) at bipolar membrane (BPM) junctions is a key reaction in a number of electrochemical energy conversion and separation technologies. While metal oxide catalysts like SnO 2 accelerate WD, conventional particle-based deposition methods typically yield thick and morphologically heterogeneous junction layers. We report a simple aqueous precursor-treatment route that reconstructs the near-surface region of Nafion into an ultrathin SnO 2 -bearing interface. In contrast to conventional spin-coated SnO 2 , which forms a discrete particulate overlayer, the embedded interface is smooth, spatially confined, and closely integrated with the membrane. Despite this major structural difference, BPMs fabricated from SnO 2 -eb-Nafion exhibit WD performance comparable to benchmark spin-coated SnO 2 junctions. When normalized by SnO 2 loading, the embedded junction delivers a ~21-fold higher current density in an electrolyzer test cell at a total cell voltage of 2 V, highlighting improved catalyst utilization. Structural and electrochemical controls show that the high activity arises from interfacially localized SnO 2 rather than bulk SnO 2 incorporation or altered proton conductivity. The embedded route improves precursor efficiency, increases membrane junction adhesion force by 7×, and maintains stable operation under continuous elec-trolyzer testing. A preliminary pseudo-PEM water-electrolysis demonstration further shows that the embedded SnO 2 interface remains beneficial in an AEI–PEM heterojunction architecture coupled to a PGM-free Co 3 O 4 anode. These results establish precursor-based interfacial self-reconstruction as a practical route to thin, active, and mechanically integrated catalyst–membrane junctions. Keywords: Bipolar membranes; Water dissociation; Tin oxide (SnO 2 ); Ionomer interfaces; Water electrolysis
items.authors: Yifan Wu, Benjamin N. Indeglia, Vivek S. Devalla, Wenbo Zhang, Helen K. Chen, Peiyao Wu

items.title: Designing Ideal Denoisers for Chromatographic and Spectroscopic Signals
items.abstract: Modern instrumental analyses have different types of noise superimposed on the true signal, from low frequencies (baselines and colored noise) to very high-frequency components like sharp spikes. Convolution based denoisers or frequency domain filters inadequately handle colored noise and induce baseline oscillations while broadening narrow peaks. Herein, two new dataadaptive denoising methods are developed for chromatographic and spectroscopic data. The goal is to suppress noise without appreciably distorting peak shape or quantitative information (area, location, and variance). The proposed methods are posed as optimization problems inspired by the Bohlmann-Whittaker smoother. The objective function consists of a data fidelity term and adaptive second difference and bi-scale log-cosh penalties. The latter term suppresses pink or colored noise effectively, while adaptive functions protect narrow and weak peaks. The second method is designed for intensity-dependent additive and proportional noise and combines an inverse hyperbolic sine variance-stabilizing transformation with adaptive second-difference regularization. Non-uniform sampling rates are tolerated by this second smoother. In simulated chromatograms containing white and pink noise, the proposed adaptive method reduced the reconstruction error by approximately 40-50% relative to Gaussian weighted moving average and penalized least squares smoothing. The resolution of closely spaced peaks was maintained, and a weak peak with a weak peak with a signal-to-noise ratio near 5 was recovered. The proposed denoisers were evaluated on real data from GC-IMS, LC-MS/MS, Raman spectra relevant to planetary studies, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy of graphitic surface, and overloaded LC-MS instruments as test cases with and without baseline correction. Most denoiser parameters are derived from noise estimated from a single chromatogram or spectrum; no training or learning algorithms are required. The denoisers are fast and can be extended to 2D data.
items.authors: M. Farooq Wahab

items.title: Interpretable QSPR Modeling of Surfactant Characteristic Curvature
items.abstract: Characteristic curvature (Cc) quantifies the intrinsic interfacial curvature tendency of surfactants under defined reference conditions and is a key input to the hydrophilic–lipophilic deviation (HLD) framework for predicting microemulsion phase behavior; however, experimental determination remains laborious, and interpretable molecular structure–Cc relationships across diverse surfactant chemistries are comparatively underdeveloped. Here, we developed a quantitative structure–property relationship (QSPR) framework using a curated literature-derived dataset of 63 anionic and nonionic surfactants, with molecular structures verified against the original sources and experimental values curated to improve consistency of the Cc endpoint, and benchmarked multiple tree-based regression algorithms using two-dimensional RDKit descriptors, fold-contained preprocessing, Yeo–Johnson target transformation, SHAP-based feature selection, and nested cross-validation. XGBoost achieved the strongest performance on 13-surfactants test set, with R 2 = 0.85, RMSE = 0.53, and MAE = 0.44 Cc units, with all metrics calculated on the inverse-transformed scale; the observed error was of the same order of magnitude as reported experimental uncertainty, supporting preliminary prediction within the represented chemical domain rather than replacing experimental Cc determination. SHAP and partial-dependence analyses identified electrotopological, topological, hydrophobicity-related, and other physicochemical descriptors associated with the model response, revealing nonlinear and threshold-like patterns that support chemically interpretable structure–property hypotheses without establishing causal mechanisms or experimentally validated design rules; the framework therefore offers a reproducible basis for prioritizing structurally related surfactants for subsequent experimental evaluation and provides a methodological reference for future Cc modeling with broader chemical coverage and prospective validation.
items.authors: Affan Dulyadech, Uthaiporn Suriyapraphadilok, Ampira Charoensaeng, Natthapong Sueviriyapan

items.title: Polyethyleneimine (PEI) molecular weight alters the photophysical and FRET properties of water dispersible NaYF4:Yb,Er upconversion nanoparticles
items.abstract: Upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) are optically active materials with near-infrared excitation and tuneable anti-Stokes emission, typically resulting in visible emission. A route to routine and reliable synthesis of water-dispersible UCNPs for biomedical imaging applications is the polyethyleneimine (PEI)- assisted solvothermal autoclave synthesis; however, the properties of the resulting UCNPs remain understudied. Herein, we report how PEI molecular weight alters properties of core-only, red-emitting, water-dispersible PEI-UCNPs. In terms of brightness, 1.2 kDa PEI-UCNPs exhibited 5 times more intense upconversion luminescence (UCL) than 25 kDa PEI-UCNPs and a 29% longer UCL lifetime (LT) for the red emission band (~640-690 nm, 4 F 9/2 → 4 I 15/2 Er 3+ transition) in DI H 2 O. Dispersal in D 2 O increased emission across wavebands, with green emission ( 2 H 11/2 , 4 S 3/2 → 4 I 15/2 Er 3+ transition) increasing by 248 - 365% whereas red emission only increased between 38-64%. From our results, we infer that PEI may quench the UCL via high-energy NH vibrations. We also examined Förster Resonance Energy Transfer (FRET) between PEI-UCNPs and an electrostatically adsorbed fluorescent model dye, AlexaFluor647® (AF647). 25 kDa PEI-UCNPs achieved highest LT-estimated FRET efficiencies of ~11% in H 2 O and 16% in D 2 O, respectively. These findings highlight that polymer MW should be considered when optimising UCNP synthesis.
items.authors: Rebecca McGonigle, Christian Homann, Ciera Connelly, Marta Gajewska, Niko Hildebrandt, Robert Pal

items.title: Asymmetric Electrical Double Layer Charging in Ionomers under Pure Water
items.abstract: Electrode interfaces with ionic polymers (ionomers) create local microenvironments in membrane electrolysis and other applications, yet the formation and dynamics of electrical double layers (EDLs) at ionomer|electrode interfaces are incompletely understood. Unlike traditional aqueous electrolytes with both mobile cations and anions, ionomer interfaces couple mobile counterion motion to the slower response of tethered polymer-backbone ionic groups. Studying these solid|ionomer interfaces, with pure water feed as in many technology applications, is more difficult than with conventional electrolytes due to the lack of a liquid supporting electrolyte for simple integration of counter and reference electrodes. Here, we use a membrane-electrode-assembly-inspired architecture with a lateral ionomer strip and a salt-bridged reference electrode to independently track anodic and cathodic potentials while sweeping the voltage between the two Pt-solid|ionomer interfaces in pure water. We quantify electrode-resolved non-faradaic charging and show that fixed polymer charges and mobile counterions contribute differently to interfacial capacitance. In anion-exchange ionomers, mobile Cl- responds rapidly, whereas fixed quaternary ammonium groups relax more slowly, producing a capacitance asymmetry. This asymmetry weakens when sufficient time is allowed for relaxation and is suppressed by supporting electrolyte. When Nafion cation-exchange ionomer is used instead, the results show a reversal in the sign of the asymmetry. Supporting molecular dynamics simulations establish coupled counterion motion and tethered-charge relaxation as governing features of pure-water ionomer EDLs. The work thus provides a framework for studying and ultimately designing ionomer microenvironments for membrane electrolysis and other applications. The Bigger Picture Pure-water-fed membrane electrolyzers rely on ionomers to carry charge to catalyst surfaces. Unlike soluble liquid electrolytes, ionomers contain mobile counterions and oppositely charged groups fixed to a polymer chain. The details of how these charges form electrical double layers under positive and negative polarization are not fully understood. We developed a model cell with a solid ionomer electrolyte that senses each electrode potential separately during cell operation. The measurements show asymmetric, time-dependent charging in pure water, with mobile counterions responding more rapidly than polymer-bound charge. Added electrolytes suppress this charging-rate imbalance; reversing the ionomer charge sign also reverses the asymmetry of the charging response, and a custom-synthesized more-flexible polymer backbone reduces the rate dependence of the apparent capacitance. The work here shows how the ionomer is an active part of the electrochemical interface, in addition to an ion conductor in the bulk. The platform and fundamental principles developed here are relevant to water electrolyzers, fuel cells, and other membrane-based electrochemical devices.
items.authors: Yunseok Kang, Fabrice Roncoroni, Andrew D. Pendergast, Wenbo Zhang, Mei-Chen Kuo, Ahmet Kusoglu

items.title: PtSe2/Graphene Interfacial Coupling Enhances the Intrinsic Electrocatalytic Activity of PtSe2 Edge Sites
items.abstract: Platinum-based chalcogenides (PtX2) can be efficiently activated as electrocatalysts for water splitting through the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Edges in layered PtSe2 are effective in HER; however, the effect of edge interaction with conductive electrodes like graphene remains unclear. This study investigates the mechanism by which PtX2 (X = S, Se, Te) edges interact with graphene to uncover the origin of chalcogen-dependent differences in electrocatalysis through interfacial electronic coupling. Graphene flakes decorated with PtX2 nanosheets have reduced overpotential and enhanced kinetics in the HER. Interestingly, PtSe2/graphene exhibits the lowest overpotential among all samples, even though it also has the lowest electrochemically accessible surface area. First-principles calculations confirm the interfacial coupling between PtSe2 edges and graphene with pronounced charge accumulation in platinum-selenium edges. Gibbs free energy calculations show different activities for different chalcogens of PtX2/graphene, consistent with experimental results. Our findings indicate that graphene acts as an electronic regulator for PtSe2/graphene, which enhances the intrinsic catalytic activity of the platinum-selenium edge sites, making them more effective for the HER despite their lower density. This interfacial electronic coupling through conductive electrodes provides a powerful strategy for the rational design of next-generation electrocatalysts, enabling enhanced activity and selectivity in advanced electrochemical systems.
items.authors: Ilias M. Oikonomou, Axel Zuber, Apostolos Koutsioukis, Iva Plutnarová, Zdenek Sofer, Michelle P. Browne

items.title: Helium Compression Chamber: an ab initio molecular dynamics approach to chemical reactions under pressure
items.abstract: Understanding how pressure affects chemical reactivity requires methods capable of describing both the structural response of molecules and the thermodynamics of reactions under compression. We present the Helium Compression Chamber (HeCC), a computational approach in which molecules are compressed within an explicit helium environment and their reaction free energy profiles are determined from finite-temperature molecular dynamics simulations. An on-the-fly machine-learning force field is employed to make extensive sampling feasible while retaining ab initio accuracy for the underlying potential-energy evaluations. The pressure response of four representative reactions is investigated, including bond cleavage, electrocyclization, cycloaddition, and hydrogen transfer. The calculated free-energy profiles show that compression systematically favors reactions associated with a decrease in molecular volume, while the opposite trend is observed for cyclobutene ring opening. In particular, the Diels–Alder reaction becomes barrierless at sufficiently high pressure, whereas the barriers for hexatriene cyclization and the 1,5-hydrogen shift decrease progressively with compression. The structural changes along the reaction coordinates and the pressure dependence of the corresponding activation and reaction volumes are compared with predictions from the extreme pressure-polarizable continuum model (XP-PCM) method. The comparison illustrates both the consistency and the differences between explicit-and continuum-pressure descriptions. HeCC therefore offers a route toward finite-temperature simulations of chemical reactions under pressure and provides a foundation for extending such calculations to more realistic solvation environments.
items.authors: Jorge Laranjeira, Roberto Cammi, Maximilian Amsler, Bo Chen

items.title: Novel Quinoxaline-Based Cyanocarbonimidodithioate Derivatives as Non-Hydroxamate Selective HDAC8 Inhibitors: Design, Synthesis, Biological Evaluation and Mechanistic Studies
items.abstract: Histone deacetylase 8 (HDAC8) has emerged as a promising anticancer target; however, most clinically approved hydroxamate-based HDAC inhibitors possess several limitations. A novel series of quinoxaline-based HDAC inhibitors containing a sulfur-based cyanocarbonimidodithioate non-hydroxamate zinc-binding group was designed and synthesized to overcome the selectivity and toxicity limitations of conventional hydroxamate HDAC inhibitors. A total of twenty-three quinoxaline-cyanocarbonimidodithioate derivatives (QZ 1-23) were synthesized and evaluated for HDAC8 inhibitory activity. The compounds demonstrated preferential inhibition of HDAC8 over HDAC4. Among the series, QZ-11 (IC50 = 0.3 μM) and QZ-4 (IC50 = 0.57 μM) emerged as the most promising inhibitors exhibiting favourable selectivity profiles against other tested HDAC isoforms. Both compounds demonstrated moderate to good antiproliferative activity against the IMR-32, SH-SY5Y, and FaDu cell lines. Biological studies revealed that QZ-4 and QZ-11 significantly suppressed colony formation, induced apoptosis, activated caspase-3/7, and induced G2/M phase cell-cycle arrest in IMR-32 cells, and increased acetylation of the HDAC8 substrate SMC3 without altering total SMC3 expression. Molecular docking studies suggested key interactions with HDAC8 selectivity-determining residues His142, Tyr306, and Phe152, while molecular dynamics simulations revealed stable occupancy of the catalytic pocket and persistent Zn-associated interactions throughout 100 ns trajectories. Collectively, these findings identify quinoxaline-cyanocarbonimidodithioates as a promising class of non-hydroxamate HDAC8- inhibitors and support further optimization of sulfur-based zinc-binding pharmacophores for the development of next-generation epigenetic anticancer agents.
items.authors: Kosana Sai Chaitanya, Dharani Sen, Markus Schweipert, Srinuvasu Nakka, Muzaffar-Ur-Rehman Mohammed, Katja Ohlemüller

items.title: An Algorithm for computing Three- and Four-Body Density Matrices from CASCI Wavefunction and AI-Assisted Code Optimization
items.abstract: Three- and four-body reduced density matrices in the active space are required for second-order n-electron valence perturbation theory (NEVPT2) following complete active-space configuration interaction (CASCI) calculations. We developed an algorithm to generate these computationally demanding quantities by extending the pi-CASCI program, which is based on the graphical symmetric group approach (GSGA). A manually written prototype was subsequently optimized through AI-assisted code optimization, resulting in substantially improved performance.
items.authors: Kiyoshi Tanaka, Takahiro Katagiri, Tatsuya Nakano, Yuji Mochizuki

items.title: Spatially-Resolved Viscoelastic Response with AFM-IR
items.abstract: The viscoelastic response of phase-separated polymers systems may deviate from bulk values at the nanoscale. However, current measurement techniques lack the resolution to unmask local variations. We previously demonstrated the advantages of using a focused, pulsed infrared (IR) laser to photothermally heat a sample locally during nanomechanical measurements with an atomic force microscope (AFM), with heating controlled by varying the laser repetition rate. Herein, we demonstrate this IR heating coupled with nano-Dynamic Mechanical Analysis (nDMA). First, we measured the storage and loss modulus of a homogenous copolymer at varying IR repetition rates (i.e., at varying sample temperature), demonstrating a viscoelastic modulus response that is typical near the glass transition temperature. Further, we varied the IR laser repetition rate while modulating the AFM probe between 5 Hz and 100 Hz. With time-temperature superposition, modulus master curves were constructed through the Williams-Landel-Ferry relation, and the shift factors of IR heating-coupled nDMA curves were used to estimate the relation between IR repetition rate and surface temperatures. Lastly, this technique was applied to a phase-separated polymer blend to demonstrate the utility of the technique to decouple the viscoelastic behavior of different phases by leveraging the high spatial resolution of AFM.
items.authors: Carina Yi Jing Lim, Jeffrey J. Schwartz, Bede Pittenger, Yuran Shi, Yoko Tomo, Peter De Wolf

items.title: Symmetry Numbers: A Flexible Approach for Molecules and Transition States
items.abstract: Symmetry numbers are essential corrections in thermochemistry and chemical kinetics, but their reliable assignment remains difficult in automated workflows, especially for stereochemical, fluxional, cyclic, and transition-state structures. We present a stereochemistry-aware automorphism (SAA) approach for computing symmetry numbers using the StereoMolGraph (SMG) framework. In this representation, local stereodescriptors encode rigid local geometries directly in the molecular graph, so the symmetry number is obtained as the order of the automorphism group that preserves both connectivity and encoded stereochemistry. This avoids the need for a post hoc “label stereocenter” correction and provides a direct graph-theoretical analogue of permutation-based symmetry number definitions. Model dependence is handled explicitly by choosing which molecular features are treated as fixed or fluxional, enabling consistent treatment of rigidity, free rotation, umbrella inversion, and pseudorotation assumptions. Beyond overall molecular and transition-state symmetry numbers, the same framework yields external and internal symmetry numbers for hindered-rotor treatments, including an effective external symmetry number for cases where the overall symmetry number is non-separable. Benchmark calculations reproduce the expected symmetry numbers for all supported benchmark molecules and resolve cases where existing rule-based or corrected-connectivity approaches fail, including stereochemically distinct structures with identical connectivity. The SAA approach is highly robust, making it suitable for automated thermochemical and kinetic modeling of molecules and reactions.
items.authors: Maxim Papusha, Andreas V. Copan, Brandon Rotavera, Kai Leonhard

items.title: The Critical Role of Water in Safe, Scalable Diboron-Mediated Nitro Reductions .
items.abstract: The use of diboron compounds for nitro group reduction, an essential transformation in the synthesis of a wide range of nitrogen-containing functional groups, offers an attractive alternative to traditional methods like hydrogenation and dissolving metal reduction. This method has seen limited uptake in the literature despite avoiding transition metals and specialized equipment. Using a combination of reaction calorimetry and kinetic analysis, careful selection of the reaction solvent, diboron source, and inclusion of water enabled the identification of safe and simple conditions for reduction of nitro groups. The scope of the reaction is broad under mild conditions where water plays a critical role in driving reactivity while maintaining wide safety margins.
items.authors: Yilin Cao, Matthew Joannou, Michael Mandler, Sergey Melnikov, Iulia Teleuca, Shasha Zhang

items.title: Dynamic Reactant Forcing Circumvents CO Poisoning in Catalytic CO Oxidation
items.abstract: Heterogeneous catalysts are usually optimized under static feed conditions, forcing a compromise between reactant adsorption, surface reaction, and site regeneration. For CO oxidation on Pt, this compromise is especially severe because CO binds strongly and suppresses O2 activation. Here we show that externally imposed square-wave modulation of the CO pressure can break this static limitation on Pt(111). Using synchronized infrared reflection absorption spectroscopy and mass spectrometry under constant O2 background, we directly resolve the coupled evolution of CO∗ coverage and CO2 production during each forcing cycle. CO introduction produces an initial CO2 burst followed by CO poisoning, whereas CO removal generates a second CO2 burst as vacant sites reopen O2 dissociation pathways. A Langmuir–Hinshelwood microkinetic model reproduces these transients and identifies the optimum forcing window as a balance between CO replenishment, CO desorption, and O2 activation on regenerated sites. Model-guided experimentation indicates the most favorable regimes of forcing frequency and duty cycle. At 475 K and PO2 = 5 × 10−5 mbar, the strongest tested protocol (approximately 0.3 s CO-on and 0.7 s CO-off) gives an approximately threefold larger time-averaged normalized m/z = 44 signal than continuous CO exposure at the same temperature, O2 pressure, and peak CO pressure. These results provide direct experimental evidence that reactant forcing can access productive non-steady-state surface coverages unavailable under static operation, establishing a mechanistic framework for programmable catalytic rate enhancement.
items.authors: Esteban L. Fornero, Eliseo Perez Gomez, Gengnan Li, Zubin Darbari, Cailey Bobadilla, Jerzy Sadowski

items.title: Rate-independent limits on a sulphating, self-renewing oxide catalyst: exact master-equation results with lattice kinetic Monte Carlo checks
items.abstract: Copper oxide takes up sulphur dioxide as a sorbent because sulphation converts it to inactive copper sulphate. Whether a copper oxide surface that sulphates in service and renews itself by exposing fresh copper can instead act as a catalyst for SO 2 oxidation is a question about site statistics as much as chemistry. We study it with a lattice model whose elementary rates are unknown, and we therefore restrict the main claims to statements that hold for every strictly positive assignment of rate constants. Three such results are established. First, under a dual-site mechanism in which O 2 adsorbs dissociatively onto a vacant nearest-neighbour pair and SO 2 onto a single site, an isolated patch of one or two active sites has a stationary product rate of exactly zero, and every connected patch of three or more sites has a strictly positive rate. This is proved and checked exhaustively on all 996 connected graphs of up to seven sites. Second, on a randomly deactivated lattice the share of surviving sites that can never turn over follows the closed form 𝐷 (𝑝) = (1 − 𝑝) 𝑧 + 𝑧𝑝(1 − 𝑝) 𝑡2 , which is 86.9% on a square lattice at 90% deactivation. Combined with exact stationary rates of every component shape, the classical cluster expansion gives the rate of a randomly deactivated surface without sampling. It shows that an earlier kinetic Monte Carlo run reporting a dead surface was a fluctuation in too short a window, on a surface that was never dead. Third, when sulphated sites are recovered only by discarding the oxide layer, the product obtained per copper atom consumed is exactly (𝑘 𝑑 /𝑘 𝑠 ) 𝑓 sulphate , bounded by the branching ratio between product release and sulphation. This quantity is the inverse cumulative site-loss selectivity of Foley, Johnson and Bhan, and a chemical regeneration channel is the only route past the bound. All stationary solutions use the Grassmann, Taksar and Heyman reduction, which we show is required. A least-squares solve used earlier was wrong by up to twelve orders of magnitude on small rates.
items.authors: Pragyaan Gaur

items.title: Extracting Latent Sequence-Function Information from Directed Evolution to Design Improved C-H Azidases
items.abstract: Directed evolution is a powerful approach for enzyme engineering, but conventional workflows use only a fraction of the information generated during experimental screening. Typically, only top-performing variants are sequenced and propagated, while sequence-function information from the remainder of the library is discarded. Here, we develop a data-efficient strategy to recover and leverage this latent information for enzyme design. Screened variants are grouped into activity-defined bins, pooled, and subjected to long-read sequencing, enabling efficient acquisition of sequence-function relationships while preserving relative activity information. Ordinal machine learning models trained on these binned data are then used to predict beneficial mutations. We applied this strategy to SadX, an engineered Fe(II)- and α-ketoglutarate-dependent azidase previously evolved for site-selective C-H azidation. Using only data from a previous directed evolution campaign, the models identified mutations that significantly improved catalytic performance. Experimental validation showed that several predicted single mutations enhanced azidation activity by up to 3-fold relative to the parent enzyme. These results demonstrate that substantial gains in enzyme activity can be achieved by extracting additional information from existing directed evolution datasets, providing a general strategy for converting routinely generated screening data into actionable sequence-function information for enzyme design.
items.authors: Ayantika Ghosh, Sameer D'Costa, Christian A. Gomez, Bryce Johnson, Prajwal Prabhu, Anthony Gitter

items.title: Distinguishing Pharmaceutical Salts and Cocrystals by Fluorescence Lifetime Mapping and Quantum Crystallography
items.abstract: Distinguishing between salt and cocrystal forms of a drug remains challenging in multicomponent systems with ambiguous proton transfer, particularly during bulk production in the pharmaceutical industry. Here, we address this challenge by combining fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) for rapid bulk-phase discrimination with Hirshfeld atom refinement (HAR) for single-crystal-level validation. This integrated FLIM–HAR approach was applied to 11 multicomponent solids derived from the pharmaceutical drugs niflumic acid, mefenamic acid, and sulfamethazine. Owing to its sensitivity to the local electronic environment and crystal-field effects, FLIM provided spatially resolved lifetime signatures that clearly distinguished salts from cocrystals, with salts consistently exhibiting longer fluorescence lifetimes. HAR unambiguously located the transferred protons, as evidenced by difference Fourier maps, thereby validating the salt–cocrystal assignments. Analysis of intermolecular interactions using the HAR models further revealed stronger interactions and tighter crystal packing in the salts, primarily arising from charge-assisted hydrogen bonding, consistent with the observed lifetime differences. The correlation between fluorescence lifetime and HAR-determined protonation state demonstrates that lifetime provides a sensitive probe of proton transfer in pharmaceutical solids. The integrated FLIM–HAR methodology therefore provides a rapid and reliable strategy for distinguishing pharmaceutical salts and cocrystals, with particular potential for bulk-phase characterization.
items.authors: Amit Kumar, Aditya Kumar Prajapati, Sofia Arefeen Khan, Monika Gupta, Sajesh P. Thomas

items.title: Mapping under-represented chalcone chemical space with an open-source Virtual Chalcone Library (VCL)
items.abstract: Chalcones are highly versatile privileged scaffolds, yet substantial regions of their synthetically accessible chemical space remain under-explored. Herein, we report an open-source Virtual Chalcone Library (VCL) comprising 489,475 unique structures generated from commercially available aromatic ketones and aldehydes using the freely available DataWarrior platform. Comparison of the VCL with a curated dataset of 8,886 literature chalcones revealed structural bias towards a small number of pharmacophore motifs, while highlighting under-represented regions of chemical space. Benzofuran-containing chalcones emerged as a prominent example and were selected as a case study for prospective exploration. Physicochemical filtering for favourable medicinal chemistry properties reduced this region to 1,181 candidates, from which diversity analysis identified 30 representative structures. Six novel chalcones were selected and successfully prepared, establishing two “synthetic outposts” in under-represented chemical space. A series of “deep-space” virtual chalcones (DS1-DS9) were identified with DS6 synthesised from commercially available starting materials. These syntheses provide experimental validation of the data-driven, VCL-guided workflow. The VCL is openly available as a community resource, accompanied by tutorials for its implementation and analysis in DataWarrior. This study establishes a framework for identifying, prioritising and experimentally accessing under-represented regions of chalcone chemical space.
items.authors: Alexander Ciupa

items.title: Persistent Alkyne-Bridged Bis-Trityl Diradicaloids with an Open-Shell Ground State
items.abstract: Organic singlet diradicaloids are of interest for spintronics, singlet fission, and quantum information science because of their electronic and magnetic properties.
